decides) or a `shared` cause (its problem holds the job): they say nothing of the item's work. It comes after the rules,
the two cases above, and a hopper bug the job reported (issue #1147).

**hopper's own client errors** match known causes: `client <machine> is not dialled in` is `machine offline` (a
problem, redirected or held, resolved by its online check); `no answer: its link closed` and `no answer within <n>
ms, or its link closed` are `link closed`, transient — a link that drops for good fails the next run with `is not
dialled in`. `test/failures/client-link.test.ts` checks every `ClientError` template in `src/executors/client.ts`,
so a reworded or new one fails there instead of falling through to a person.

**Hold or redirect.** A problem planned `redirect` (socket path, disk full, machine offline) redirects a failed
job that may run elsewhere — not pinned, its machine known, the problem on one machine, automatic redirect on:
it runs again at once, and the decider keeps it off that machine. Any other is held: it waits on the problem's
release. While a problem is open the decider (`DecisionInputs.problems`, `problemHold` and `eligible` in
`assign.ts`) keeps every new job it covers off its machine, and holds one with no other machine — pinned there,
or no other online machine runs its executor — with the reason `held by problem: <title>`. A resuming job returns
to its pane. With automatic hold off, problems are still grouped and shown, but hold no job. A **general** (Recurring)
problem holds only the jobs grouped in it, never every job of its scope (issue #637): with no known cause, nothing says
another job would meet it — problem `ba0f00fc` held every queued job of one machine for ten hours over done-check misses.

**A done-check miss** (issue #637, the `not-complete` cause) is looked at once more before it is assessed
(`lookedAgain`, `done-at-source.ts`, at most `PR_LOOKUP_MS`): its job said it was done, and its source said not done twice,
a minute apart; GitHub may still show the work late. So is every other failed job (issue #2040): a job can end failed
after it delivered, on a check its machine could not make (`HOPPER_FAILED` because `HOPPER_GH` was empty), and its
source's answer, not its own words, says whether its work is done. Done now: its record is written `resolved` (the note says done at its
source), no hand-off opens, and its job ends finished, its source told again. Not done, or not known: assessed as before
(a `job` cause: a person), and then it is a decider call like a failure no known cause explains — Jev picks run it again
or a person, in the words of a done-check miss. Whether it is done stays GitHub's to say, never Jev's, so Jev is not
offered `done` or PR waiting: those come only from the source's own answer, here and before every run again.

**Running again** is the sync loop's Run again (issues #313, #354), `by: "assessor"` on `job.rerun`: the item is
given back by its source and a new job queued, `rerunOf` the failed one. Each run again the assessor decides is
**pending** on the failure record (`pending`, `pendingAt`) until made, so a retry due later, a redirect or a
release outlives a restart; the sweep (every tick) makes the due ones. A refusal that may pass — the end not yet
reported to its source, the source not running, the source down — is tried again later; any other ends it
`not_retried`, its reason kept. **Finished work is never run again** (issue #637): before each run again — a retry, a
redirect, a release, a person's Retry — the source is asked whether the job's work is done there
(`FailuresOptions.doneAtSource`, the source's `notComplete`: its issue closed as completed, a pull request that closes
it ready or merged). Done: the job ends finished (`finishShipped`, its source told again: `hopper:done` or
`hopper:pr-ready`, its pull request followed), the record `resolved` with the note `done at its source: …`, and nothing
runs again — Run again would reopen the closed issue (`takeBack`). A person's Retry is then refused, saying so. A source
that cannot tell postpones the assessor's run again 30 s; it does not hold a person's Retry, which runs (issue #855: an
answer the source can never give left the job stuck). The attempt count is the chain of earlier jobs of the item a retry ran again.

**Release.** Resolving a problem (a person; or its **check**: a `machine offline` or `disk full` problem whose
check saw the cause on its machine — offline, disk low — and then sees it gone) sets its held jobs to run again,
and new jobs are no longer held for it. Release held does the first without resolving.

**Events** (`docs/events.md`): `job.assessed` (once per failed job: decision, class, reasons, summary, attempt,
`auto`), `failure.grouped` (a job joined or opened a problem), `failure.resolved` (by `user` or `check`, how many
held jobs released). Webhooks and notifiers take them as any event.

**Profile** (`profile.ts`): per signature counts and a daily trend over 14 days, its jobs and machines, flagged
recurring on `groupThreshold` jobs; breakdowns by machine, repo and executor.

**Settings** (`failureSettings`, a user setting in the database; Failures view, admin): `maxAttempts`, the
backoff, the grouping threshold and window, `activeWindowMin` (issue #630), `auto.retry` / `auto.hold` / `auto.redirect`
/ `auto.continue` (default on: off, the decision is recorded and waits for a person; one saved before it existed takes
its default), `retentionDays` (default 90: records and resolved problems older
are deleted, a pending one never). Read at each assessment and sweep: no restart. Named causes: `failureCauses`.

**Failures view** (its own nav entry, after Logins; the badge counts open problems and open hand-offs, "Needs a person"): first
what is left (issues #517, #1067) — the work items the work-item ledger has as `failed`, and those handed to a person on
their failure (`needs_you`, waiting on a hand-off), `counts` in `GET /api/failures` (`failed`, `needsPerson`), both
zero once nothing is left; the same counts every other view reads; open problems with their
jobs, the held ones, Resolve and Release held; the recent assessed failures with their decision, summary and
Retry; the profile and the known causes (an admin names a signature, or forgets one); the settings. `GET
/api/failures` gives each problem and failure its `actions`, `{ ok }` or `{ ok: false, why }`, and the routes
refuse with the same reasons: the view offers only what is taken, and the role (operator for the actions, admin
for settings and causes) is checked by the UI session guard as for every mutation. A failed job's assessment shows
under its error in the Queue and the Dashboard.

Open decisions taken conservatively, each one entry to change: no model judges a failure (rules only; an unclear
one goes to a person); every automatic action on by default, each switchable; retries move to another machine
only through a problem's redirect; the profile is its own view; the assessor never opens or drafts a GitHub issue.

## The failure assessor under crashes, poison failures and retry storms (issue #1961, 2026-10-18)

**Why.** The assessor (#509) and Needs a person (#516) had tests for the usual path and a clean restart only. Not tested:
a hopper killed during an assessment, a failure whose own data makes the assessment throw, many jobs that fail at once,
and two hosts on one database.

**Kill points** (`src/sagas/kill-points.ts`, "The crash harness"). The assessment passes two:
`failures:assess:before-commit`, in its transaction after the record, the assessment, the events, the problem and the
hand-off are written and before it commits, and `failures:assess:after-commit`, just after the commit. A kill at the first
leaves nothing of that assessment (Postgres rolls the transaction back); at the second, all of it.

**A poison failure** (`src/failures/poison.ts`). A failure whose assessment throws — for example a job spec with no
payload, as an older build or a broken plugin can leave — is handed to a person in one transaction: a record with the
decision "a person", the class "job", the reason `the hopper could not assess this failure: <the error>` and that summary,
the assessment on the job, `job.assessed`, and its hand-off. It is never assessed again. If that throws too, the hopper says
so once and leaves the job; it never blocks the assessment of the other failures. A store that fails is not poison: a
`StoreError` (`src/domain/store-error.ts`, every call `src/store/db.ts` could not make — a lock wait past its time, a
dropped connection) is said, and the job stays unassessed, not left, so the next sweep assesses it.

**What it found.**
- **A poison failure stopped every assessment after it.** The throw ended the sweep's backlog pass at that job, on each
  sweep. Now the poison failure is handed to a person, and the pass goes on.
- **A host that did not hold the failure sweep's lease never swept again.** The sweep under way was cleared in the pass's
  `finally`. A pass that ended before its first `await` — the lease held by another host, or a throw — ran that `finally`
  before the pass was assigned as the sweep under way. The resolved pass then stood as the sweep under way for good: the
  host never asked the lease again, so when the host that held it was killed, no host assessed the failures it left. The
  sweep under way is now cleared after the pass ends (`.finally` on the pass).
- **A store failure was taken for a poison failure.** On a loaded CI runner, host B's assessment of the job A was killed
  in waited on A's lock past its time. The poison handler took that error as the job's own, its hand-off failed the same
  way, and B left the job for good. Now a `StoreError` is never poison: the next sweep assesses the job.

**What the tests show.**
- `test/crash/assess-kill.test.ts`: hosts A (armed) and B on one database, A holding the failure sweep's lease. Failed jobs
  are written into the database, failed two minutes ago, as a restart leaves them. A is killed at its third assessment, at
  each kill point. B takes the sweep and assesses each failure once: one record, one decision, one `job.assessed`, one open
  hand-off for each job-specific failure, and a pending retry for the transient one. B is killed too and a host C starts:
  each hand-off is still open, and nothing is assessed again.
- `test/integration/failures-poison.test.ts`: a poison failure between four other failures. Each is assessed; the poison
  one is handed to a person with the reason, once.
- `test/integration/failures-storm.test.ts`: 110 jobs fail in one sync, 60 with a reset connection and 50 with a full disk,
  with a retry limit of 2 and a backoff of 1 s. Each failed job is assessed once. Each signature is one problem, opened
  once, that its jobs join ("Disk full on local", and "Recurring: read ECONNRESET" once three failed). Each run again by the
  assessor comes at or after its retry time, and no item runs more than the retry limit allows. Each failure writes at
  most one grouping and one hand-off, and each job's end is reported to its source at most once (the manual source stands
  for GitHub's labels). Each failure for a person has one open hand-off.

**Decisions.**
- **The failed jobs of the crash test are written into the database, not run.** A host's manual source is in its own
  process, so a host that is killed takes the items it offered with it. A failed job written two minutes back is what a
  restart leaves, and the sweep's backlog assesses it the same way.
- **The poison test's poison is a spec with no payload.** It is data a store can hold that the assessment cannot read. The
  fix catches any throw of the assessment, so the test does not need a seam to throw.

**Not covered here.** A kill between a run again the assessor makes and its record (the host that goes on needs the item
from a source of its own); a kill while a person resolves a hand-off; a retry storm through the GitHub source.

## A failure the job reported as a hopper bug (issue #1147, 2026-10-14)

**The problem.** A tend job's push was refused by a bug in the shrink guard. The job reported the bug on the hopper with
`hopper-gh report bug`, then failed (`not complete: tending failed: the shrink guard refused its last push, …`). The
assessor found no cause for it but the job's own, so it went to Needs a person. Nothing a person could do there helped:
the job's work was right, and the hopper was wrong. Owner request: such a failure does not land in Needs a person; the
assessor runs it again once the fix landed.

**The rule** (`src/failures/hopper-bug.ts`, `assess.ts`, pure). A failure the rules hand to a person (step 5, a done-check
miss, a retry limit) of a job that filed a **bug report** about itself while it ran — its row in Your reports, `fromJob`,
`jobId` the job — is held on that report instead, while automatic hold is on: decision `hold`, class `shared`, first
reason `it reported a hopper bug (#N): it waits for the fix, then runs again`. It joins the open **hopper bug problem** of
the report's issue, or opens one: `Hopper bug #N` (a report kept to send later: its own, by its id), cause `hopper-bug`,
scope every machine, planned `hold`. A held record opens no hand-off, so the job is not in Needs a person, and Jev is not
asked. A superseded, stale or done-at-source failure is as before.

**It holds only its own jobs.** Like a Recurring problem (issue #637), it is not in `blocks()`: only the jobs that
reported the bug are known to meet it, and a bug in one route must not hold every job of every machine.

**The fix landed.** Each sweep, the problem's check reads its reports as Report a bug last read them (every 10 minutes,
`later.ts`, which now keeps `closedAt` and `closedAs`, GitHub's `closed_at` and `state_reason`). The check resolves it
(`failure.resolved`, `by: check`) once a report of its issue is closed as completed and this hopper's build was made
after that close (`installedAt` of its install record, from the updater). Only then does the build have the fix: a merge
into the landing branch closes the issue, and the build moves to it later, through its update channel. With no install
record (a run from a checkout) the close alone is enough. Resolved, its held jobs run again through the normal release
(`pending: release`, `by: assessor`), after the done-at-source check. An issue closed any other way (`not_planned`,
`duplicate`) does not resolve it: it stays open in the Failures view, where a person resolves or releases it.

**Not taken.** The closing pull request's merge commit against the installed commit: exact, but it needs the issue's
timeline and a git history of the hopper, for a decision the build's time makes well enough. A retry that still meets the
bug fails again and is assessed again; it waits on a fix again only if it reports again.

## A timed-out job (issue #630, 2026-10-10)

A job that ran out of its time (`timeoutMs`, error `timed out`) got no known cause and went to a person, though the
facts that decide it were at hand: was it still at work? Its **liveness** (`JobLiveness` on the job, and in its failure
record's evidence) says:

- `outputAt` — when its pane output last changed. The herdr-claude monitor reports each change of the turn's output
  (`TurnWatch.onOutput`); the executor keeps the last one per job and gives it with the failure.
- `pushed` — the reap at the timeout (`keep`, "Work tree" → "The reap") found a repository in its scratch dir whose
  `HEAD` holds a remote branch the default branch does not. The scratch dir is kept: the job may go on there.
- `pullRequest` — its source says a pull request of its own is open (`JobSource.pullRequestOpen`; GitHub: an open
  pull request closing its issue that it opened, or an older one it pushed to; a draft counts). The assessor asks
  before it assesses (`timeouts.ts`), at most `PR_LOOKUP_MS` (10 s); a lookup that fails or takes longer leaves it
  not known, and the other two decide.

A fact absent is not known. The rules (`timed-out.ts`, pure: liveness and the chain in, decision out):

- **Active** — output changed within `activeWindowMin` minutes (default 10, a failure setting) before the timeout, or
  commits pushed, or a pull request open: **Continue** (decision `continue`, class `transient`, `auto.continue`).
  The sweep makes it at once: its own agent session resumes in its kept work tree when it can (`continueResumes` as for
  a hand-off: an executor that parks, a recorded session, a work tree) — `job.continued` with `recordId` —, else its item
  runs again, `job.rerun` `by: "assessor"`. Either one is told it timed out while at work and to go on from its
  branch or pull request (`timedOutBrief`). The third active timeout in a row of its chain (`MAX_ACTIVE_TIMEOUTS`)
  goes to a person: an agent that keeps producing output is not continued for ever.
- **Silent** — none of them: **Retry** once, after the first backoff. Silent again right after that retry: a person.

The chain (`chain.ts`) is read from the failure records: a continued run is the same job, so its earlier records
count as well as its earlier jobs'. Only timed-out runs the assessor ran again count, newest first, back to the first
that was not one. A person names no cause with `continue`: it needs a timeout's liveness.

## Own PR checks red (issue #1230, 2026-10-15)

A job opened its pull request (`Part of #1194`); one check went red on a timing assertion; the job ended done. The done
check hid the pull request — a part whose checks failed was not counted — and said `no pull request … closes or references
it`. The built-in cause **Not complete** matched, its decision `person`: a hand-off and `hopper:failed` on the first
attempt, though the fix was the hopper's own work, and the queue sat idle for hours.

**The miss says it.** `notComplete` (`src/sources/github/completion.ts`) asks for the job's own open pull request — opened
by it, updated by it, or the one it reworks; closing its issue or shipping part of it; ready but for its checks (not a
draft, no merge conflicts) — and its checks (`ownPullRequestChecks`, the failed ones read by its number). Red, the miss
names it: `not complete: the issue <url> is open, and PR #1226: checks failed: test (node 24)`, never `no pull request`
(`redChecksLine`). A pull request that closes the issue is still listed as found, `#N (open, checks failing)`.

**Its own cause.** The built-in cause **Own PR checks red** (`own-pr-checks-red`, class `transient`, decision
`continue`), matched before **Not complete** by that text (`OWN_PR_CHECKS_RED_TEXT`). The issue asked for decision `retry`;
the act it describes — the same job goes on in its own session — is `continue`, so that is the decision. The rules
(`assess.ts`): never grouped and never joined to a problem; while its chain was sent back for red checks fewer than
`maxAttempts` times (`checksFixesOf`, `chain.ts`: the records of the cause whose Continue was made, across the job and the
jobs a retry ran again before it), **Continue**; then a person, `retry limit reached: sent back N times for red checks`.

**Its Continue** is pending on the record, and each sweep takes one step (`src/failures/checks-red.ts`), before the done
check, from the pull request as the job's source reads it then:

1. Checks running: wait `HOPPER_CHECKS_WAIT_MS` (default 60 s), at most `MAX_CHECKS_WAIT_MS` (60 min) from the assessment.
   The done check does not run meanwhile: checks still running count as ready to it, and would end the job done.
2. Red, and its failed checks not run again for this head commit: the hopper runs each failed check that is a GitHub
   Actions job again (`JobSource.rerunChecks`; GitHub: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job}/rerun`, the port's
   `rerunJob`), once per head commit — the flake guard —, records `job.checks_rerun` (the checks run again, and why any
   were not: no Actions job, no permission), and waits as in 1. It records `job.checks_rerun_asked` before it asks
   (issue #1607): a stop while it asks makes no second run again of that head commit. With only that event, whether any
   check ran again is not known, so the brief lets the job run them again itself.
3. Passing, or no such pull request: the done check decides — done, the record `resolved` and the job finished.
4. Red again, or not run again: the job goes on, its own agent session in its kept work tree when it can (`job.continued`
   with `recordId`), else its item runs again (`job.rerun`, `by: "assessor"`). It is told the **checks-red brief**
   (`checksRedBrief`, `src/domain/pull-requests.ts`): fixed text, the failed checks with their links, what they reported
   and their logs' excerpts (`JobSource.checkLogs`), to fix them on the same branch, open no new pull request, and end
   done; told the hopper ran them again already, or, when it could not, that it may once.

**No `hopper:failed` while the hopper fixes it.** The sync loop reports such a failure only once it is assessed
(`job.assessed` triggers the report). While its Continue is pending, the report says so (`SourceReport.fixing`): the
GitHub source leaves the issue as it is, claimed, no label. When a person gets it — its retries spent, or its Continue
refused, a hand-off opened — the end is told again (`src/sources/fixing-reports.ts`), as failed: `hopper:failed`.

**Permission.** A run again needs the GitHub App's **Actions: write** permission. Without it GitHub refuses (403):
`job.checks_rerun` says so in `refused`, and the job goes on at once, allowed to run the checks again itself, once, with an
empty commit.

**Scope.** Only a job's own pull request whose checks were red when it ended. A PR waiting job's pull request that goes
red later is tended ("Tending a waiting pull request"); a landing batch's red run has its own path (bisect, revert, fix
issue: "Landing batches"). Within a run, the finish brief `fix_checks` still comes first (`MAX_FINISH_BRIEFS`).

## Own PR unfinished (issue #1265, 2026-10-15)

A job opened its pull request; a merge on the base branch left it with merge conflicts; the job ended done. The cause
**Not complete** matched, its decision `person`: a hand-off whose card recommended Continue, "the job can fix the
conflicts". Merge conflicts on the hopper's own pull requests are expected, and the fix is the hopper's own work.

**The miss says it.** `notComplete` (`src/sources/github/completion.ts`) asks for the job's own open pull request that one
fixed step finishes (`unfinishedPullRequest`: opened by the job, updated by it, or the one it reworks). With merge
conflicts or as a draft, the miss names it and its step (`unfinishedLine`): `PR #1260: merge conflicts with its base`, or
`PR #1260: a draft`. A pull request with red checks only is said as in "Own PR checks red".

**Its own cause.** The built-in cause **Own PR unfinished** (`own-pr-unfinished`, class `transient`, decision `continue`),
matched before **Not complete** by that text (`OWN_PR_UNFINISHED_TEXT`). The rules (`assess.ts`) are those of Own PR checks
red: never grouped, never joined to a problem; while its chain was sent back for it fewer than `maxAttempts` times
(`checksFixesOf` of this cause, `chain.ts`), **Continue**; then a person, `retry limit reached: sent back N times to finish
its pull request`. Automatic Continue off (`auto.continue`): it waits for a person, as before. Any other Not complete is
unchanged.

**Its Continue** (`src/failures/unfinished.ts`), after the done check: the job's source names the step now
(`JobSource.unfinishedPullRequest`; it cannot tell: asked again later). The job goes on in its own agent session in its
kept work tree when it can (`job.continued` with `recordId`), else its item runs again (`job.rerun`, `by: "assessor"`),
told the **unfinished brief** (`unfinishedBrief`, `src/domain/pull-requests.ts`): fixed text, the step — rebase onto the
base branch, resolve every conflict keeping the intent of both sides, run the checks and push, or mark it ready —, make
the checks pass, open no new pull request, end done. No `hopper:failed` while it is pending, as for Own PR checks red
(`src/sources/fixing-reports.ts`).

**Scope.** Within a run, the finish briefs still come first (`MAX_FINISH_BRIEFS`); this cause is the job's end after them.
A PR waiting job's pull request that has conflicts later is tended ("Tending a waiting pull request").

**Its work decides, not only its text** (issue #1522, 2026-10-16). A job that pushed to a pull request its issue only
names, which neither closes nor references the issue, failed with the generic Not complete text, and Needs a person
opened for plain merge conflicts. Two changes:

- The job's own open pull requests (`ownOpenPullRequests`, `completion.ts`) take in one that only references its issue,
  in its repository, with no closing keyword for another issue: the miss names it, as above.
- Before a done-check miss is assessed, after it is looked at once more, its work is asked at its source (`workCause`,
  `done-at-source.ts`, at most `PR_LOOKUP_MS`). Its item open, nothing shipped, and a pull request the job opened or
  pushed to open with merge conflicts or as a draft: the cause is **Own PR unfinished**; else one open with failing checks
  (`WorkPullRequest.checks`): **Own PR checks red** (`ownPullRequestCause`, `causes.ts`, pure). It replaces Not complete
  only, and the record says why (`its work shows its own pull request …, whatever the failure text says`). The rules,
  the retry limit and `auto.continue` are those of the cause. Not known in time: the text decides, as before.

## Needs a person (issue #516, 2026-10-08)

A failed job the assessor handed to a person showed among the recent failures, which a window of 50 hides, and as a
locked entry, which a dismiss hides: either way it could fall out of sight while nothing was still trying. A
**hand-off** (`src/failures/handoffs.ts`, the `handoffs` table, tenant migration 23) is the durable place for it: it
stays open until a person acts.

**It opens** in the transaction that ends automatic handling (`handoffReason`, `handoff.ts`, pure): the assessor's
record surfaced to a person (`person`; `retry_limit` when a transient cause used its retries), its decision's
automatic action off (`auto_off`: a recommended retry, or a hold with automatic hold off, or a failure assessed more
than a day after it failed, issue #517), or a run again the
assessor decided refused (`not_retried`). A dismissed locked entry with no hand-off, no pending run, not run again
and not held by its problem opens one (`dismissed`). At start, records left waiting with no hand-off (a restart
between the two, or a store from the build before) whose job is still failed, not dismissed and the newest of its
item are handed off. One per job at a time; the record keeps `handoffId`, so it is never handed off twice. It keeps
its assessment's summary, reasons and error, so it outlives the record's retention.

**It closes** when its item runs again — a new job whose `rerunOf` is its job, from Needs a person, the Queue, the
failure's Retry or the source (`run_again`) —, when a person resolves it (issue #551, below: `continued`,
`done_by_hand`, `wont_do`, or `run_again` with the resolution; `cleared` is a close by the build before), or when its
job ends finished (`finished`: its issue closed as complete). A failure whose
item already ran again when it is assessed is **superseded** (issue #517) and opens none; one whose item runs again
later, by a way that records no run again on it (the Queue's Run again, the source), turns `superseded` by the sweep,
`nextJobId` the newer job. Run again from
Needs a person (Run again, Continue) runs the item again past the retry limit and past its problem's hold (Release /
Retry with override: one action), and marks the record `retried`.

**It never goes by itself.** The prune deletes closed hand-offs older than `handoffRetentionDays` (default 30) and
never an open one; the failure records' prune does not touch them.

**Stale data clears itself (issue #529, 2026-10-09).** A hand-off nothing waits on any more closes without a person,
by the same rule at start and on every sweep, so one recorded before the rule existed clears on the upgrade. Closed,
never deleted, with why (`handoffs.ts` `settle`, `checked`):

- a newer job of its item exists that no `job.queued` closed it for — a store from the build before, or a newer job
  made while nothing followed the events (`superseded`, `nextJobId` the newer job); its record turns `superseded`;
- its job ended finished (`finished`) or is gone (`job_gone`);
- its job is live again (`resumed`, issue #1777): a Continue, Push it or a resume took it back to the queue by another
  way than this hand-off. It closes at the sweep and at once on the job's `job.continued` or `job.queued`, never while a
  person resolves it; its record turns `retried`, with the job itself as its next job. No hand-off opens for a live job.
  A failure record whose job is live again (Push it while it waits on its problem, then the problem resolved) ends the
  same way: Push it settles it in its own transaction, and a pending run again (`runPending`) reads the job first and
  after a refusal, so a release runs nothing and opens no hand-off. A live job's hand-off card offers no resolution, and
  the Run again checks (`takesBack`) say "it is already queued again: it runs when a lane is free", not "its end is not
  reported to its source yet" — that one is for an ended job only;
- its item is closed at its source any way but as completed, or gone (`item_closed`): the sweep's work check
  (`work-check.ts`, below "What happened, from the work") asks the source (`JobSource.workState`; GitHub: the issue's
  state, 404/410 gone) for each open hand-off, at once for a new one and then at most every 10 minutes; its record
  turns `item_closed`. A source that cannot tell leaves it open. Closed as completed, the work shipped: below.

A record nothing waits on (`superseded`, `item_closed`: `SETTLED`, `handoff.ts`) leaves Recent failures; the profile
and the history still count it. The badge and `counts` follow the open hand-offs.

**Open and ended (issue #618, 2026-10-09).** Failures shows only what is still open: Needs a person lists the open
hand-offs, and Recent failures the records that have not **ended**. A record ends (`endedAt`, `view.ts`) when its job
ran again or something settled it (an outcome in `RAN_AGAIN` or `SETTLED`), when its hand-off closed — continued, run
again, resolved, superseded, its item closed, its job finished — or when its job ended finished. The hand-offs closed
in the last day and the records that ended in the last day are history: Failures shows them under **Ended in the last
day** (`handoffs` with `status: closed`, `ended` in `GET /api/failures`), out of the counts and the badge. The same rule clears questions and
logins: an open question whose job ended or is gone is cancelled at `recover` and on each tick (`QuestionService.sweep`),
with `question.cancelled`, so the UI's open questions and the Needs you count drop it (issue #1457),
and a login, below in "Logins".

**Events.** `handoff.opened` (reason, summary, `notify`), `handoff.closed` (end, `nextJobId`) and `handoff.checked`
(its work state changed, issue #621: `item`, how many `pullRequests`, `shipped`). `notify` is the
setting `handoffNotify` (default on); off, the event is still recorded and streamed, but no webhook delivers it — the
dispatcher delivers no event whose data says `notify: false`.

**Failures view.** Needs a person first, its own count, then the open problems: each hand-off with its reason, what
happened in one plain sentence and the recommended resolution (its **card**, issue #621, below), its resolutions
(below, issue #551), and behind **Details** the assessment summary, the known cause, the reasons and the raw error. The Failures nav
badge counts open problems plus open hand-offs, read again on each `handoff.*` event: still open means still counted.

### Resolving a hand-off (issue #551, 2026-10-09)

Run again (a cold job, told nothing) and Clear (closed, nothing recorded) left a person not knowing what to do, what
doing it would lead to, or where to say what they did; the issue stayed `hopper:failed`. Now a card says it and takes
the answer.

**What to do.** Each card says what happened and recommends one resolution (its **card**, issue #621, below) and, by
each other resolution, what it leads to — for Continue whether the job's own session resumes (`continueResumes`) or a new
job runs. A resolution the daemon does not take now is said with its reason (`actions[*].why`), never offered.

**One place to answer.** A note box and four resolutions (`POST /ui/api/failures/handoffs/:id/resolve`, operator;
`handoffs.ts` `resolve`):

- **Continue** — when the job's own agent session can resume (its executor parks, it recorded `agentSession`, its
  pane state is kept), the *same* job is queued again (`SourceHost.continueJob`, `job.continued`): its source takes the
  item back as for Run again (`hopper:failed` goes), its end is to be reported again (`claimReported`,
  `finalReported` reset), it is pinned to the machine it ran on with the brief pending (`brief.ts`: the failure, the
  assessment, the error, the note), and `continued` sends its claim to the executor's reopen — the parked job's path:
  a new pane in its work tree (the worktree command finds it, or makes it again at the same path, so `claude --resume`
  finds the session), `--resume <session>`, the brief typed in. Its new failure is assessed on its own (the record
  continued is `retried`, `nextJobId` its own id). Otherwise a new job of its item runs (Run again with the brief after
  its prompt: the earlier error, the assessment and the note).
- **Run again** (`fixed`; *I fixed it* before #621) — the cause was outside the job; Run again with the note.
- **Done** (`done_by_hand`; *Done by hand* before #621) — the work is done, by the job's pull request or by a
  person; its job ends finished (`result` the link); its record `resolved`.
- **Won't do** — the note (required) says why; its locked entry is dismissed; its record `resolved`.

A run again a resolution makes closes the hand-off with the resolution, not by the new job's `job.queued` (the
hand-offs being resolved are skipped there).

**Report back.** The resolution is kept on the hand-off (`resolution`: action, who — the signed-in person's name, kept
here and never written out —, when, note, link, `resumed`) and `handoff.closed` carries its action. The sync loop tells
the job's source (`JobSource.resolved`) on the job's report chain, after the job's own end is reported, at once on
the event and again at each sync while `writeBack` is `pending` (a transient error is kept as `writeBackError`; a
permanent one ends `failed`). On GitHub (`writeResolution`): Done `hopper:done`, Won't do `hopper:rejected`,
in place of `hopper:failed`, so the issue is not taken again; Continue and Run again took it back already; then one
comment — what was done, the note quoted, the link — naming no person. It is the hopper's one comment (AGENTS.md
"GitHub text is neutral").

**Learn.** An admin names the hand-off's cause from its card ("this was X", "next time Y", its decision) through the
known causes (`POST /ui/api/failures/causes`, keyed by the record's signature): the next failure with it follows that.

**Follow it.** The card links the job that follows (`nextJobId`): the same job continued, or the new one.

### What happened, from the work (issue #621, 2026-10-10)

A card that repeated the raw error — "not complete: no pull request opened by this job…" — with a next step chosen by
the hand-off's reason left a person unable to tell what happened: the #613 job had updated a pull request that was
already merged, and the card still said the job hit a problem of its own. Now the hopper checks the real state first,
and the card says it.

**The work check** (`work-check.ts`, in the failure sweep). For each open hand-off, at once for a new one and then at
most every 10 minutes, the sweep asks the job's source what its work shows (`JobSource.workState`): its item — `open`,
`done` (closed as completed), `closed` (any other way), `gone` — and the pull requests the job opened or pushed to,
each with its number, `by` (`opened`: created at or after the job; `updated`: its head commit made at or after the job,
issue #618), its state (open, merged, closed), draft and merge conflicts. GitHub (`completion.ts` `workState`) reads the
issue, the merged pull request that closed it, the open pull requests that close it, the pull requests that mention it
in its own repo, and those the issue's text names (as the done-check does, at most 10). The answer is kept on the
hand-off (`work`, with `checkedAt`; JSON in its row: no migration, the build before ignores it); `handoff.checked` says
when it changed. A source that cannot tell, or fails to, leaves the hand-off as it was, asked again later.

**The work shipped** (`workShipped`, glossary **Shipped**): a pull request of the job's merged, or its item closed as completed. Nothing is left
to do, so the hopper closes the hand-off itself (`finished`) and the job ends finished (`SourceHost.finishShipped`,
`job.finished`, `result` what happened and the merged pull request's link); its end is reported to its source again, so
on GitHub its issue loses `hopper:failed` (`hopper:done` once closed, else `hopper:pr-ready`). A job whose pull request
merged never stays a failure. Its item closed any other way, or gone: the hand-off closes `item_closed`, as before.

**The card** (`card.ts` `handoffCard`, pure; `HandoffView.card`). `whatHappened`: short ASD-STE100 sentences from the
work, never from the error — "The job updated PR #616. #616 is merged. The issue is done.", "The job stopped before it
opened or updated a PR." — naming at most two pull requests (merged first, then open and ready, open otherwise, closed),
counting the rest. Before the first answer: "The job stopped with an error. The hopper is checking its PRs and its
issue." `recommended` and `why`, in order: the work shipped → Done ("The work is done."); the item closed or gone → Won't
do; the first pull request open and ready → Done, with its link ("The PR is ready. Review and merge it."); with merge
conflicts or a draft → Continue; closed without a merge → Run again; no pull request → by the reason (job-specific:
Continue; retries used up, automatic action off, run again refused: Run again; dismissed: Won't do). `link`: the pull
request Done points at, put in the Link box.

**The view.** The card's sentence first, then the recommended resolution as the main button with its why, the others
after it, smaller, each with what it leads to; the assessment summary, the known cause, the reasons and the raw error
behind **Details**. A viewer sees the recommendation without buttons. The buttons read Done, Continue, Run again,
Won't do; the actions (`done_by_hand`, `continue`, `fixed`, `wont_do`) and the API are unchanged.

A model's short summary of a long assessment is the hand-off's TL;DR (issue #569, "TL;DR"), under what happened.

Not done here, carried: Park, ask a question, or send to another machine or model as resolutions; a model-written
diagnosis of the failure on the card (issue #550).

**Only an action the hopper takes** (issue #1010, 2026-10-13). A card recommended Run again or Continue that its source
then refused (409), so the main button failed the same way each time. Now the view asks the source first, and the card
recommends only what is taken.

- **What the source takes back** (`SourceRegistry.takesBack`, `rerun.ts` `takesBackOf`): its source runs, can run an
  item again (`JobSource.rerun`), and was told the job's end. Run again, Continue and Push it refuse with the same words.
  Continue and Run again on a card (`handoffView`), Retry on a failure (`recordRetry`) and Push it on work not pushed
  (`pushAllowed`) are offered only when it does, else said with its why.
- **`Allowed.soon`**: a refusal that clears by itself in a short time — the job runs again by itself, or its end is
  reported to its source in a moment.
- **The card** (`card.ts` `takenCard`, pure): the recommended resolution refused for a short time stays, "… is taken soon:
  <why>. Try again in a minute."; refused for good, the other one that runs it again (Continue ↔ Run again) when taken,
  else Done: "<label> is not taken: <why>. Do the work by hand, then press Done. Or press Won't do." A closed hand-off's
  card is as it was.

Open decisions taken (issue #516): the name is *Needs a person*, a section of the Failures view, not a nav entry of its
own, and the domain word is *hand-off* (*dead letter* stays a not-term, as for the locked entry); the locked entry
stays in the Queue beside its hand-off (Won't do dismisses it; Clear did, before issue #551); entering notifies by a setting, default on. No setting
moves the badge: the Failures entry carries it.

### Work not pushed (issue #1010, 2026-10-13)

The reap and the sweep keep an ended job's scratch dir when a repository in it holds uncommitted or unpushed work
(`job.work_kept`, issue #401). Nothing showed it but a log line on each sweep, so the work sat there with no way out.
Now Failures lists it, and each has an action that moves it.

- **The list** (`src/domain/kept-work.ts`, pure; `src/failures/kept-work.ts`). An ended job whose newest work event is
  `job.work_kept` is **work not pushed** while its work item still waits on it (issue #1067, `keptWorkLeft`): the
  work-item ledger's items name their jobs with kept work, and `keptWorkShown` leaves out an item done or closed and an
  older job's of an item a newer job took over, even when the newer job failed too; `keptWorkLeft` leaves out a job a
  person dismissed (issue #1457: nothing waits on it). So a merged or closed item lists none, however old: `keptWork` in `GET /api/failures`,
  newest first, each with its paths, its machine (`machineRanOn`), its open hand-off, and `actions.push` and
  `actions.discard` (`{ ok }` or `{ ok: false, why }`). The Failures badge and `GET /api/sections` count each one that
  no open hand-off counts already.
- **Push it** (`POST /ui/api/failures/kept-work/:id/push`, operator, a box action, an optional note). Taken for a failed,
  finished or cancelled job (`PUSHABLE_ENDS`; not a rejected one, which never ran) whose own agent session resumes (`Engine.resumable`), the newest of its item. The job goes on in its own session and
  kept work tree, told `pushBrief`: look at the work tree, commit, push, open the pull request, as a draft when the work
  is not finished, and the note. With an open hand-off it resolves it as Continue (`handoff.closed`, `end:
  "continued"`); else `SourceRegistry.continueJob` with `{ keptWork: true }` (`job.continued`). Its source takes the item
  back as for Run again. The next reap at its end that keeps nothing records `job.work_removed` (`cleanup.ts`), so it
  leaves the list.
- **Discard** (`POST /ui/api/failures/kept-work/:id/discard`, operator, a box action; the UI asks first). `Sweep.discard`
  (`Engine.discardWork`) reaps the job's scratch dir on its machine with `discard` (the reap script's `$3`, a client
  target's `/reap` body `discard: true`): its git worktrees removed with `--force --force`, the dir removed whatever it
  holds; then `job.work_removed` with `discarded`, `person` and `via`. Refused, with why, when no work is kept, the job
  has not ended, or its machine is unknown or offline. The answer comes once these checks pass; the reap runs after it
  (issue #1194, "Actions answer at once"): the entry's `discarding` is `removing` meanwhile, and Failures shows it so from
  the click on. Out of reach, or kept all the same — a client older than this ignores `discard` —, the removal fails:
  `job.work_discard_failed` with why and who, `discarding` `failed` with the error (the refusal says to update the
  client), and Discard is offered again. `discarding` is kept in memory: after a restart the work shows kept, as it is.
- **Kept again** (issue #1470, `keptAgainOf`). A job pushes only to its own repository, so work in a clone of another
  repository in its scratch dir is never pushed by the job: Push it went on, the push was refused, and the reap kept it
  again, so Push it was offered again with the same brief, in a loop. Now, when the job went on in its kept work tree
  (`job.continued`: Push it, a Continue) and its reap kept no path it did not keep before, Push it is refused with why
  (Stuck lists it under `kept_work`); Discard stays. `pushBrief` also says a push goes only to the job's own repository,
  so the job names the work that stays and ends, and does not try the push.
- **Quieter sweep.** The sweep logs kept work only when it keeps it the first time.
- **Discarded once done** (issue #1105). Kept work of a job whose work item is `done`, as the ledger has it, waits on
  nobody: the sweep reaps its scratch dir with `discard`, as Discard does, and records `job.work_removed` with
  `discarded` and no person. A client older than the discard keeps it, and the sweep records nothing new.
- **Nobody waits on it** (issue #1187, `discardReasonOf`). The sweep discards kept work the same way, with no person, and
  `job.work_removed` names the `reason`: `merged` (its item is done, above); `superseded` (the newest job of its item
  finished, its cleanup done, with no work kept: it took the work over, and Push it is refused for an older job anyway);
  `proposal` or `research` (it finished a proposal or a research report, never work to push). The reap's rule reads
  work already on a remote under other commits as pushed ("The reap"), so the sweep's next pass removes such kept work
  with no reason at all. Each pass reads every kept entry again by these rules, so entries kept before them clear
  themselves. `pushed` (issue #2087): the hopper pushed each commit of it for the job ("The reap", kept tips).
- **Never a push on the machine** (issue #2087). A job's machine holds no GitHub credentials, so a push there fails.
  No refusal, todo or brief tells a person to open the work tree on its machine and push it: Push it goes through the
  job, which pushes through the hopper; else Discard, or run its item again.
- **Gone from disk** (issue #1120, "Hopper's own disk use"). Kept work whose scratch dir and job worktree a person or a
  cleanup outside the hopper removed leaves the list at the next sweep: `job.work_removed` with `gone`.

Done since, in issue #1010: the Stuck list ("Stuck
work"), with counts by cause and one bulk action per cause; a hand-off card recommends only an action the hopper takes ("Only an action the
hopper takes", under "Needs a person"); Tend again on a pull request the hopper gave up on ("PR waiting", "A pull request stays in sight"); Push it
for a finished or cancelled job — its source takes the item back as for Run again (a cancelled job's too, for this
Continue only), and `SourceHost.continueJob` takes those ends only `by` `keptWork` (a hand-off's Continue stays a failed
job's).

**Verification:** `test/domain/kept-work.test.ts` (`keptAgainOf`, issue #1470), `test/engine/sweep.test.ts` (the log once), `test/engine/sweep-discard.test.ts` (discard, its refusals, the removal after the answer and its failure),
`test/client/reap-discard.test.ts` and `test/client/reap.test.ts` (the script for real: dirty and unpushed work removed,
the worktree entry gone, nothing outside the job's scratch dir; issue #1187: squash-merged, rebased and re-made commits
read as pushed, part of the work or other content not), `test/integration/kept-work.test.ts` (Push it through
the hand-off, and for a finished and a cancelled job, resuming the session; Discard, its event, a second discard refused; issue #1470: the same work kept again, Push it refused).
Issue #2087: `test/client/reap-tips.test.ts` (the kept tips of a clean worktree and a clone, none for a change),
`test/domain/kept-work.test.ts` (`proxyPushedOf`, `keptPushedOf`), `test/engine/sweep-discard.test.ts` (kept work the
hopper pushed removed, `pushed`; a tip it did not push stays kept), `test/integration/work-kept.test.ts` (no
`job.work_kept` at the job's end when the hopper pushed each tip), `test/github-proxy/push-saga.test.ts` and
`test/gitlab/git-broker.test.ts` (`heads` recorded), `test/failures/push-brief.test.ts` and `test/domain/stuck.test.ts`
(no push on the machine).

### Push it by itself (issue #1472 part 2, 2026-10-17)

A job that ended done with work not pushed waited for a person's Push it, sometimes for days. The issue asks that the
hopper push the work from any state with no click. This part does it for the case that is the hopper's alone to decide.

- **What** (`autoPush`, `src/failures/kept-work.ts`; run by the failure sweep after its work check). Each entry of
  **work not pushed** whose job is `finished`, has no open hand-off, and whose Push it is taken now (its session resumes,
  it is the newest job of its item, its source takes the item back, it was not kept again) goes on as Push it does: its
  own agent session and kept work tree, told `pushBrief` with "The hopper asks you" in place of "A person asks you".
  `job.continued` records `keptWork` and `auto`.
- **Once for each job.** A job that has a `job.continued` with `keptWork` already (a person's Push it, or this) is not
  pushed by itself again: its work waits for a person, and the kept-again rule (issue #1470) still applies to Push it.
  So a push the hopper refuses, or a job that cannot push, costs one turn, not a loop.
- **Not a failed or a cancelled job.** A failed job's failure goes to the assessor, which runs it again, continues it, or
  hands it off; a hand-off's Push it is a person's. A cancelled job a person stopped. Both stay as they were.
- **The setting.** `auto.push` in the failures settings, default on (`POST /ui/api/failures/settings`, Failures → settings,
  "Push work a finished job did not push"). Off, the work waits for a person as before. A settings record saved before the
  field existed reads it on, field by field (`failureSettingsOf`).

- **A fresh session when none was recorded** (`Engine.reopens`). Push it, by a person or by itself, takes a job whose
  executor parks and whose pane state is known, whether or not its agent session was recorded (`Engine.resumable` asks
  for both). With no session, herdr-claude reopens the job in its kept work tree as a parked job's fresh start does
  (issue #530): a new pane, a new `--session-id`, then its task and `pushBrief` with `fresh`, which says it has none of
  the earlier session's history. Through an open hand-off only when its own session resumes: else the hand-off's
  Continue runs a new job, away from the kept work, so Push it is refused with why.

- **A print-mode agent's job** (`Executor.reopensKept`). Its executor cannot park, but its state names its work tree
  (saved before the first turn) and its reap keeps work in the job's scratch dir there. `Engine.reopens` takes it too.
  Push it continues the same job (`job.continued` with `keptWork`); the executor's `resume` sees `continued` and starts a
  fresh turn in the saved work tree, never the old chat: its task, then `pushBrief` with `fresh` (it is never
  `resumable`), then the protocol. The same job id keeps the same scratch dir, so the turn sees the kept work.

- **A job with no pane state** (`keptTreeOf`, `src/domain/kept-work.ts`). A herdr-claude job whose pane state was never
  recorded (a state save is dropped while the hopper stops) left no work tree in its state. Its kept work does name one:
  the sweep records `job.work_kept` with each repository it kept, and the job's own worktree is
  `<work tree>/.worktrees/<name>/<job id>`. `Engine.reopens` takes such a job when its executor parks and its newest
  `job.work_kept` names its job worktree. The runner gives a job Push it continued that tree (`ExecutionContext.keptTree`);
  the executor's reopen uses it when it has no pane state: a new pane in that work tree, a fresh session (never a
  recorded one: with no state the job is not `resumable`, so the brief says fresh), its task, then `pushBrief`. Kept
  work that names only a clone in the scratch dir names no tree the agent ran in: Push it is still refused, "its work
  tree cannot reopen". Running the agent in the shared work tree beside the clone could change another job's files.

Left of issue #1472 part 2: a push to a repository other than the job's own and not one of its user's job repositories
(refused, issue #1470). Which repositories a job may push to is a security decision for a person.

**Verification:** `test/integration/auto-push.test.ts` (a finished job pushed by itself once, with `auto`; not again when
its work is kept again; `auto.push` off; a failed job not pushed by itself), `test/integration/kept-work.test.ts` (a
person's Push it, with `auto.push` off), and in `auto-push.test.ts` a finished job with no recorded agent session pushed in
a fresh session in its kept work tree. `auto-push.test.ts` also: a finished job of an executor that `reopensKept` goes
on in a fresh turn, and one of an executor that neither parks nor reopens is refused with why;
`test/adapters/print-agent-executors.test.ts`: each print-mode agent, continued, starts a fresh turn in its saved work
tree, its task first, never its old session. `auto-push.test.ts` also: a finished job with no pane state goes on in a
fresh session in the job worktree its kept work names, and is refused with why when its kept work names none;
`test/herdr/executor-park.test.ts`: the reopen of a continued job with no pane state opens that job worktree, fresh.

### Actions answer at once (issue #1194, 2026-10-14)

A person's action on a local hopper must feel instant. Approve took 5 to 20 s: the route awaited a GitHub read of the
issue and then a full sync of the source before it answered, and the UI waited for that answer. Discard of kept work
awaited a round trip to the job's machine that removes git worktrees. The rule now: **an action records its decision and
answers; its slow side effects run after the answer**, and what the person sees follows from the answer, the stream and
the next read, never from a poll.

- **Intake actions** (`SourceRegistry.intakeAction`, `src/sources/sync.ts`). The sync an action asks for runs after the
  answer, not awaited; its status reaches the UI on the stream (`source.status`). Since issue #1238 it is no full sync:
  it runs after the action's GitHub outbox rows are sent ("GitHub outbox").
- **Approve** (`src/sources/github/approvals.ts`). The hash is checked against the request card the last sync showed, and
  that text is recorded at once (`IntakeTrust.approve`, `source.request_approved`); the issue is not read again. The
  person approves the text they read: an edit since makes the next sync show the card again, with the approved text and
  the change, and no job runs a text nobody approved. After the answer, not awaited: on a reopened card `hopper:done`
  goes from the issue, and the assignee's comments the job would see are read and added to the approved snapshot
  (`IntakeTrust.approvedComments`). Both are GitHub outbox rows; a discover does not take the issue until they are sent. One that
  fails shows on the item, its **write-behind** (below), until Approve again goes through; an Approve again of the same
  text before a discover listed the issue taken is `done` and records nothing more.
- **Decline** writes nothing to GitHub and answers at once; so does Dismiss.
- **Assign to me, Release claim, Take off the backburner, Take into Intake** (`src/sources/github/intake-actions.ts`,
  part 2). The checks the last sync can answer run, then the answer; the GitHub write runs after, and its event
  (`source.issues_assigned`, one per issue, `source.claim_released`, `source.backburner_lifted`,
  `source.issue_taken_in`) is recorded once GitHub took it, so no event says a write that never happened. No connected
  account is refused at once.
- **Write-behind**: the GitHub work an intake action leaves after its answer — Approve's, and the four above. Since
  issue #1238 it is rows in the **GitHub outbox** (below), kept in the user's store. The item shows it
  (`IntakeOutcome.writeBehind`): `running`, then gone once it went through, or `failed` with why, also in the source's
  `detail.writeBehindErrors`. The same act sent again before a discover listed the item again (a second click, another
  tab) is `done` and writes nothing more, unless it failed; then it is sent again.
- **Discard kept work** ("Work not pushed"): the checks, then the answer; the reap after, followed by `discarding`.
- **Run again and Rework** (`SourceRegistry.giveBack`, `src/sources/rerun.ts`, part 3). Run again took 20 s and Rework
  22 s with GitHub slowed to 2 s a call: the route awaited the source's **give-back** — on GitHub the issue read, assigned,
  reopened and its labels changed, read again, its projects and comments read; for Rework the pull request read and made a
  draft first — and only then made the new job. Now the checks the hopper can make itself (the job the newest of its
  item, its end reported to its source, a source that takes an item back; for Rework finished and following an open pull
  request) run, then the answer, `202 { jobId, giveBack }`. The give-back runs after, on the job's report chain, and the
  new job follows as before, with `job.rerun` (now naming who and the way) or `job.rework_requested`. A give-back that
  fails — GitHub out of reach or refusing, the issue no longer assigned and not to be assigned, a newer job made meanwhile —
  records `job.give_back_failed` with why and makes no job; the act is offered again. The same act sent again while one
  runs answers that one. The state is kept in memory, as the write-behind's is: after a restart the job is as it ended,
  and Run again is offered.
- **Retry, a hand-off's Continue and I fixed it, Push it, Tend again** (`SourceRegistry.afterAnswer`, part 4). Each
  awaited the same give-back, and Retry also its source's done-check. Now each is checked by its own service —
  `Failures.retryable`, `Failures.handoffResolvable`, `pushable` (`src/failures/kept-work.ts`), `checkTendAgain`
  (`src/sources/tend-again.ts`): the record, hand-off or kept work as the view offers it, and for Tend again its tend
  job's end reported —, then the answer, `202 { jobId, giveBack }`, `jobId` the ended job. The act's own path runs after,
  unchanged: the failure `retried`, the hand-off closed, the job continued (`job.continued`) or tended
  (`job.pull_request_tended`). One that fails records `job.give_back_failed`, its `act` `retry`, `continue`, `fixed`,
  `push` or `tend`; a Retry whose work is done at its source finishes its job, and says so there. The same job's act sent
  again while one runs answers that one, whatever act it was. Done by hand and Won't do write nothing first and answer
  as before.
- **A stuck cause's bulk action** (`src/failures/stuck.ts` `actOnStuck`, part 6). It awaited each item's give-back, one
  after another: two hand-offs took 16 s with GitHub slowed to 2 s a call. Now each item is checked and answered as its
  own button is (`giveBackOf`, `src/http/ui/failures.ts`), and its give-back runs after, in the same runner, with the same
  `job.give_back_failed` when it fails. The answer is `{ cause, done, refused }` as before: `done` the items answered, their
  give-back running; `refused` the items a check refused now. Won't do writes nothing first, and is resolved before the
  answer as before. The toast says how many move.
- **Merge now and Close PR** (`src/sources/pull-request-acts.ts`, part 5). Merge now took 12 s with GitHub slowed to 2 s a
  call, and a merge GitHub refused 4 s: the route awaited the source's merge on the job's report chain — the pull request
  read, merged, the issue read, labelled and maybe closed. Now the checks the hopper can make itself (the job, its source
  running and following pull requests, the job following an open one) run, then the answer, `202 { jobId, act }`. The
  merge or close runs after, on that chain, and is recorded as before (`job.pull_request_merged`,
  `job.pull_request_closed`, with who and the way). One that fails — GitHub refused it (a draft, merge conflicts, a
  required check) or was out of reach, or the pull request was no longer open — records the new event
  `job.pull_request_act_failed` with why; the card stays, and the act is offered again. The same job's act sent again
  while one runs answers that one. The state is kept in memory, as a give-back's is.
- **Queue order, the landing batches, Answer, End wait and Pick up** record and answer without GitHub or the job's
  machine: the budget tests hold them to it.
- **The UI.** Approve and Decline wait on the card only for the answer. Discard shows removing from the click on, and
  `failureAct` reads the failures again before the action ends, so the entry shows the result, never what was before.
  Assign to me, Release claim and Take off the backburner (`ui/src/components/intake-groups.tsx`): from the click on,
  the row says GitHub is updated and offers that action no more, until a list the daemon sent after the click says how
  it ended; a failed write says why, and offers the action again. A refusal shows the action again at once.
  Run again (Dashboard) and Send back for rework (Pull requests; `ui/src/store/give-back.ts`): from the click on, the
  button says Running again or Sending back and sends nothing more, until the stream's `job.rerun`,
  `job.rework_requested` or `job.give_back_failed` for that job says how it ended — a toast says which, a failure with why.
  Retry and a hand-off's Continue and I fixed it (Failures), Push it (Work not pushed, which offers no Discard
  meanwhile) and Tend again (Pull requests) do the same, until `job.rerun`, `job.continued`, `job.pull_request_tended` or
  `job.give_back_failed`; the Pull requests page reads its cards again then. Merge now and Close PR
  (`ui/src/store/pull-request-acts.ts`): from the click on, the button says Merging or Closing, and the card sends
  nothing more, until the stream's `job.pull_request_merged`, `job.pull_request_closed` or `job.pull_request_act_failed`
  for that job says how it ended — a toast says which, a failure with why —; the page reads its cards again then.
  Take into Intake (Pull requests, Not tracked; part 6): its write-behind shows on its row too, as the untracked pull
  request's `writeBehind` (`census.detail`, from the source's write-behind of its issue), since the issue is in no Intake
  list yet. From the click on, the row says the issue is taken into Intake on GitHub and offers it no more, until a list
  read after the click says how it ended: failed, with why, and offered again; or the issue in Intake.
- **Budget.** `test/integration/action-latency.test.ts`: with GitHub held and the machine slowed to 2 s, Approve, Decline,
  Discard, Assign to me, Release claim, Take off the backburner, Run again, Rework, Queue order and the landing batches
  answer in under 200 ms, their decision recorded, and the slow work ends after;
  `test/integration/action-latency-give-back.test.ts` holds Retry, I fixed it, Push it and Tend again to the same;
  `test/integration/action-latency-give-back.test.ts` holds a stuck cause's bulk action to it too;
  `test/integration/action-latency-pull-requests.test.ts` Merge now and Close PR; and
  `test/integration/action-latency-local.test.ts` Answer, End wait and Pick up. **CI asserts the order, not the time**
  (`test/support/latency.ts`): a clock on a shared runner is not reliable — one took 210 ms for an answer that takes
  18 ms on a developer machine. So GitHub is **held** (`test/support/slow-github.ts`): each of its calls waits until the
  test releases it. An action that waited for GitHub would never answer, and the test fails by its timeout; one that
  answers first answers, and its GitHub work is recorded only after the release. The time of an answer is asserted
  against the 200 ms target only off CI, or with `HOPPER_PERF=1`; `HOPPER_TEST_LATENCY_BUDGET_MS` sets the bound for one
  run.
- **In a browser** (`test/integration/action-latency-browser.test.ts`, part 9). The built UI in Chromium (Playwright),
  against the real daemon, with GitHub held: a click on Approve shows the card Approved, and a click on Assign to me shows
  its row updating GitHub, before GitHub answers anything. After the release, the approved job shows on Jobs. The time is
  asserted as above: the card within the 200 ms target, the job on Jobs within 1 s of the release. Measured on a developer
  machine: the card in 37 to 87 ms, the job in 100 to 111 ms. It needs the built UI (`npm run build:ui`) and a Chromium —
  Playwright's own (`npx playwright install chromium`), or the one `HOPPER_TEST_CHROMIUM` names —; without them it is
  skipped and says why. The pull request check builds no UI and installs no browser, so there it is skipped. Chromium
  gets a temp dir one level above the run's (`cr-*`), since its socket path must fit in 108 bytes.

- **Approve of a sandbox request** answers before the box starts, since issue #1002 ("Sandboxes jobs start"): the
  approval is recorded, and the start runs after, in the background. `test/integration/sandbox-start-hangs.test.ts` holds
  the answer to the budget (part 7).
- **After-answer timings** (`src/sources/after-answer-timings.ts`, part 7). The work an act leaves after its answer runs
  on a queue: the job's report chain (a give-back, Merge now, Close PR) or the source's sync chain (the sync an act asks
  for). A slow act was either slow itself or stood behind other work: before this issue, an Approve waited up to 15 s for
  a sync already running, then ran its own sync for 5 s. So each run is kept as its wait on the queue apart from its run,
  per act. The act is named where it starts (`withAct`, an `AsyncLocalStorage`, so every await under it keeps the name):
  a give-back act, `merge` or `close` on the job's report chain, and `sync:<act>` for each sync an act asks for — an
  intake action's (`sync:approve`), or the sync after a Run again (`sync:rerun`). A sync that several acts asked for is
  timed once for each, each wait from its own ask. Work no act started (a timer's sync, a report) is not timed. Kept in
  memory, the last 100 runs of each act; `GET /api/sources` answers `afterAnswer`: per act, `count`, `waitMs` and `runMs`
  (each `{ p50, p95, max }`) and `lastAt`. `test/integration/action-latency-after-answer.test.ts`: an Approve sent while
  a sync runs answers within the budget, and its `sync:approve` shows the wait for the running sync apart from its own
  run; `test/integration/action-latency-pull-requests.test.ts`: Merge now's `merge` wait and run together cover the time GitHub held it.

- **Fixed waits on the action paths** (part 6, checked). `PR_LOOKUP_MS` (10 s, `src/failures/timeouts.ts`) bounds a
  done-check's look at its source: on Retry it runs after the answer (part 4), never before it. `RECONCILE_MS` (10 s,
  `src/sandbox/service.ts`) is how often the sandbox module checks its boxes; no action this section names waits for it.
  The UI's 10 s tick (`ui/src/store/stream.ts`) reads the health and the update notice only; an action's result comes
  from its answer and the stream.

- **The write-behind tries again, and Sources shows it** (part 8). A write GitHub refused for now — a 5xx, or GitHub out
  of reach — failed at once before, and waited for a person to press the act again. Now it is tried again after 1 s and
  after 4 s more (`RETRY_MS`, the in-memory write-behind; since issue #1238 the **GitHub outbox**'s backoff below); meanwhile the item's `writeBehind` is `running` with
  its `attempt` and the `error` of the try before. A write GitHub refuses for good (`GitHubApiError.permanent`: a 403, 404,
  410 or 422), or rate-limited past the next try (`retryAt`), fails at once: trying again gets the same answer. The next
  discover waited for every write-behind under way, so its tries too (until issue #1238: no discover waits now). The source's detail says how many writes run (`writeBehindPending`) and when the last went through
  (`lastWriteBehindAt`), beside `writeBehindErrors`. Each act's write is timed as an after-answer timing of its source:
  `afterAnswer` entries with `source`, the act its name (`approve`, `assign`, `release`, `unbackburner`, `take_in`), its
  run every try. Sources shows both: on a source's card a line "GitHub writes: N under way · last went through …" and each
  write that failed (`ui/src/views/source-sync.tsx`); below the sources, **Work after an act** (`ui/src/views/after-answer.tsx`),
  per act its wait and run as p50 / p95, the slowest first, read when Sources opens and on Read again.

Not yet so (issue #1194, later parts): no end-to-end check measures the card in a browser. The outbox that batches and
merges GitHub writes, and keeps them across a restart, is issue #1238 ("GitHub outbox" below).

### GitHub outbox (issue #1238, 2026-10-15)

Issue #1194 made intake actions answer at once, but their GitHub writes were a fire-and-forget in memory: a restart lost
them, nothing coalesced them, each was sent at once, the next discover waited for every write under way, and each action
started a full sync of its source. The **GitHub outbox** is the durable form of that write-behind.

- **Rows** (`github_outbox`, tenant migration 62, `src/store/github-outbox.ts`; the types, the port and the coalescing are
  `src/domain/github-outbox.ts`). One row per GitHub change an action asks for: its source, repository, issue (the item's
  key), the act and its tag (Approve's hash), the change (`add_labels`, `remove_labels`, `add_assignees`, or Approve's
  `read_comments`), the event to record once GitHub took it, its state (`pending`, `sending`, `sent`, `failed`), attempts,
  last error and when it is due. The action keeps its rows in the transaction of its own local change (Approve's
  approved text and its rows commit together, or neither does). Sent rows are kept 7 days.
- **Sending** (`src/sources/github/outbox.ts`, `JobSource.flushOutbox`; when, `src/sources/outbox-flush.ts`). The rows due
  are sent in one batch: half a second after an intake action (`OUTBOX_BATCH_MS`), so the clicks of a burst go together,
  and every 5 s (`OUTBOX_EVERY_MS`) from the start on, so a restart sends what a stopped hopper left. A send **claims**
  its rows (issue #1959): one `UPDATE` makes the rows due `sending` until the claim ends (`OUTBOX_CLAIM_MS`, 2 minutes,
  renewed before each call), so of two hoppers on one database one sends each row; a row a stopped or killed hopper left
  `sending` is due again once its claim ends. Labels and assignees are idempotent, so a second send of the same change
  does no harm.
  A comment is not (issue #1590): its first line is a hidden key (`<!-- job-hopper v1 kind=outbox id=… -->`, a hash of
  its first row's source, id and time), and its send lists the issue's comments first: one that carries the key is the
  post a stop left unrecorded, and the row is `sent` with no second comment. The key is in the form the context filter
  and the thread's reply check already take as the hopper's own.
  One batch runs at a time per source; one call that does not end holds the source's next batch, never a sync. Every call
  goes through the source's GitHub API, so the shared rate limiter applies.
- **Coalescing** (`coalesce`, pure). The rows due for one issue become the fewest calls: an add and a remove of the same
  label cancel out and send nothing (those rows are `sent` with no event); the newest row of a label says what it ends as;
  the labels left go in one remove call and one add call; the assignees in one call; Approve's reads in one. Each issue
  gets its own calls.
- **Failure.** A call GitHub refused for now (a 5xx, a rate limit, no answer) leaves its rows `pending`, with the error,
  due after a backoff — 5 s, doubled each time, at most 5 minutes, or GitHub's own retry time —; a permanent refusal, or
  the fifth attempt, leaves them `failed`. While the outbox tries again by itself the item's `writeBehind` is `running`, with
  its next `attempt` and the `error` of the try before (as issue #1194 part 8 had it); a failed row shows `failed` with why.
  The same act sent again sends failed rows again, from their first attempt.
- **A reconnect needed holds the writes** (issue #1891). While the connected account is **expired** (`connected`, from
  the account source), the outbox sends nothing. A call that fails once the account is expired — the token read refused,
  or GitHub refused the token and the renewer ended the connection — leaves its rows `pending`, with the error and no
  attempt counted: they are never `failed` for it, and no act is told it gave up. Later issues of the same batch make no
  call. The action's own local change stays committed: the database is the source of truth. The owner gets the one notice
  of the expired account (`connected_account.expired`), and every screen asks to connect again; once a connection is
  there, the rows go through at the next send.
- **Syncs never wait for it.** A discover lists what GitHub says. An issue with rows not sent is not taken (`held`): the
  sync neither overtakes the action (a job before its approved comments are read, before `hopper:done` is gone) nor undoes
  it. The listing is not overlaid with the rows' labels: a job taken on a label not yet removed would get its claim label
  from the hopper's own report, which the outbox would then remove.
- **No full sync per action.** An intake action asks for none. Once its rows are sent, each repository the outbox wrote to
  is due (`repoChanged`) and the source syncs — a timed sync, which lists only what is due; an action with no row (Decline,
  an Approve that reads no comments) gets the same sync after the batch window. Take into Intake sent drops its pull
  request's offer at once (`takenIntoIntake`), until the next census reads it.
  The sync after an action is timed `sync:<act>` ("After-answer timing") from the action on, so its wait counts the batch
  window and the send.
- **What the UI reads.** The source's status is read again after an action and after a batch that had rows due, and sent on
  the stream, so the item's marker follows the rows. The detail keeps part 8's names, so Sources' line on the source's card
  reads the outbox: `writeBehindPending` (rows not sent, not failed), `lastWriteBehindAt` (when the last row went through),
  `writeBehindErrors` (each item whose rows failed). Each row sent or failed for good is timed as an after-answer timing of
  its source (`afterAnswer` with `source`): its wait in the outbox, from its row to its call, apart from the call.
- **Hand-off resolutions** (part 2). A person's resolution of a hand-off (issue #551) is rows too, act `resolve`, tagged
  `<job id>@<resolution time>`: for Done by hand and Won't do, the claim labels and `hopper:failed` removed and the end
  label added, then for every action the one `comment` (`resolutionChanges`, `src/sources/github/report.ts`). The
  write-back (`src/sources/write-back.ts`) keeps them once, still on the job's report chain after the job's end is
  reported, and asks the source at each sync where they stand (`JobSource.resolved` answers a `ResolutionWrite`):
  `written` once GitHub took each row, `pending` with the error of the try before, `failed` for good. The hand-off's
  `writeBack` follows it. At the hand-off's close its source sends after the batch window; a sync that asks again never
  asks for a send, so a resolution still pending never starts sync after sync. A resolution that failed before part 2 has
  no rows and is not sent again by itself, so no comment is posted twice. Comments coalesce too: the same body on one issue
  is one call; comments go after the labels. An `add_labels` call makes the hopper's labels on the repository first.
- **Failed rows on Sources** (part 2). The detail lists them as `outboxFailed`, one per item and act (`key`, `repo`,
  `act`, `error`, `attempts`), and Sources shows each with a **Retry**: the intake action `retry_outbox` sends the item's
  failed rows again from their first attempt, then the source sends after the batch window. A resolution's hand-off
  failed meanwhile goes back to `pending`, then `written`, at the syncs after. `writeBehindErrors` stays for the item
  markers.
- **Merge now and Close PR** (part 3). A person's act on a job's open pull request is one row, act `merge` or `close`,
  tagged with the job's id, change `pull_request` (the act, the job, who acted): `JobSource.pullRequestAct` keeps it, and
  answers the act already on its way for the job, so a second click, another tab or the CLI sends nothing more. It must
  be seen now, so its source sends at once (`outboxFlushes.now`), with no batch window. The source's send hands the row
  to the sync loop (`OutboxActs`, `src/sources/pull-request-acts.ts`), which follows the pull request with the act on the
  job's report chain and records the merge or the close with who pressed it, as before. A refusal for now waits the
  backoff; a permanent refusal, or the last attempt, fails the row and records `job.pull_request_act_failed` once. A
  restart sends a row not sent. The act sent again sends its failed row again; Sources lists the failed row with a Retry.
  The row is no intake marker: the Pull requests card shows the act. Tests: `test/sources/github-outbox-pull-requests.test.ts`,
  `test/integration/github-outbox-pull-requests.test.ts` (sent after a restart), `test/integration/action-latency-pull-requests.test.ts`.
- **Run again and Rework** (part 4). A person's Run again or Rework of an ended job is one row, act `rerun` or `rework`,
  tagged with the job's id, change `give_back` (the act, the job, who acted, Rework's notes): `JobSource.giveBackAct`
  keeps it once the answer's checks pass (`src/sources/rerun.ts`), and answers the give-back already on its way for the
  job, so a second click, another tab or the CLI sends nothing more. Its new job must be seen now, so its source sends at
  once, as Merge now's does. The source's send hands the row to the sync loop (`OutboxActs.giveBack`), which runs the
  same give-back as before on the job's report chain — on GitHub the issue reopened and assigned, its end labels gone,
  for Rework the pull request made a draft first —, then makes the new job (`job.rerun`, `job.rework_requested`, with who
  pressed it). **The new-job step is durable**: a row sent again once its new job was made — a stop after the job and
  before the row was marked sent — finds the item's newest job made from this one (`rerunOf`) and makes nothing more. A
  refusal for now (a 5xx, GitHub out of reach) waits the backoff; a permanent refusal (a refused give-back: the job no
  longer the newest of its item, its end not reported), or the last attempt, fails the row and records
  `job.give_back_failed` once. The act sent again sends its failed row again, with the notes it was kept with; Sources
  lists the failed row with a Retry. A restart sends a row not sent. A source with no GitHub outbox (the `direct` source)
  gives back as before, in memory. Tests: `test/sources/github-outbox-give-backs.test.ts`,
  `test/integration/github-outbox-give-backs.test.ts` (sent after a restart).
- **Retry, Continue, I fixed it, Push it and Tend again** (part 5). Each is run by its own service — the failures
  service, its kept work, the tending —, so its row names the run, never holds it: change `give_back` with the act, the
  job, who acted, `target` (what the act names: the failure record for Retry, the hand-off for Continue and I fixed it,
