  the job for Push it and Tend again), the person's `input` (a hand-off's note and link, Push it's note) and `at` (when it
  was kept). The services' check (`GiveBackCheck`, `src/failures/give-backs.ts`, set on the sync loop at the start) is the
  one each button's route ran before: `SourceRegistry.afterAnswer(act, id, acting, input)` asks it, refuses with why, else
  keeps the row through `JobSource.giveBackAct` and sends at once, as Run again's. **The send checks it again**, then runs
  it (`OutboxActs.giveBack`): after a restart the same check holds, and the run is the same as before the outbox. A check
  that refuses at the send while the job moved on since `at` — it runs again (Continue, Push it), or a job of its item was
  made since (Retry, I fixed it, Tend again) — means a stop came between the run and the row's sent mark: the row is sent
  and nothing more is done. Any other refusal, or a run that fails, fails the row at once and records
  `job.give_back_failed` once, as before the outbox: a run may have done part of its work, so it is not tried again by
  itself. The act sent again, or Sources' Retry, sends its failed row again, checked again. A source with no GitHub outbox
  (the `direct` source) runs it in memory, as before. Tests: `test/sources/github-outbox-after-answer.test.ts`,
  `test/integration/github-outbox-after-answer.test.ts` (a row in the store sent by the sync loop on its own).
- **A job act's marker** (the last part). A person's act on one job — Merge now, Close PR, a give-back — shows on the job
  from its row, as an intake item shows its write: the detail's `jobActs`, by job id, holds each job whose act row is not
  sent (`jobActMarkers`, pure, `src/domain/github-outbox.ts`): `running`, with the next `attempt` and the `error` of the try
  before while it waits its backoff, or `failed` with why (a failed row wins over the job's other rows). The Pull requests
  card and the job view show it (`ui/src/components/job-act.tsx`) under the job's facts, read from the sources the stream
  keeps current: the source's status is sent again after each batch that had rows due. A failed act says to press its
  button again, which sends the failed row again; Sources still lists it with a Retry. Once the row is sent the job has no
  marker. Tests: `test/sources/github-outbox-job-acts.test.ts`, `test/ui/job-act-marker.test.ts`.
### Stuck work (issue #1010, 2026-10-13)

Failures, Parked and Pull requests each showed their own part of what waits on a person, one card at a time. With 169
failed jobs, seven parked and pull requests the hopper gave up on, no page said how much was stuck or why, and each card
took its own press. Now Failures starts with **Stuck**: every item that waits on a person, counted by its stuck cause, and
one press per cause where the hopper can move each item.

- **The causes** (`src/domain/stuck.ts` `stuckOf`, pure; `stuck` in `GET /api/failures`, built in `viewOf`). Each item is
  in one cause only, in this order: an open hand-off by its card's recommended resolution — `continue`, `run_again`,
  `wont_do`, `done_by_hand`, or `taken_soon` while that resolution is refused for a short time (`Allowed.soon`) —; a
  failure that Run again takes and no open hand-off counts (`retry`); work not pushed, `push` when Push it is taken (its
  open hand-off is then counted here, not with the hand-offs) else `kept_work`; an open pull request card (the Pull
  requests page's own list, `pullRequestList`) the hopper gave up on, `tend` after a failed tend else `checks`, or one whose
  tend its source refused (`tend_refused`); a job on a wait that names nothing it waits on (`wait_unnamed`,
  "waiting on nothing recorded", issue #1245); a job on a wait whose agent session ended (`stranded`, issue #1779); a job whose own wait broke (`own_wait`, issue #2684: below); an
  item blocked with no pull request to wait on (`pr_open_stale`, issues #1231, #1891).
  Each has `ids`, `what` in a few words, and `act`, the bulk action's button, or `todo`, what a person does.
- **The bulk action** (`POST /ui/api/failures/stuck/:cause`, operator, a box action; `src/failures/stuck.ts`
  `actOnStuck`). Only the causes in `STUCK_BULK`: `continue`, `run_again`, `wont_do`, `retry`, `push`, `tend`, `wait_unnamed`, `stranded` (else 400;
  `wait_unnamed`, Resume all, ends each such wait with a note that tells the job to go on or name what it waits on, issue #1245;
  `stranded`, Wake all, ends each such wait as a person's End the wait, issue #1779).
  It reads the view at the press and runs the cause's action on each item, through the same path as its own button, with
  who pressed it, answered once each is checked, its give-back running after (issue #1194, "Actions answer at once"): the hand-off's resolution (Won't do with its card's why as the note, so the
  source is told why), the failure's Run again, Push it, Tend again. An item refused meanwhile is skipped and said with
  why (`refused`); the others go on. The answer: `{ cause, done, refused }`.
- **The view** (`ui/src/views/stuck.tsx`). First in Failures, only when some work is stuck: the total, then each cause's
  count and what it is, its bulk action — asked first, with the count — or what a person does. A viewer sees no button.
- Why no bulk Done: Done needs a person to look at each pull request or the work. The cause says so.
- **No parked job** (issue #2414). A parked job waits by design, not as a failure: it is in Parked only, never in Stuck,
  and it counts toward neither Failures' list nor its badge (`viewOf` reads no parked job for `stuckOf`; the Failures
  section counts open problems, open hand-offs and work not pushed). The `parked` cause had no bulk action, so nothing
  moved to Parked. Each workflow keeps one home (issue #896).
- **No job that only still waits, and no cleanup leftover** (issue #2684). A job on its own wait whose agent the hopper
  ended (a wait release, issue #2326) is parked off its machine by design; past its wait's deadline it only still waits.
  Listed as `own_wait` for being overdue, such jobs filled Failures. Now a wait is stuck work only when it **broke**
  (`waitBroke`): its own command was flagged stuck (`stuckAt`), or it is overdue and its check cannot test its condition
  (`brokenAt`: a read of the items or the pull request failed, or the job's source reads none) or it was met before and the
  hopper does not wake the job for it again (`repeat`). A wait with no check (`none`: an approval, a grant, a gated outside
  event) only waits. An ended job's cleanup leftover is not job work for a person: the cleanup worker tries it again at
  each sweep pass, Machines counts it, and the job's parts list names each entry ("The resource ledger").
- **Direct jobs** (issue #901). A direct job has no issue, so nothing is assigned: the `direct` source gives its
  submission back (`JobSource.rerun`), and a failed direct job is in Stuck as any failure, by its hand-off or as `retry`,
  and its bulk action runs it again. Since issue #1068 the `direct` source follows a direct job's pull request
  ("Direct jobs", "Its pull request"): one the hopper gave up tending is an open pull request card like any other
  (`tend`, `checks`).

**Verification:** `test/domain/stuck.test.ts` (each cause, an item counted once, the order, no parked job),
`test/integration/park.test.ts` (a parked job in neither Failures' stuck work nor its section count),
`test/integration/stuck.test.ts` (two hand-offs resolved by one press; a cause with no bulk action refused),
`test/integration/direct-jobs.test.ts` (a failed direct job in Stuck with a bulk action, and one press runs it again),
`test/ui/stuck-view.test.ts` (the counts, the todo, the bulk action asked first, a viewer).

## Parked jobs (issue #501, 2026-10-08)

A person takes a running job, or one on a question, out of its lane for an open-ended time — days or weeks —
and re-queues it later on the same machine, where it resumes its agent session. Distinct from a job on a
question (`waiting_answer` keeps its waiting pane and Claude in it) and from a job's own wait for something
(issue #483, "A job's own wait"): parking is a person shelving a job, and holds nothing live.

- **Park.** `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/park` (least role `operator`, the same as cancel). Accepted for a `running`
  job or a `waiting_answer` one whose executor has `park` (`parkingExecutors` of `GET /api/health`), with or
  without an **agent session** (issue #530); else 409 with the reason (`parkRefusal`, `src/engine/park.ts`). A running job is
  interrupted at once (abort reason `park`): the herdr-claude executor leaves its pane as it is, the runner
  records the park and frees the lane in one transaction (`recordPark`), then `Executor.park` ends Claude,
  stops the job's scope and processes through the machine's own connection (the reap without a scratch dir),
  and closes the pane. A job that ended done in that moment is recorded as done. A job on a question is
  parked the same way, without the runner. The job is `parked`, `parked: { at, from }`, `resumeOn` its
  machine; `job.parked { from, machineId }`. A machine that cannot be reached is logged; the sweep stops what
  still runs there (a parked job is not live).
- **Kept.** The work tree, the job worktree and branch in the scratch dir, the agent's own session data, the
  machine, the open question. The sweep removes scratch dirs of ended jobs only; the reap runs only at a job's
  end; the deferred cleanup is of ended jobs: none touches a parked job. Restart recovery leaves it as it is.
  Credential files left in the scratch dir are not renewed while parked (no process reads them) and are
  written again at the re-queue's start.
- **Its question.** Stays open, in **Parked** with its job (issue #565), and in Questions too (issue #2634): it still
  blocks its job, and since every wait on a person parks its job (issue #2335) most open questions are a parked job's.
  Questions, its badge, Needs you and the Attention panel show it, and `GET /api/sections` counts it in `questions`
  as its job is counted in `parked`; the cloud link's `questionsAwaitingOwner` counts it too. One answer, from either
  place, clears it from both. While its job is parked it never
  expires and is not renotified (`QuestionService`: `expire`, `renotify` and `armHuman` skip it). An answer
  or a close is kept as `pendingAnswer`; the job stays parked. Dismissing it cancels the job, as for any job
  on its question.
- **Pick up** (a re-queue; the UI's word since issue #565). `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/requeue` (least role `operator`), `job.unparked { to }`. With its
  question still open: back to `waiting_answer` (`to: waiting_answer`), the human timeout started again
  (`QuestionService.unparked`); the answer then re-queues it as any. Else `queued` (`to: queued`) with
  `pendingAnswer` the answer kept, or `PARKED_RESUME` (it was parked; go on). A pending answer pins it to
  `resumeOn` and gives it the resume boost, so it waits for its machine — held `pinned machine <m> offline`
  while it is — and never starts elsewhere, unless it is picked up to **resume elsewhere** from its checkpoint
  (issue #921, "Checkpoints and resume elsewhere"). A fresh start elsewhere is not offered: cancel it and Run again.
- **Resume.** The claim calls `Executor.resume`; with `job.parked` set, herdr-claude reopens: it stops
  whatever of the job still runs there (two agents in one session would interleave), opens a new pane in the
  recorded work tree, enters the same job worktree (the worktree command uses the one there), starts
  `claude --resume <agentSession>`, and sends the answer. The next outcome clears `job.parked`.
- **Fresh start** (issue #530). A parked job with no agent session (`startsFresh`: started before the session
  was recorded) cannot resume one. Its re-queue is refused (409) unless the request says `freshSession: true`,
  the person's confirmation from the UI's Re-queue dialog: never a silent fresh start. Its claim then opens
  the new pane in the kept work tree as above, starts Claude with a new `--session-id` (recorded, so a later
  park resumes it), and sends the task, then `freshStartBrief` (`src/engine/park.ts`, wrapped around the
  pending answer by the runner: no history, look at the work tree first, and — parked on a question — the
  question and the answer, or that none was given), then the protocol footer. With its question still open it
  waits on it again first, as any; the answer then starts it fresh the same way.
- **Agent session.** herdr-claude starts Claude with a session id it chose (`--session-id`, a UUID) and
  reports it once Claude is up (`ExecutionContext.agentSession`). Jobs started before that have none; they
  park all the same, and start fresh at the re-queue. Executors that cannot park (the print-mode agent
  executors, the test executor) are not in `parkingExecutors`.
- **Machine and lanes** (issue #530). Capacity is lanes: the decider counts busy and draining lanes, and a
  job on a question or a parked one holds none, so neither counts against its machine's lane cap.
  `jobsOnMachine` (`src/engine/queries.ts`) is not capacity: it keeps a client machine's connection and
  refuses removing a machine while jobs need it. A job on a question stays in it — its pane and Claude are
  live there, and the answer is typed into them. A parked job is not in it: nothing of it runs, and parking
  ends its pane and agent, so the machine is free of it at once.
- **UI.** Park on a running lane's job, on a job on a question in the Waiting panel, and on its question card
  (For you / Questions, issue #530), where a person decides a job must wait; Pick up and Cancel on a parked
  job. Park only where `canPark` (`ui/src/model/board.ts`, from `parkingExecutors`) says the daemon takes it;
  on a running job or one on a question it does not apply to, the job says why instead (`parkRefusal`).
  Pick up of a job that starts fresh asks first, saying it starts a fresh session in the kept work tree with
  its question and answer as context. Only for a role that operates. The Dashboard's Waiting panel and the Queue view list parked jobs in their own group
  (`/api/queue` `parked`); the Waiting card says how many are parked; they are never running and on no lane.
- **The Parked section** (issue #565, `ui/src/views/parked.tsx`). Parked jobs have their own place, a section like
  Questions, Logins and Failures, with its own nav entry in Waiting on you (issue #2713; a tab of Failures before), never
  counted in Failures (`SECTIONS.parked`, events `job.parked` and `job.unparked`): one compact row per
  job — its issue title and number, the machine it resumes on, how long it has been parked, its open question's first
  line, whether its agent session resumes or it starts fresh —, high-priority jobs first, then the longest parked
  (`parkedOrder`). Expanded, the full question and **Answer and pick up**: the answer (`POST
  /ui/api/questions/:id/answer`, kept as `pendingAnswer`), then the pick up, in one step; a fresh start is confirmed
  first; an answer kept when the pick up fails leaves the job parked, answered. Pick up and Cancel on each row. Its
  badge counts the parked jobs, marked when high priority, quiet (muted): a reminder, not an alarm.
- **A login it waits on** (issue #476) fails when it is parked, as for any job that no longer runs (`the job
  ended`); the resumed session meets its tool again and reports a new one.
- **Auto-park** (issue #650; the timeout replaced by issue #2335, "Every job that waits on a person parked" below: a
  job parks 5 s after its question reached a person, with no setting). A question that waits on a person longer than the **park timeout** parks its job by
  itself, so a night of unanswered questions does not keep panes and agents live on the machines. The engine checks
  on each tick (`src/engine/auto-park.ts`): a `waiting_answer` job whose question is open at the human stage, waited
  at least the timeout since `escalatedToHumanAt` (time at the escalation levels, Jev and the fixed answers does not
  count), or since `waitRestartedAt` when it began to wait on a person again — its job re-queued from parked with
  the question still open, or the item of its fork rejected (issue #692: re-queued, it waits the full timeout again,
  not a second) —, is parked on the Park button's path (`recordPark`, then `releaseParked`), with `parked: { auto: true, why }`
  and `job.parked { auto: true, why }`; `why` reads "Parked automatically: the question waited 30 min." (the timeout
  that applied). The timeout is the user's setting `autoPark` (`GET /api/auto-park`, `POST /ui/api/auto-park`,
  least role `admin`, `auto_park.settings_changed`; Settings → Auto-park; `hopper auto-park [set]`): `minutes` for a
  job that is not **high priority** and `highPriorityMinutes` for one that is, its live priority; default 30 for
  both; 0 turns it off for those jobs; at most a week. Read on each tick, so a change applies without a restart, and a
  restart loses no timer (the wait is from the stored time). Never parked by it: a question a risk rule or the
  consequential guard sent to a person (`Question.keptBy`, set by `toHuman`: `risk`, `guard`) — it keeps its pane, as
  before —; a job with no agent session (its pick up needs a person's confirmation, issue #530); one a fork of its
  question still works for (issue #548). A job waiting on a login is running, not on a question, and never parks by
  itself. **Its answer picks it up**: the answer (or a close) to an auto-parked job's question re-queues it in the
  same transaction (`onAnswered` → `recordUnpark`): `queued`, its priority as it was, pinned to its machine, and its
  claim resumes its agent session there with the answer; no Pick up. The Parked row offers **Answer** in place of
  Answer and pick up, and the Parked row and the Dashboard's parked row show `why`. A job a person parked keeps the
  answer until it is picked up, as before.
- **Settings.** Who may park is the operator role, as for cancel, and roles apply live. Auto-park's timeouts above;
  no limit for parked jobs.
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: the status and the fields are in the job's JSON. A build before
  this one, on a store holding a parked job, shows it in no group and never runs it.

### Parking a proposal or a research report (issue #2167, 2026-10-19)

A person sets a proposal or a research report aside without acting on it or rejecting it: they park the job that waits
on it. Parking was already open to that job (it is `waiting_answer`); this adds who parked it and why, takes the item out
of its section, and keeps the review from moving on while it is parked.

- **Who and why.** `POST /ui/api/jobs/:id/park { reason? }` (`parkBody`, at most 500 characters) and `hopper job park
  <id> [--reason <text>]`. The person signed in (`actingOf`: `by` their name, `via` `ui`, `cli` or `api`) and the reason
  are kept in `parked` (`by`, `via`, `reason`, `src/domain/park-ask.ts`) and on `job.parked`. A running job is parked
  only once its executor stepped aside, maybe by another hopper (issue #1662): the command keeps the ask on the job
  (`parkAsk`) before it stops the run, and `recordPark` moves it into `parked`. Auto-park and the moves keep no person:
  their `why` says why. Nothing is written to GitHub: a park is the hopper's own state, and the hopper writes only labels
  to an issue ("GitHub text is neutral").
- **Out of its section.** A **parked item** (`parkedItemOf`, `src/domain/review.ts`) is an open or sent-back item whose
  job is parked on it. `GET /api/<section>` leaves it out of `status=open`, and `status=parked` lists only those, each
  with `parked: { at, by?, via?, reason? }`; `GET /api/sections` does not count it in its section (Parked counts its job).
  The UI shows it folded under the section's list (`ui/src/views/parked-items.tsx`: its job, its first part, how long
  parked, by whom and why, Pick up), and the Parked row of its job says what it waits on.
- **Nothing moves while it is parked** (`src/review/service.ts`). No reviewer level enters it; a level's reply that comes
  back after the park is dropped, its call cleared, so the level is asked again later; the end of the levels neither
  continues with it (auto-continue) nor sends it to a person; a person's decision is refused, 409 `parked` ("pick it up
  first"), so no follow-on job starts and its job neither ends nor runs.
- **Pick up puts it back.** `recordUnpark` already returns the job to `waiting_answer` on its open item. After the
  commit, `ReviewService.resume` starts the review again from the stage it stopped at (`resumeAt`), unless a review of
  it is still in flight. The item keeps its versions, trail, stage and seen mark.
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `parked` and `parkAsk` are fields of the job's JSON body, and the build before
  ignores them. A park survives a restart and a move to another hopper: it is all in the database.
- **Its issue closes meanwhile.** As for any job: closed in a way that cancels it (not planned, label removed, gone),
  its job ends cancelled at the next sync, the sweep cancels the item, and a pick up is refused (409). The item keeps
  its versions in the history. Closed as completed after it started, the job stays parked, and a pick up puts it back.
- **A job parks through the `park` skill** (the last part of issue #2167, `src/http/job-park.ts`). A running job lists its
  user's open proposals and research reports, parked or not (`GET /job/park`), and parks or picks one up (`POST /job/park
  { act: park | pick-up, item, reason? }`), with its proxy token, only while it is at work. It reaches the same
  `engine.park` and `engine.requeue` a person's buttons do; who did it is `job <its id>`, `via` `job`, on the job's
  `parked` and on `job.parked` and `job.unparked` (which now also names who picked a job up, a person or a job). The
  limits keep a job's power under a person's:
  - It parks only an item whose job waits on it (`waiting_answer` on that item): never a running job, never itself, never
    a question. Parking stops nothing that runs; it only holds a decision back.
  - It picks up only an item a job parked (`parked.via` `job`). A person's park stays until a person picks it up (409),
    so a job cannot undo a person's act.
  - It takes no decision: a parked item is still decided only by a person, after a pick up.
  - Nothing is written to GitHub, as for a person's park.
  The owner's issue asked for it, and AGENTS.md's list of `/job/*` routes names it, as each such route.
- **Verification.** `test/integration/park-review-item.test.ts` (a proposal and a research report parked and picked up,
  the refusals, a restart, a reviewer level in flight, a running job's park with a reason, a long reason refused),
  `test/integration/park-review-item-closed.test.ts` (its issue closed both ways), `test/ui/park-review-item.test.ts`,
  `test/integration/job-park.test.ts` (a job lists, parks and picks up; a person's park it cannot pick up; a running job
  it cannot park; bad tokens and calls refused).

## Preemption (issue #1525, 2026-10-16)

When a job of higher priority waits and no lane it may use is free, the hopper parks a running job of lower priority and
gives its lane to the waiting job. The job parked resumes later from where it stopped, not from the start.

- **Who preempts whom** (the decider, step 7b, `src/decider/preempt.ts`; pure). Only a job that step 7 left waiting for a
  lane (a wait, never a hold) preempts. Its own priority (`job.priority`, the live priority, never the resume or router
  boost) must be strictly higher than the running job's: equal priority never preempts. The running job must be
  `running` (not `claimed`), its executor must park (`parkingExecutors`), it must have an **agent session** (else its pick
  up needs a person's confirmation, issue #530), and it must have run at least the **minimum run time** since its start or
  resume (`startedAt`). Its lane must be busy and not drained in this Decision, and the waiting job must fit on that
  machine once the lane is free: step 7's own fit (`fitsLane`), with the lane taken out of the machine's, its executor's,
  the unpinned and the priority-lane counts. Of these: the lowest priority, then the one started last (it loses the least
  work), then the lowest id. Each waiting job preempts one job at most, in step 6's order; each running job is preempted
  once.
- **In flight.** The Decision marks the job `preempted: { at, by, byPriority, priority, machineId }` and emits
  `job.preempted` in the transaction that applies it (`src/engine/decision-step.ts`). The decider counts a running job
  with that mark as in flight: it is not preempted again, and its `by` job preempts no other. A mark older than
  `PREEMPT_IN_FLIGHT_MS` (2 min) — a park that never came, a restart in between — is void, so nothing waits on it for good.
  A job the runner does not hold any more loses the mark at once (`preemptRunning`).
- **The park** (`src/engine/preemption.ts`). After the commit the runner parks the job on the Park button's path
  (`runner.park`: abort reason `park`, `recordPark` frees the lane in one transaction, `releaseParked` ends its pane and
  agent and takes its **checkpoint**). Its work tree, branch, agent session and checkpoint are kept. A job that ended done
  in that moment is recorded as done. The freed lane wakes the engine (`job.parked`); the waiting job takes it in the next
  Decision.
- **Back in the queue.** Once parked, the job is picked up at once (`requeuePreempted` → `recordUnpark`, `job.unparked
  { to: queued }`): `queued`, pinned to its machine (`resumeOn`), `PARKED_RESUME` pending, so its claim resumes its agent
  session in its kept work tree (`claude --resume`). While `preempted` it waits at its own priority with **no resume
  boost** (a boost would take the lane back from the job that preempted it), and step 6 orders it ahead of the other jobs
  of the same effective priority. Its next start clears the mark, and its minimum run time counts from that start.
- **No thrash.** Only a strictly higher priority preempts, the minimum run time stops a resumed job from being preempted
  again at once, and the preempted job never outranks its preempter.
- **Settings** (`preemption`, a user setting; `GET /api/preemption`, `POST /ui/api/preemption`, least role `admin`,
  `preemption.settings_changed`; Settings → Preemption): `enabled` (default on) and `minRunMinutes` (default 10, 0 to a
  day). Read on each Decision (`preemptionInput`), so a change applies without a restart. Off, `DecisionInputs.preemption`
  is absent and nothing is preempted; Decisions stored before this change have none either.
- **Shown.** The job graph and the job's parts list say `Queued: preempted by #12 Fix the roof` (or `Parked: …`) and what
  comes next ("It resumes from where it stopped when a lane is free", `preemptedByOf`, `src/domain/job-words.ts`). The
  Dashboard's Waiting and Parked rows show which job took the lane, both priorities, and that it resumes
  (`ui/src/model/preemption.ts`). The job's timeline has `job.preempted`, `job.parked` and `job.unparked`.
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `preempted` is in the job's JSON, `preempt` and `preemption` in the Decision's,
  the setting a key of its own. A build before this one ignores the mark; a job it shows as queued resumes as a parked
  job picked up does.
- **Not built.** Resume on another machine: the preempted job waits for a lane on its own machine (its pin), as a parked
  job picked up does. "Resume elsewhere" from its checkpoint stays a person's act (issue #921). The companion issue on
  durable work items is not needed for this: the park keeps the work tree and the agent session, and takes a checkpoint.

Verification: `test/decider/preemption.test.ts` (who preempts whom, ties, equal priority, the minimum run time, off,
executors that cannot park, no agent session, in flight, the order of a preempted job), `test/integration/preemption.test.ts`
(the real daemon over the fake herdr: a high job parks the low one and starts, the low one resumes its own session; equal
priority, the minimum run time and off preempt nothing; the settings), `test/domain/preempted-words.test.ts`,
`test/ui/preemption.test.ts`.

## The memory floor (issue #2291, 2026-10-20)

Seven jobs queued at once on a WSL machine of a 14 GB VM all started on free lanes before any of them took its memory.
Their Gradle builds (a JVM each) and agents then filled the VM: load over 270, under 1 GB available, and the hopper's own
API stopped answering for hours. Lane counts, lane tuning (issue #688) and placement by expected cost did not stop it: a
lane count says nothing about memory, the recommendation applies nothing by itself, and the expected cost is a preference,
never a hold, read from a machine reading taken before the burst took its memory.

- **Admission** (the decider, step 7, `src/decider/memory-floor.ts`; pure). Each machine with a memory reading has a
  **memory floor**: its `memoryFloorGiB` option, else 10% of its memory and at least 1 GiB (`MEMORY_FLOOR_PERCENT`,
  `MEMORY_FLOOR_MIN_GIB`). A job there needs a **job's memory**: the `memoryPerJobGiB` option (default 2 GiB,
  `MEMORY_PER_JOB_GIB`), or its expected memory peak when that is more. The Decision counts, per machine, the memory
  available less a job's memory for each job on its lanes that is claimed or started (or resumed) less than 10 minutes
  ago (`MEMORY_RAMP_MS`: its memory is not in the reading yet), and for each job it places there. A job starts or resumes
  there only while that, less its own need, stays at or above the floor. Else it **waits**, with the reason
  `waiting for memory: <machine> has 7 GiB available, 4 GiB of it kept for 2 jobs started lately, and a new job needs 2 GiB over its floor of 1.4 GiB`,
  each such machine after a `;`, then the machines left out (step 7, issue #2499). A job's need is the flat 2 GiB, or its
  expected memory peak from its repository's or kind's job cost group when that is more ("Job cost profiles"): a
  repository whose jobs peak at 3 GiB reserves 3 GiB a job.
  Issue #2499: the memory a job holds with no lane in use (its **waiting memory**, "Machine resources over time") is in
  the reading, so it is counted; the wait names it after the memory available: `local has 3 GiB available (2.5 GiB is held
  by 1 job with no lane), and a new job needs …`. A machine sample keeps it (`waiting_mem`, tenant migration 93, a nullable
  column the build before never writes), and the job costs ("Job cost profiles") and the lane load leave it out of the
  memory used, so a job on its own wait no longer raises the expected peak of the job that runs beside it.
  A wait for memory preempts nothing: preemption frees a lane, not memory. This holds for an elbow-in and a critical job
  too, and for a job resuming on its pane.
- **WSL.** The memory available is Linux's in the VM, or Windows' own free memory (`hostMemFreeBytes`, issue #868) when
  that is lower. A machine with no reading (a container target, an old client, offline) has no floor.
- **A host pool** (issue #2499, `poolHosts`). Seats in containers on one VM each read their own cgroup limit, so each had
  room while the VM they share did not, and only the hopper's own machine read Windows' free memory. A reading names its
  kernel by its boot id (`bootId`, `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, the same in every container on one kernel) and,
  under a cgroup limit, the kernel's own memory (`kernelMemTotalBytes`, `kernelMemAvailableBytes`, from /proc/meminfo).
  The machines with a memory room whose readings name one boot id are a **host pool**: two machines or more, or one in a
  container. Its memory available is the lowest kernel reading of its machines (a reading not in a container is the
  kernel's), or Windows' free memory when one of its machines reads that lower; its floor is 10% of the kernel's memory
  and at least 1 GiB. A job there needs room in its machine's memory and in the pool's: the pool's available less a
  job's memory for each job that any of its machines keeps (started lately, or placed in this Decision), less its own
  need, at or above the pool's floor. Else it waits: `waiting for memory: a's host (shared with b) has 4 GiB available,
  2 GiB of it kept for 1 job started lately, and a new job needs 2 GiB over its floor of 1.4 GiB`. A machine with a floor of
  0 is in no pool. A pool below its floor pauses a job ("The memory pause").
- **Memory pressure** (issue #2499). A seat near its cgroup limit reclaims all the time (`memory.events` `max` in the tens
  of thousands): its tasks stall on memory while its reading still shows memory available. Each reading says its **memory
  pressure** (`memPressure`, PSI): the share of the last 10 s that some task (`someAvg10`) and every task (`fullAvg10`)
  waited on memory, from `memory.pressure` of the cgroup whose limit it reads, else `/proc/pressure/memory`; an ssh target's
  probe prints `/proc/pressure/memory`. A machine whose `someAvg10` is at or above 20% (`MEMORY_PRESSURE_PERCENT`) takes
  no new job and no job back, whatever its memory available: `waiting for memory: a's memory is under pressure: its tasks
  waited on memory 35% of the last 10 s, and a new job starts only below 20%`. A floor of 0 turns this check off too. At
  40% or more (`MEMORY_PRESSURE_PAUSE_PERCENT`) it also pauses a job ("The memory pause").
- **OOM kills** (issue #2499). A seat at its cgroup limit has processes killed for memory, and once a kill frees memory its
  reading shows memory available again. Each reading says its **last OOM kill** (`memOomKillAt`): when its meter last saw
  the count `oom_kill` grow, in `memory.events` of the cgroup whose limit it reads (that cgroup and every cgroup under it),
  else in `/proc/vmstat`. A count is a counter, so the meter compares it with its read before: its first read, and a read
  of another cgroup, see no kill. A machine whose last OOM kill is less than 10 minutes old (`MEMORY_OOM_KILL_MS`) takes
  no new job and no job back, and has no memory room: `waiting for memory: a's memory killed a process 3 min ago (out of
  memory), and a new job starts only 10 min after`. A floor of 0 turns this check off too. An ssh target's probe prints the
  same counts (`cgo <dir> <n>` for each cgroup with a limit, `oom <n>` from `/proc/vmstat`), and its attached machine keeps
  the count from one probe to the next (`oomWatch`, part 13). `memory.events` `max` (the limit was hit and memory reclaimed) is not
  read: a cgroup full of page cache hits it in normal work, and the memory pressure already says when the reclaim stalls tasks.
- **The CPU throttle** (issue #2499, `src/decider/cpu-throttle.ts`). A seat with a CPU quota (`cpu.max`) whose tasks want
  more CPU than the quota gives is throttled, while its CPU busy can read below resource pressure. Each reading says its
  **CPU throttle** (`cpuThrottledFrac`): of each cgroup on its path with a quota, its own and those above it, the share of
  its CPU periods throttled since the read before (`cpu.stat` `nr_throttled` of `nr_periods`), the most of them. A machine
  whose CPU throttle is 50% or more (`CPU_THROTTLE_FRAC`) takes no new job and no job back, and no job elbows in there:
  `waiting for CPU: a's CPU quota held its tasks back in 62% of its periods lately, and a new job starts only below 50%`.
  A memory wait comes first: the CPU wait names only machines whose memory holds the job. A machine with free lanes and a
  waiting job says so on its lane plan (`CPU holds no more job: …`), and a wait names it as left out (`a is throttled: …`).
  It is not turned off by a floor of 0, since it is no memory check. A machine with no quota and a first read say none.
  An ssh target's probe keeps no count from one probe to the next, so it reads `cpu.stat` of each cgroup with a quota
  before and after its one second of CPU lines (`ct0`, `ct1`, part 13): its throttle is that second's.
- **Placement by memory room** (issue #2499, `better` in `src/decider/assign.ts`). A machine's lane cap is a count of jobs,
  and 9 lanes of 2 GiB each did not fit a 14 GiB VM. So of the machines a job may go to, after placement pressure, the one
  with the most **real room** goes first: its lane room, only as far as its **memory room** holds jobs (its memory over its
  floor, the lower of its own and its host pool's, less what is kept, divided by a job's memory; none under memory
  pressure). A job whose expected memory peak (from its cost history) is more than a job's memory counts its real room in
  jobs of its own peak (issue #2737): a machine with many free lanes and little memory holds one such job, and a machine
  with fewer lanes and more memory may hold as many. So a heavy job goes where its peak fits most often, not where the
  most small jobs would fit. Then the one with the most memory over its floor, then the most lane room, then the lowest id. A machine with
  no memory room counted is judged by its lanes alone. Each place in the Decision lowers the machine's memory room, so a
  burst spreads over the machines by what they hold now. The Decision's reasons name each machine's memory room:
  `b: memory for 5 more jobs (10.6 GiB over its floor of 1.4 GiB)`. A machine with free lanes, a waiting job and no memory
  room says so on its lane plan: `memory holds no more job: 3 GiB available, and a new job needs 2 GiB over its floor of
  1.4 GiB`. The lane cap itself stays as configured: a lane cap below its busy lanes would drain them.
  The lane recommendation ("Lane tuning") is never more than the jobs the machine's memory holds in all (its **memory
  lanes**), so an admin who applies it gets a lane cap that the memory holds.
- **The memory pause** (step 7c, `memoryPauses`). An online machine whose memory available is below the floor itself
  pauses the running job that started there last: its executor parks (`parkingExecutors`, now an input of every
  Decision, whatever the preemption setting), it has an agent session, and no preemption names it. One per machine every
  2 minutes (`MEMORY_PAUSE_EVERY_MS`): a job marked `memoryPaused` that recent, or the hopper's own record of its last
  pause there (`memoryPausedAt`, kept in memory, since between the park and the requeue the paused job is no input), holds
  the next. The Decision marks the job `memoryPaused: { at, machineId, availableBytes, floorBytes }` and emits
  `job.memory_paused` in its transaction; the runner parks it after the commit on the preemption's path
  (`preemptRunning`, `requeuePreempted`): lane freed, pane and agent ended, work tree, agent session and checkpoint kept,
  then queued at once, pinned to its machine, to resume its session. It starts again only when the memory holds it; its
  start clears the mark.
  Issue #2499 (`src/decider/memory-pause.ts`): a machine whose memory pressure is at or above 40%
  (`MEMORY_PRESSURE_PAUSE_PERCENT`, twice the admission's share, so a machine that only takes no new job pauses none)
  pauses too, whatever its memory available: `pauses r2 on local/lane-2: local's memory is under pressure: its tasks
  waited on memory 45% of the last 10 s, at or above 40%; r2 started there last`. And a host pool whose kernel memory
  available (as admission reads it, Windows' free memory when lower) is below the pool's floor pauses the job that started
  last on any of its machines, though each has memory of its own: `pauses r2 on b/lane-1: the host of a, b has 1 GiB
  available, below its floor of 1.4 GiB; r2 started there last`. One pause at a time for the pool: a recent pause on any
  of its machines holds the next, and a pool pauses none when one of its machines pauses in the same Decision. The event
  carries the pool's memory available and floor, and the job's own machine.
  Issue #2737: the pause takes the job of the **lowest priority** there (on any machine of the pool), and of those the one
  that started there last, so high-priority work runs on while lower work makes room: `pauses r1 on local/lane-1: local has
  0.5 GiB available, below its floor of 1 GiB; r1 has the lowest priority there (10)`, `… and started there last of them`
  when more than one has it; with one priority among them, `r2 started there last` as before. The job's mark also keeps its
  `priority` and the pause's `why` (the reason's middle part), and the Queue shows it on the job while it is queued or parked:
  `Paused for memory: local has 0.5 GiB available, below its floor of 1 GiB. This job had the lowest priority there (10). It
  resumes from where it stopped when the memory holds it.` A mark from the build before has only the bytes, and says them.
- **The API stays up.** The hopper runs on the machine it guards, so keeping the machine off its memory limit is what
  keeps `/api/health` and the UI answering; the held-loop health port (issue #1383) still tells a held event loop apart.
- **Settings.** Plain options of the `local`, `ssh` and `client` machine sources (`memoryFloorShape`), read at every
  list, so a change applies at the next Decision. A floor of 0 turns both admission and the pause off for that machine.
  Not on a container target, whose memory is not read.
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `memoryPaused` is in the job's JSON, `memoryPause`, `parkingExecutors` and
  `memoryPausedAt` in the Decision's. A build before this ignores them; a job it shows as queued resumes as a parked job
  picked up does. Issue #2737 adds only optional fields to both (`priority`, `why`), which a build before ignores.
- **Not built.** A cap on JVM or Gradle memory inside jobs (`org.gradle.jvmargs`, `--max-workers`): the hopper does not
  know a job's build tool, and the floor bounds every kind of job. Per-job memory accounting by process tree is not read
  (as in "Machine resources over time").

Verification: `test/decider/memory-floor.test.ts` (a burst of 7 starts what fits, jobs started lately keep memory, a
resume waits, the better machine, own options and 0, no reading, the expected peak, WSL, no preemption for memory; the
host pool: two seats on one kernel, two kernels, Windows' free memory for the pool, no pool alone or with a floor of 0; memory
pressure: at 20% no new job, below it one, the machine not under pressure, a floor of 0; the
pause: the newest job, at the floor nothing, one at a time, executors that cannot park and no session, off),
`test/decider/memory-pause.test.ts` (issue #2499: a host pool below its floor pauses the newest job of any of its machines,
none at its floor or across kernels, one at a time for the pool, a machine's own pause first; memory pressure at 40% pauses,
below it none, a floor of 0), `test/decider/placement-cost.test.ts`, `test/plugins/memory-floor-options.test.ts`, and
`test/integration/memory-floor.test.ts` (the real daemon over the fake herdr: a burst of 7 queued jobs on 8 lanes starts
2, the rest wait for memory while `/api/health` answers; below the floor the newest job is paused, queued again, and
resumes its own session once the memory holds it).
Issue #2737: `test/decider/memory-burst.test.ts` runs Decision after Decision against a model of two machines' memory
(a 14 GiB WSL VM whose Windows holds 1 GiB more, and a 16 GiB machine): 16 jobs that each take their 3 GiB peak three
minutes after they start all run, and neither machine falls below its floor; a job that takes 4 GiB over its peak makes
its machine pause the job of the lowest priority, which starts again on that machine only after the extra memory is freed.
`test/integration/memory-floor.test.ts` pauses the low job through the daemon, though the high one started later.

### Wait release: jobs on their own wait hold no agent while a job waits for memory (issue #2303, 2026-10-21)

Reported from a real run: a queued job did not start for 40 minutes with no job running. Every machine said `waiting for
memory`: 4.3 GiB available, a new job needs 3.8 GiB over its floor of 1.4 GiB. The VM held about 9.5 GB with nothing running:
50 Claude processes, about 7.5 GiB in all, one for each of the 50 jobs on their own wait. A job on its own wait keeps its pane
and agent ("A job's own wait"), so with the memory floor on, the waiting jobs alone held the memory that no new job got, and
the queue moved only when waits ended by chance.

- **The release** (the decider, step 7d, `waitReleases` in `src/decider/memory-floor.ts`; pure). A new input, `waitSessions`:
  each job on its own wait whose agent the hopper may end (`waitSessionsOf`, `src/engine/wait-release.ts`) — not released
  already, not stranded, with an agent session, an executor that parks, a machine to resume on (`resumeOn`), and a wait the
  hopper ends by itself: what it waits on is the hopper's to see (`paneCarriesWait` false), or the job named a time to wake
  at (`time_passed`). Never a wait on its own command or an outside event only its pane's background poll watches: ending
  the pane would end the wait's only watch. On each machine a job **waits for memory** on (the machines it had a lane on,
  `memoryShort` from step 7), the Decision names every such job there, the oldest wait first (`waitRelease`, with a
  reason). All of them, not as many as the shortfall: what one agent holds is not read (about 150 MiB in the report, against
  2 GiB or more a new job needs), and a released wait costs only a resume. The memory it frees is not counted in this
  Decision: the next Decision reads it, so the job waiting for memory starts at the next tick once the reading shows it.
- **Applied** (`recordWaitReleases`, in the Decision's transaction): the job stays `waiting_on`, marked `waitReleased: { at,
  machineId }`, and `job.wait_released { reason }` (with its `machineId`). After the commit (`releaseWait`) its executor ends
  its pane and agent on the Park button's path (`Executor.park`, its scratch dir kept) and its checkpoint is taken
  (`releaseParked`), as auto-park does.
- **While it waits.** What it waits on, its wait check, a comment, the hopper's answer or a person's End the wait still end
  the wait as before. The pane probes skip it (`src/engine/pane-answers.ts`): it has no pane, its old pane id may name
  another job's, and it is not taken for a stranded or lost-pane wait. Its job end reaps only, as a parked job's
  (`cleanup`), and the lost-machine move does not take its old pane for its live one (`pane-left.ts`).
- **Its resume.** Woken, it is queued with what it is told pending, pinned to its machine, and admitted by the memory floor as
  any job resuming. herdr-claude reopens it as a parked job (`reopen`): what is left of it is reaped, a new pane opens in its
  work tree, Claude resumes its agent session, told `RELEASED_NOTE` (`src/executors/herdr/restored.ts`) and then the note. Its
  run's outcome clears `waitReleased`.
- **Nothing running, a job waiting for memory** is stuck work: the cause `memory_starved` ("Jobs that wait for memory while no
  job runs", `src/domain/stuck.ts`), first among the causes with no bulk action in Failures, with what a person does (free
  memory, or lower the machine's `memoryFloorGiB` or `memoryPerJobGiB`). It shows while a queued job's wait reason is a
  memory wait and no job is claimed or running.
- **UI.** The Dashboard's wait row says "waiting: agent ended to free memory", with End the wait.
- **The estimate.** The 3.8 GiB in the report is the job's expected memory peak, not the 2 GiB default: placement by expected
  cost ("Job cost profiles") takes each run's highest sample of the machine's memory used over its idle baseline (samples with
  no busy lane), split over the busy lanes, and the group's mean of those peaks. Memory of jobs on their own wait holds no
  lane, so a waiting agent that started after the baseline counts as the running job's: with 50 agents resident, the expected
  peaks grew with them. With waits released while a job waits for memory, that share falls away; what their scopes still
  hold is left out since issue #2499 (waiting memory). The floor of 1.4 GiB is 10%
  of the 14 GiB VM, as set. Not changed here: the expected peak still counts when it is more than the job's memory.
- **Not built.** A count of each agent's memory. (Releasing a wait before a job waits for memory: issue #2326, below.)
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `waitReleased` is in the job's JSON, `waitSessions` and `waitRelease` in the
  Decision's. A build before this ignores them: a released job's wait ends as a lost pane's does (issue #1508), or it is
  marked stranded, and its resume opens a new pane (`resumeLostPane`).

Verification: `test/decider/memory-floor.test.ts` (the oldest first, only on a machine a job waits for memory on, none while
every job fits), `test/domain/stuck.test.ts` (`memory_starved` only while nothing runs), `test/ui/job-wait-view.test.ts`, and
`test/integration/wait-release.test.ts` (the real daemon over the fake herdr: a job on a vault-grant wait, the memory short,
a new job queued; the wait is released and its pane closed, not stranded, Failures shows `memory_starved`; the memory back,
the new job finishes; End the wait resumes the first job's own session in a new pane with `RELEASED_NOTE`, and it finishes).

### Every wait released, and its wake on any machine (issue #2326, 2026-10-21)

Reported from a real run of the release above: 45 jobs on their own wait still held 34 resident Claude processes with
nothing queued, as the release ran only while a job waited for memory. The owner's direction: a waiting job is parked at
once, the wait check wakes it, and it does not need to start again on the machine it came from.

- **Every wait, at once.** `waitReleases` (`src/decider/memory-floor.ts`) names every job of `waitSessions`, on every
  machine, the oldest wait first, once its wait is 5 seconds old (`WAIT_RELEASE_AFTER_MS`), whether or not a job waits for
  memory. Step 7 no longer gives `memoryShort`. The 5 seconds spare a park and a restore to a wait the hopper answers at
  once (a request of the job, issue #998), and let a wait whose agent ended at once be seen as stranded (issue #1779) first. Which waits stay is as before: one only its pane carries (its own command, a background
  poll) keeps its agent. With nothing queued, the steady state is no agent for any wait the hopper ends by itself. A stranded
  wait is not released: its agent ended already.
- **Its checkpoint, marked.** After the commit, `releaseWait` (`src/engine/wait-release.ts`) ends the pane and agent
  (`Executor.park`), then takes its checkpoint and waits for it. A checkpoint that holds the agent session is marked on the
  job: `waitReleased.checkpointAt`. A checkpoint the same as the last one (issue #1975) is the last one, and is marked so.
- **Its wake, on any machine.** `recordEndWait` (`src/engine/wait.ts`), the one path every wake takes (the event that
  settles what it waits on, its wait check, a comment, the hopper's answer, a person's End the wait), queues a released job
  whose marked checkpoint is still its checkpoint, with its agent session and no machine pin of its spec, as picked up to
  resume elsewhere (issue #921): `parked: { from: 'waiting_answer', auto, why, elsewhere: { checkpointAt, from } }`,
  `resumeOn` and `waitReleased` cleared. Admission control places it on any machine with room; herdr-claude restores the
  checkpoint in a new job worktree there (`relocate`, with the #2316 restore that needs the job's way to the hopper first)
  and resumes the same session, told `WAIT_RELEASED_NOTE`, then that it moved (`elsewhereBrief`), then the wake's note. A
  released job woken before its checkpoint was marked resumes on its own machine as before (`RELEASED_NOTE`); the
  busy-machine move may still take it elsewhere.
- **UI.** The Dashboard's wait row says `parked (waiting on <what it waits on>)`, with End the wait.
- **Not built.** A job parked on a question (the Park button, auto-park) keeps its pin to its machine; the busy-machine move
  and a person's pick up elsewhere still move it. A wait that ends a few seconds after it began is released all the same.
  (A job on a question: issue #2335, below.)
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `waitReleased.checkpointAt` is in the job's JSON. A build before this reads a woken
  job as one picked up to resume elsewhere, as after a busy-machine move.

Verification: `test/decider/memory-floor.test.ts` (every wait released, on every machine, with nothing queued, none less than
5 seconds old),
`test/ui/job-wait-view.test.ts`, and `test/integration/wait-release.test.ts` (two machines over the fake herdr: a job on a
vault-grant wait with nothing queued has its pane closed and its checkpoint marked; its machine drained, End the wait
resumes it on the other machine from its checkpoint, with the same session and `WAIT_RELEASED_NOTE`).

### Every job that waits on a person parked, and its pick up on any machine (issue #2335 part 1, 2026-10-21)

Follow-up to issue #2326: a job on a question, or on its proposal or research report, still kept its agent, its pane and
its pin to its machine while a person had not answered; auto-park parked it only after a timeout (30 minutes by default). The
owner's direction: a waiting job never stays a live Claude session; a hopper-side check, not the pane, wakes it, and it
resumes from its checkpoint on any machine.

- **Every job on a person, parked.** Auto-park (`src/engine/auto-park.ts`) parks a `waiting_answer` job, on the Park button's
  path, `WAIT_RELEASE_AFTER_MS` (5 seconds) after its question reached a person (`escalatedToHumanAt`), or after it began to
  wait on one again (`waitRestartedAt`, issue #692); a job on its proposal or research report as long after that item reached
  the human stage (its newest version, or a level's last review). A question a risk rule or the consequential guard sent to a person (`keptBy`) parks too. `why`: `AUTO_PARK_WHY`. A
  question on the issue thread parks at once, as before. Still not parked by it: a job with no agent session (issue #530),
  and one a fork of its question still works for (issue #548). Time at the escalation levels does not count, as before: a
  level answers with no agent of the job's.
- **No setting.** The park timeout is gone: `GET /api/auto-park`, `POST /ui/api/auto-park`, Settings → Auto-park and
  `hopper auto-park` are removed. A stored `autoPark` setting is no longer read; `auto_park.settings_changed` stays a known
  event for the ones recorded, and is no longer written.
- **The item stays in review.** A job auto-park parked on its proposal or research report sets nothing aside (`parkedItemOf`
  is only a person's park, issue #2167): the item stays in its section, levels review it, and a person decides it. Its decision
  or a send back picks the job up (`requeue` in `src/engine/reviews.ts` → `recordUnpark`), as the answer to a question does.
- **Its checkpoint, marked.** `releaseParked` (`src/engine/park.ts`) still takes the checkpoint after the executor ended the
  agent; a checkpoint with the session is now marked on the park (`parked.checkpointAt`), for every park — a person's,
  auto-park's, a preemption, a memory pause, a budget pause.
- **Its pick up, on any machine.** `recordUnpark` queues a parked job whose marked checkpoint is still its checkpoint, with
  its agent session and no machine pin of its spec, as picked up to resume elsewhere (issue #921, `recordElsewhere`):
  `resumeOn` cleared, `parked.elsewhere` set, `job.unparked` `{ to: 'queued', elsewhere: true }`. Every pick up takes it: the
  answer, the decision, a person's Pick up, a preempted or memory-paused job's re-queue. Admission control places it on any
  machine with room; herdr-claude restores the checkpoint there (`relocate`) and resumes the same session. A job parked
  before its checkpoint is marked resumes on its own machine, as before.
- **A pane that ended is no pane.** A job on its own wait whose agent was released (`waitReleased`), or a job picked up with
  its question still open after a park (`waiting_answer` with `parked`), holds no pane: its pane id may name another job's
  pane by now. `holdsPane` (`src/engine/terminal.ts`) says so, so the job's terminal and the machine terminal's job of a pane
  refuse it (`no_pane`, 409). A park of a job picked up with its question open (auto-park, or the Park button) asks no
  executor to end its pane (`releaseParked` with `paneless`): it has none.
- **Lanes.** A parked or waiting job holds no lane in the store already (its `laneId` is cleared when it parks or waits); its
  `executorState` keeps the lane and pane of its last run as the record of where its work tree is, which the sweep and the
  cleanup read (`machineRanOn`). Its next run on any machine replaces it.
- **The checkpoint on every machine.** The checkpoint is kept in the user's schema (`job_checkpoints`, issue #921): the session
  file, the patch from a commit the remote has, and the commits not pushed (as uncommitted changes when it is restored). No
  machine but the one that restores it needs to be reached.
- **Not built (later parts).** A wait only its pane carries — a job's own command, a background poll for what the hopper
  watches nothing of — still keeps its agent (issue #2335 gap 2): a hopper-side check of the condition (a command exit
  recorded by the hopper, a time) replaces the pane's poll. A parent of a fork (`forkParent: wait`) keeps its agent while the
  fork runs. (Both: part 2, below.)
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `parked.checkpointAt` is in the job's JSON. A build before this reads a parked job
  with it as before, and pins its pick up to its machine. A stored `autoPark` setting row stays, unread.

Verification: `test/integration/auto-park.test.ts` (a question parks its job 5 s after it reached a person; a risk-rule
question too; a job on its proposal parks 5 s after it reached the human stage, stays in Proposals and its send back resumes its session; on two
machines over the fake herdr, the answer resumes a parked job on the other machine from the checkpoint marked on its park,
with the same session, and its terminal is refused while it is parked), `test/integration/wait-release.test.ts` (a released
wait's terminal is refused), `test/integration/thread-ask.test.ts` (parked for its thread question, its pick up is refused:
issue #2415 below).

### Part 2: a wait the pane carried, rechecked by the hopper; a fork's parent parked (issue #2335, 2026-10-21)

Gap 2 of issue #2335: a job on its own wait on an outside event the hopper watches nothing of (no item, no run, no time
named) kept its agent and its pane, as only a background poll in its pane could end the wait (issue #1508). The owner's
direction: a hopper-side deterministic check, not a pane-side poll, wakes the job; only a truly running build or test of the
job keeps its session.

- **The recheck** (`recheck`, `conditionOf` in `src/domain/wait-checks.ts`). Such a wait (an `outside` wait, or one with
  nothing recorded, that names nothing `watchedOf` reads) gets the condition `recheck { at }`: the check-in the job named on
  its `check:` line (`in 20m`, kept to 1..30 minutes), else `RECHECK_MS` (30 minutes) after the wait began. A time the job
  named (`check: after|at`) stays `time_passed`; an approval, a grant or a plan stays `none` (the event that settles it wakes
  the job). The check is first tested at that time, not before. Met (`recheckOutcome`), the wait ends (`job.wait_ended
  { by: hopper, check: 'recheck:<at>' }`) and the job is told that the hopper cannot see what it waits on, to look again, and
  to end with `HOPPER_WAITING` again if it did not happen yet — naming what the hopper can check where it can.
- **Every wait released but its own command.** `waitSessionsOf` (`src/engine/wait-release.ts`) names every job on its own
  wait whose condition is not `command_exited`: an outside wait with a recheck is released 5 seconds after it began, as every
  other wait (issue #2326), its pane and agent ended, its checkpoint marked; its recheck, or any other wake, resumes it on any
  machine. A wait on its own command (`own command`, `until: own command <id> ends`) keeps its agent: the command is a build
  or a test run of the job that runs in its pane. The memory floor's `waitSessions` input reads the same list.
- **The wait rule** (`WAIT_LINE`, the job rules' protocol): it no longer asks for a background poll. It says the session ends
  while the job waits (but on its own command), that a command left in the background ends with it, so never to start a poll,
  and to name `on:` what the hopper can check; for an outside event the hopper cannot see, it wakes the job after 30 minutes,
  or at its `check:` time.
- **A fork's parent parks.** `forkJob` (`src/engine/phase-shifts.ts`) parks the parent at the fork, where its executor can
  park, and its checkpoint is marked (part 1), so the fork's result resumes it on any machine. Auto-park no longer skips a job
  a fork of its question works for. The `forkParent` phase-shift setting is gone (`GET /api/phase-shifts`,
  `POST /ui/api/phase-shifts`, the Questions settings form): a stored value is not read; a recorded
  `phase_shifts.settings_changed` with it stays valid (`forkParent` optional in its schema).
- **UI.** The job card's wait check says `the hopper cannot see it: it wakes the job at <time> to look again`.
- **What stays.** A wait on its own command keeps its agent, as the issue allows. A wait that ends a few seconds after it
  began is released all the same (part 1). Gap 5 needs no change (part 1).
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `recheck` is a new condition kind in the job's JSON (`wait.check`). A build before
  this cannot test it: its sweeper logs that the check failed and tries again at the next pass, so the wait ends by its other
  wakes (a comment, a person's End the wait). A stored `phaseShifts` row with `forkParent` is read without it.

**Decisions:**
- **A recheck wakes the model, not a model-free poll of the outside.** The hopper cannot read what the job waits on, so only
  the job can look. 30 minutes is the longest time between checks (`MAX_EVERY_MS`); a job that wants it sooner names
  `check: in <time>`.
- **Own command keeps its session.** The issue names a running build or test of the job as the one exception.
- **No `forkParent` setting.** With every waiting job parked, `wait` would be a dead control (repository rule: no backwards
  compatibility for contracts).

Verification: `test/engine/wait-sessions.test.ts` (each wait type released but its own command),
`test/domain/wait-checks.test.ts` and `test/engine/wait-checks.test.ts` (the recheck: its time, its check-in, another hopper
ends it at its time and the job is told to look again), `test/ui/board.test.ts`, `test/integration/wait-release.test.ts`
(two machines over the fake herdr: an outside wait naming nothing has its pane closed and no lane, its checkpoint marked; at
its recheck it resumes on the other machine with the same session, told to look again), `test/integration/auto-park.test.ts`
(a fork's parent parks at the fork and its pane closes), `test/integration/phase-shifts.test.ts`, `test/ui/phase-shifts.test.ts`.

### An outside wait with no check stays parked until a person ends it (issue #2338, 2026-10-21)

Follow-up to issue #2326 and part 2 of issue #2335. Waits on an outside event the hopper watches nothing of —
`outside: gated: <what>`, `outside: not managed: <what>`, `outside: <what>` (reason not given), or a wait with nothing
recorded — still kept a live agent: `paneCarriesWait` was true for them, so the pane was their only watch, and a lost pane
woke them. An agent ended by hand resumed a minute later in a new, larger agent that waited again, which burned tokens.
Part 2 of issue #2335 released them, but its 30-minute recheck woke the agent again and again for an event only a person
settles. The owner's scope: such a job ends with no agent, no pane and no lane; it stays parked until End the wait (or an
item or a time it named); a lost pane does not wake it; after End the wait it resumes its own session on any eligible
machine.

- **No recheck unless the job asks.** `conditionOf` (`src/domain/wait-checks.ts`) gives such a wait `recheck { at }` only
  when the job named a check-in (`check: in <time>`); a time it named (`check: after|at`) stays `time_passed`, and items it
  names stay `items_ended`. Else its condition is `none`: the wait check wakes nothing, and past its deadline it is overdue
  once, so a person is told. `RECHECK_MS` is gone.
- **The pane carries only its own command.** `paneCarriesWait` (`src/domain/watched-items.ts`) is true only for a wait on
  the job's own command. A lost pane of an outside wait in the seconds before its release is marked stranded (issue #1779),
  never ended: a person or what it names wakes it.
- **Released as every other wait.** Its condition is not `command_exited`, so `waitSessionsOf` releases it 5 seconds after it
  began (issue #2326): its pane and agent end, it holds no lane, its checkpoint is marked, and its wake resumes it on any
  machine.
- **The wait rule** (`WAIT_LINE`) says that for an outside event the hopper cannot see, only a person who ends the wait, or
  the time its `check:` line names, wakes the job, so a job that waits on an event that ends by itself names a `check:` line.
- **Persisted state.** No schema change. A wait stored with a `recheck` condition keeps it until its check ends it.

**Decisions:**
- **Every outside wait that names nothing, not only gated ones.** The issue names `outside (gated)` and `outside (reason not
  given)`; the owner's scope says every outside wait with no check. `not managed` is a person's act too.
- **A check-in the job named keeps the recheck.** The issue asks to encourage jobs to name an item or a time so a check can
  watch them; the wait rule says so, and a job that names `check: in <time>` is woken to look again.

Verification: `test/domain/wait-checks.test.ts` (condition `none` for gated, not managed, reason not given and nothing
recorded; a recheck only at a check-in), `test/domain/watched-items.test.ts` (`paneCarriesWait` only for its own command),
`test/engine/wait-sessions.test.ts` (gated and not managed waits released), `test/engine/wait-checks.test.ts`,
`test/integration/job-wait.test.ts` (an outside wait's lost pane does not wake it; End the wait does),
`test/integration/wait-release.test.ts` (two machines over the fake herdr: a gated wait has its pane closed, no lane, its
checkpoint marked and condition `none`; after End the wait it resumes on the other machine with the same session).

### A long check-in, and a pushed head at resume (issue #2459, 2026-10-22)

A job waited on `outside: gated: <what>` with `check: in 12h`, and the hopper woke it every 30 to 60 minutes, on a new
machine each time. `checkAskOf` kept a check-in to 1..30 minutes (`MAX_EVERY_MS`), so the recheck of issue #2335 came 30
minutes after the wait began. One resume also told the job that a pushed commit was not pushed, and put the tree at the
default branch with that commit as uncommitted changes. The owner's scope: a recheck is not before the check-in's time
unless a person ends the wait or its check fires; a resume of a head the remote holds stays on the job's branch.

- **The check-in, kept to a week.** `checkAskOf` keeps `in <time>` and `every <time>` to a minute..a week
  (`MAX_WAKE_MS`). A recheck (`conditionOf`) is at that time, and its deadline is an hour after it at least (`newCheck`). A
  wait the hopper can test still starts its checks at most `MAX_EVERY_MS` apart: `newCheck` caps `everyMs` and the first
  check, as before.
- **The pushed head, from the push records.** The checkpoint script finds the pushed branch from the worktree's remote
  branches; a push through the hopper need not move them. The hopper records each push's refs and heads (issue #2087), so
  a checkpoint whose head is not its base reads the job's pushes (`pushedBranchOf`, `src/domain/kept-work.ts`) and keeps
  `pushedTo`, the branch a push moved to its head (the job's own branch first, else the newest push's).
- **The restore at the head.** With `pushedTo`, the restore (`src/client/checkpoint.ts`) gets that branch and the head
  (`$5`). It checks out the base and applies the patch as before, then fetches the head if it is not here and moves the
  branch to it with `git reset` (the work tree stays): only the work not committed then is uncommitted. A file the patch
  left out (issue #2428) takes the head's content. A head it cannot get is said on stderr, and the work stays as before.
- **What the job is told.** `elsewhereBrief` names the head on its branch, "which the remote holds", and lists no
  commits as not pushed.
- **Persisted state.** No schema change: `checkpoint.pushedTo` is an optional field in the job's JSON; a build before
  ignores it and restores as before.

**Decisions:**
- **The push records, not a fetch in the checkpoint.** The checkpoint script never fetches (it runs often, on the job's
  machine); the hopper already knows what it pushed.
- **Only the head.** A checkpoint whose head the hopper did not push (commits after the last push) restores as before.

Verification: `test/domain/wait-checks.test.ts` (a check-in of 12 hours and 3 days; a testable wait still checked at 30
minutes), `test/engine/wait-recheck.test.ts` (two hoppers sweep a gated wait every 15 minutes for 12 hours: no wake-up,
then one at its time), `test/domain/kept-work.test.ts` (`pushedBranchOf`), `test/client/checkpoint-pushed.test.ts` (real
git: a pushed head with no remote branch restores on the branch at it, with only the work not committed uncommitted),
`test/integration/checkpoint.test.ts` (a pushed head: `pushedTo`, the restore command, the job told the remote holds it).

### No pick up of a job auto-parked on a person (issue #2415, 2026-10-21)

Pick up on a job auto-park parked on a person had no lasting effect: the job went back to `waiting_answer` on the same
open question, proposal or research report, and auto-park parked it again within seconds. The person saw a button that
did nothing, and could press it again and again.

- **What waits on a person** (`personWaitOf`, `src/engine/park.ts`): the job's open question at the human stage, else its
  open proposal or research report at the human stage. A question or an item still with a reviewer level is not: picked
  up, its level goes on.
- **Refused.** `recordUnpark` refuses (409) a job whose park is auto-park's (`parked.auto`), that waits on a person and has
  no answer kept: picked up, it would only park again. The answer to its question, or the decision on its item, picks it
  up, as before. A question on the issue thread (issue #435) is the same: a reply there picks it up.
- **A person's park still picks up.** A job a person parked on a person goes back to its question or item, as before, and
  auto-park parks it again a few seconds later; then its pick up is refused. For an item this puts it back in its section
  to be decided (issue #2167); for a question, the answer picks it up after that. An answer kept while it was parked
  (`pendingAnswer`) picks it up as always.
- **The UI.** The same rule, pure (`ui/src/model/auto-park.ts`: `personWait`, `pickUpRefused`). Pick up is not shown for
  such a job, wherever parked jobs are listed. Its Parked row says what it waits on and what picks it up: Answer opens the
  answer form; for a proposal or a research report, Decide opens its card inline, and a link opens its section. A job a
  person parked on a person keeps Pick up, and the button and the row say that it parks again until the answer comes.
- **Persisted state.** No change.

Verification: `test/integration/auto-park.test.ts` (parked by a person, picked up, it parks again by itself; then its pick
up is 409, it stays parked with one `job.unparked`, and the answer resumes it; a job auto-parked on its proposal: 409),
`test/integration/thread-ask.test.ts`, `test/ui/auto-park.test.ts`, `test/ui/parked-view.test.ts`.

### The heavy-step gate (issue #2622 parts 3, 4, 5, 2026-10-23)

Admission counts a lane's memory when the lane opens. On one WSL VM (14 GB) lanes were admitted while their agents were
light, about 0.4 GB each; within 2 minutes four of them started a JVM build, each up to ~5 GB, and the VM ran out of
memory. Nothing gated the build itself. Now a **heavy step** asks first.

- **What is a heavy step** (`heavyKindOf`, `src/domain/heavy-steps.ts`): a JVM build (`gradle`, `gradlew`, `mvn`,
  `mvnw`, but not only `--version` or `--help`), a package install (`npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn` `install`, `i`, `ci`, `add`; a bare
  `yarn`), a Playwright browser install or test run (`playwright install|test`, `npx … playwright install|test`), an image
  build (`podman`/`docker` `build`, `buildx`, `image build`). Each kind keeps at most `HEAVY_STEP_GIB`: a build 3 GiB
  (under the build defaults), an install 1 GiB, a browser run or an image build 2 GiB.
- **How a job asks** (`src/github-proxy/heavy-script.ts`): `sh "$HOPPER_HEAVY" <command>`, in the job's credentials dir
  beside its proxy token, asks `POST /job/heavy` (`op: take`, the command and its first arguments). Its answer is a slot
  (run, and renew it every 10 s), a wait (ask again in 5 s; the client prints why, once per reason), or light (run with no
  slot). When the command ends, the client lets the slot go (`op: release`); its exit code is the command's. A hopper it
  cannot ask, or one that says no, never stops the command: it runs, and the client says so. Inside a heavy step
  (`HOPPER_HEAVY_HELD`) a heavy command runs as it is: it holds its step's slot already.
- **The shims.** The guards step (`src/client/job-runtime.ts`) writes a shim for each of `gradle`, `gradlew`, `mvn`,
  `mvnw`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `npx` and `playwright` beside the podman and docker guards, first on the job's PATH; each
  runs the real command further on PATH, through the gate when its first words may make it heavy. The podman and docker
  guards send a `build` or `buildx` through the gate too. `./gradlew` is a path, not a name on PATH: the protocol line
  `[hopper heavy steps]` (`HEAVY_STEPS_LINE`) tells every job to run it as `sh "$HOPPER_HEAVY" ./gradlew …`. The shims
  still fit the guards step's terminal line (4095 characters).
- **The rule** (`heavyAdmits`, `src/decider/heavy-steps.ts`, pure). The step's host is its machine, or the **host pool**
  its machine shares a kernel with (the kernel's memory, and Windows' free memory when one machine reads that lower). A JVM
  build waits while the host runs as many as its memory less its floor holds at 5 GiB each (`BUILD_WORST_GIB`), at least
  one: 2 on a 14 GiB VM. The first heavy step on a host always runs. Any other waits while the memory available, less what
  the heavy steps of the last 2 minutes keep (`HEAVY_RAMP_MS`: the reading does not show them yet) and its own need, is
  under the floor. The wait says which: `local runs 2 JVM builds, and holds at most 2 at once: 14 GiB less its floor of
  1.4 GiB, at up to 5 GiB a build`. A machine with no memory reading, or its memory floor off, has no gate.
- **The slots** (`src/engine/heavy-gate.ts`): one gate per user, in memory, each slot on a 60 s lease the client renews;
  a job that stopped renewing (it died, its machine went away) holds no slot after its lease. Only the job that took a slot
  renews or lets it go. The route records nothing and changes no job, question, webhook or setting.

- **Demand from history** (part 4, `heavyNeedOf`). A step's need is what its repository's recent jobs took at their peak:
  the most of the `memoryPeakBytes` that `job.resources_used` recorded (each job's scope's `memory.peak` at its reap) for
  the last 10 jobs of its repository (`HEAVY_HISTORY_JOBS`, the job's `source.repo`, in any case) in the last 30 days
  (`HEAVY_HISTORY_DAYS`). So a 3 GiB history reserves 3 GiB, for the 2 minutes the reading does not show the step yet, and
  in the step's own need. With no peak recorded, or a history that cannot be read, the need is its kind's estimate
  (`HEAVY_STEP_GIB`). The read goes through the read pool (`memoryPeaks`, `src/store/events.ts`), before the gate looks at
  its slots: the gate does not wait between its look and its new slot. The wait names the recorded peak: `and this step
  needs 6 GiB (its repository's recorded peak) over its floor of 1.4 GiB`. A job's peak holds its agent too (about 0.4
  GiB): the reserve is a little high, never low. The JVM build cap stays at 5 GiB a build.

- **The shed on memory pressure** (part 5, `heavyPressure`, `heavyShed`, pure). A host is under pressure when it has less
  than 2 GiB available (`HEAVY_SHED_AVAILABLE_GIB`; a quarter of its memory on a host of less than 8 GiB), when its tasks
  waited on memory over 10% of the last 60 s (PSI `some avg60`, `MEMORY_PRESSURE_60_PERCENT`), or when its swap is over 50%
  used (`HEAVY_SHED_SWAP_PERCENT`) while some task waits on memory (`some avg60` 1% or more): Linux reads swapped memory back
  only when it is used, so swap alone stays full after a burst and would hold every step for good. On a host pool each
  signal is the most of its machines'. Under pressure no heavy step starts, not even the first: `local is under memory
  pressure: its tasks waited on memory 25% of the last 60 s, over 10%; a heavy step starts when it clears`. At each renew
  the gate reads the host again: the newest step that runs is **paused**, never the last one that runs, so the oldest goes on
  and frees its memory; while the pressure lasts, one more each 30 s (`HEAVY_SHED_EVERY_MS`). The renew's answer says
  `pause` and why; the client stops the command's process group (SIGSTOP: it runs the command in a group of its own, so a
  build's JVM stops too, not only its wrapper), keeps renewing its slot, and prints why. When the pressure clears, the paused
  step that started first runs again (SIGCONT, at the first renew with no `pause`), one each 30 s; while one is paused no new
  step starts. The client renews every 10 s, so a pause reaches the newest step within 30 s of a reading that shows the
  pressure. A paused step keeps its memory: a pause stops the growth, and the oldest step's end frees memory.
- **Job admission** (part 5): a machine whose `some avg60` is over 10% takes no new job either (`memoryShort`,
  `src/decider/memory-floor.ts`), beside the `some avg10` at 20% of issue #2499. The readings carry `someAvg60`: the client's
  meter and an ssh target's probe parse it from the same PSI line.

- **Host signals** (part 6). Windows' own free memory was already in admission (issue #868: a WSL machine's memory
  available is at most Windows' free memory, `src/decider/memory-floor.ts`), and in the heavy-step host. Guest
  allocation-failure bursts are a machine alert now: "The allocation failure watch" below.

- **The pool's job limit** (part 7). A job's default memory limit is shared by every lane of its host pool, not only its
  machine's: "The job's scope" above.
- **The slots on the Machines page** (part 7). The gate also keeps, in memory, each job's step that waits, while its job
  asks again (within 15 s, `HEAVY_WAIT_SEEN_MS`; it asks every 5 s), since its first ask. `GET /api/machines` gives each
  machine its `heavySteps` (`HeavyStepView`, `src/domain/heavy-steps.ts`): the steps that hold a slot, then those that
  wait, each with its job, kind, command, since when, the memory it keeps, `paused` or `waiting`, and why. A machine's
  card lists them, one line each (`heavyStepLines`, `ui/src/model/machine-list.ts`): `job j3 waits to run gradlew build
