  the hopper first saw the failure, never older than the base the tend job saw. Another commit later marks the base moved
  (`tended.baseMoved`).
- `tendRetryAt` makes the same `rebase` due from `baseMoved` (`rebasesWhenBaseMoves`): a tend job of the item, the brief
  as before, the tend note on the pull request, `retries` one more. At most `MAX_TEND_RETRIES` (3) in a row, the same count
  as a cancel's retries; a person's Tend again starts a new row. After that, it waits on a person.
- The card says it: while the base is watched, its "gave up" line ends "the hopper rebases it again when its base branch
  moves"; once moved, it waits "its base branch moved since its rebase failed".
- A source with no mirror, or outside a pass, says no commit: the pull request waits on a person, as before. A throw is
  only logged.
- **The tend of a job, at any distance** (`tendOf`). A tend run again keeps `tended` on the job it tended, not on the tend
  job before it. So `failedTend` and the tending queue's head (`tending`) look up the whole chain of runs again. Before,
  a failed retry was taken as no tend: reconciling followed its pull request again and tended it at once, past the cap.

**Part 4: strays.** A **stray pull request** is an open pull request a job named in its source state that no job
follows, of an item no job works on: every job of the item ended (`strayPullRequests`, pure). A tend whose tend job failed
or was cancelled leaves one, as do a cancelled or rejected newer job of the item and a rework that ended with none. Before,
only the batch runner's move from the tested branch reached it.

- In a round of every follow (the reconcile interval), after reconciling, the sync loop gives the source its strays, each
  held by the newest job that names it, once that job's end is reported (`JobSource.housekeepStrays`). The source reads the
  open pull requests of their repositories in one batch (`openPullRequestsIn`, as reconciling does). One not open is read
  once by its number (issue #1420): merged or closed without a merge on GitHub, it has **ended** (`ended`); open after all
  (a repository with more open pull requests than one read lists), it is left. For each open one: its item closed as not planned, it is left as it is (as an abandoned follow leaves it); else it is
  closed as superseded by the pull request that closed its issue (never a part), or gets the follow's housekeeping
  (`housekeep` in `follow.ts`, shared with the follow): moved to the landing branch, or closed with its changes on its base.
  Each act says so on the pull request, with the same notes.
- What the source did is recorded on the job that holds it, with `stray: true`: `job.pull_request_retargeted`, or
  `job.pull_request_closed` with `superseded`, and that job's `follow: closed`, so it is a stray no more. One that ended on
  GitHub (issue #1420) is recorded as it ended: `job.pull_request_closed` with no `superseded`, or
  `job.pull_request_merged`, and that job's `follow: closed` or `follow: merged`. Before, a stray closed on GitHub was left
  as it was: the job that holds it kept `follow: tended`, and the job graph, which counts a tended pull request as open,
  showed it open, with merge conflicts and tended, for ever, while Rework said the job follows no open pull request. Now
  both read the one `follow`, and a stray that ended before is corrected at the first round of every follow after a start.
- **A stray's close moves no work item.** No job followed it, so its close ends no wait of its item: a hand-off stays a
  hand-off. Only the item's own pull request's state is marked closed — or merged, for a stray merged on GitHub.
- **A stray is never tended.** Each way to a stray is a decision that stands: a person cancelled or rejected the newer job,
  the hopper gave up after a failed tend (part 3 retries a rebase once its base moves), or the cap of retries was used.
  Tending it again would undo that. A person's Tend again, or Run again, still works.
- A source that is paused does nothing; a repository GitHub does not answer for, or a stray whose housekeeping throws, is
  logged and asked again at the next round.

**Not done, by decision: "behind" with no merge conflicts.** With merge commits, a pull request behind its base merges as
it is, and the landing batch tests it on top of the tip. A repository that requires branches up to date before a merge
refuses the merge, and the card shows it (`mergeError`). Rebasing every pull request at each move of the base would spend
a lane and a check run on each, for no change in what lands.

Tests: `test/sources/github-pr-housekeeping.test.ts` (retarget, a stack, no landing branch known, after the batch,
superseded both ways, a part), `test/integration/pull-request-housekeeping.test.ts` (the events and the comments over the
real daemon, and a rebase held an hour), `test/landing-batches/runner.test.ts` (the batch runner's move and its note),
`test/store/jobs-lanes.test.ts` (`namesPullRequest`), `test/domain/stray-pull-requests.test.ts` (part 4: which pull
requests are strays, and which job holds each), `test/domain/work-items.test.ts` (a stray's close or merge moves no item), the strays
in `test/integration/pull-request-housekeeping.test.ts` (with issue #1420's: closed or merged on GitHub, and the job graph and
Rework agree), `test/integration/pull-request-retend.test.ts` (part 3: a failed
rebase tended again once its base moves, at most three in a row; no mirror, no retry), `test/domain/tend-retries.test.ts`
(`tendOf`, `tendRetryAt` with a moved base), `test/git-mirror/mirrors.test.ts` (`baseTip`).

## Untracked pull requests (issue #1176, 2026-10-14)

**The problem.** Two open pull requests sat with merge conflicts, and nothing rebased, landed or closed them, because the
ledger did not know them. One closed an issue with no hopper label and no assignee: Intake never took the issue, so the pull
request had no work item. The other was "Part of" an issue the ledger tracks, but its base was `dev`, the base from before
job pull requests moved to the landing branch, and no job named it: the item's jobs followed other pull requests on `main`.
Nothing showed either one.

**The census** (`src/sources/census.ts`, the sync loop's half; `src/sources/github/census.ts`, the source's). In a round of
every follow (the reconcile interval), after reconciling and the strays, the sync loop asks the source for a census
(`JobSource.censusPullRequests`), at most once an hour for each source (`CENSUS_EVERY_MS`), and at once on a sync a person
asked for or a start. It reads every job repository, and an untracked pull request changes slowly: at each round it would
spend more of GitHub's budget than intake, reconciling and the in-motion cycle together (`test/integration/github-budget.test.ts`). The source reads the open pull
requests of every job repository it scanned in one batch (`openPullRequestsIn`, the read reconciling makes, now with each
one's base and title), and keeps the **untracked pull requests** in memory, shown in its status (`detail.untrackedPullRequests`)
and in the Pull requests view's **Not tracked** list (`GET /api/pull-requests` `untracked`). A repository GitHub does not
answer for keeps what was last read of it (`detail.untrackedErrors`). Not while the source is paused.

**Tracked.** A pull request is tracked when a job of the source names it in its source state, or the ledger holds it as an
item's pull request (`WorkItemLedger.byPullRequest`). Every other open pull request is untracked, with one reason
(`untrackedPullRequests`, pure, in this order):

- `no_issue`: its text closes no issue of its repository and is part of none (`issueOfPullRequest`: a closing keyword
  first, then "Part of #N").
- `issue_not_in_intake`: its issue is no work item — no job of the source has it, and the ledger has no item of it (a
  request card is one). The UI says what takes it in: the hopper label and an assignee.
- `wrong_base`: its issue is a work item, the repository has landing batches, and its base is not the landing branch and is
  no other open pull request's head (a stack).
- `second_pull_request` (part 2): its issue is a work item, and a job of the item follows another pull request
  (`followed`, `CensusFacts.followedOf`, from the jobs of the source that follow one). One item, two pull requests: the
  hopper tends only the one its job follows. The UI says which one, and to close one of them.
- `not_by_a_job`: its issue is a work item, and no job of it made it or follows it — a person's, a second one, or one moved to
  the landing branch that no job follows yet.

**Attached.** Reconciling (issue #763) runs first in the same round: an item whose newest job ended and follows no pull request
is given its open pull request, whatever its base, and the follow's housekeeping moves it to the landing branch. So a pull
request the census lists as untracked is one reconciling cannot give to a job.

**Moved.** One `wrong_base` on a branch named for its issue (`namesIssue`, the branches jobs make) is moved to the landing
branch (`GitHubApi.retarget`), with the follow's fixed note (`retargetNote`), and listed as `not_by_a_job` with `retargeted`.
One on any other branch is a person's: it is listed, never moved. A move GitHub refuses is logged and tried at the next round.
No event: no job holds it.

**Take into Intake** (part 2). An untracked pull request whose issue is not in Intake carries `offer: take_in`, and the Not
tracked list (`GET /api/pull-requests` `untracked`, each with its `source`) shows Take into Intake for an operator. It is the
source's intake action `take_in` (`POST /ui/api/sources/:name/intake`, a box action as every intake action): only on an issue
the last census offers so (`takeIn`, else `not offered: no untracked pull request closes it`), the source gives the issue its
label and assigns it to the connected account, records `source.issue_taken_in { source, key, pullRequest, assignee }`, and
syncs at once. The assignment counts as the user's act, as Assign to me does (`assignedHere`). The label is the hopper's
app's act, so Intake lists the issue as a request card: a person approves its text before a job runs it, whoever wrote it.
Then its pull request is `not_by_a_job`; the job the approval starts makes its own.

**A second pull request with merge conflicts: closed** (issue #1208, 2026-10-16). A wrong base on a job's branch is moved
(above); a job's pull request whose item no job follows is attached by reconciling, then tended as any. What stays is a second
pull request of an item whose job follows another one. A rebase is a tend, and a tend runs the item again for the pull request
its job follows: tending the second one would take the follow off the first. Two paths were open: tend the second one with a
job that follows no pull request, or close it. Closing is the smaller change and keeps one item, one followed pull request:
a job of the item already does the item's work in the followed one, so a second one with merge conflicts is a leftover of an
earlier job. So the census closes a `second_pull_request` (`closedAsSecond` in `src/sources/github/census.ts`) when:

- its head branch is named for its issue (`namesIssue`, a job's branch); one on any other branch is a person's, listed, never
  closed;
- GitHub reads it with merge conflicts (`conflicting` in the batched read); one with none stays open and listed, for a person;
- the census did not move it in the same round: its merge conflicts were read against the base from before, so the next census
  decides.

It closes it without a merge (`GitHubApi.closeWithoutMerge`), posts one fixed comment (`secondPullRequestNote`: it has merge
conflicts, the work on its issue continues in the followed pull request, which a job follows, and a change to keep goes
there), and lists it no more. The followed pull request and its job do not change. A close GitHub refuses is logged and tried at
the next round, with no comment. No event: no job holds it, as for the move. Its branch stays, so a person can reopen it.

Tests: `test/domain/untracked-pull-requests.test.ts` (each reason, a stack, no landing batches, the issue a text links),
`test/sources/github-pr-census.test.ts` (the census, the move of a job's branch, a person's branch left),
`test/sources/pr-census-cadence.test.ts` (once an hour, at once when asked, never paused; what is tracked),
`test/integration/untracked-pull-requests.test.ts` (over the real daemon: the source's status and `GET /api/pull-requests`),
`test/ui/pull-requests-view.test.ts` (the Not tracked list), `test/sources/github-graphql-pull-states.test.ts` (base and
title in the batched read). Part 2: `test/sources/github-take-in.test.ts` (Take into Intake, only on an issue the census
offers), `test/ui/pull-requests-untracked.test.ts` (its button, a viewer's none, a second pull request's text), the second
pull request in the domain, census and cadence tests, and Take into Intake over the real daemon in
`test/integration/untracked-pull-requests.test.ts`. Issue #1208: `test/sources/github-pr-census.test.ts` (a second pull request
closed with its note, the followed one left; none closed without merge conflicts, on a person's branch, or just moved; a refused
close tried again).

## Companion pull requests (issue #1143 reopened, 2026-10-24)

**The problem.** In a job repository other than the hopper's, two pull requests sat with merge conflicts after their jobs
finished, and nothing rebased them; comments on their issues asking for a rebase requeued nothing. Each job changed two
repositories, so it opened two pull requests: one in the other repository that closes the issue, and one in the issue's
own repository that records the work. The job followed the first one (`ownOpenPullRequestOf`, issues #2004, #2510). The
second one was followed by no job, so no follow saw its merge conflicts and no tend started. It was no stray (no job named
it in its source state), and the census skipped it: the ledger holds it as the item's pull request, from the job's own
`pr.create` record at its end (issue #2693, `withOpened`). The tending of parts 1 to 4 only reaches a followed pull request.

**A companion pull request** (`src/domain/companion-pull-requests.ts`) is an open pull request a job of an item opened
through the hopper (`github_proxy.done` of op `pr.create`), in the item's own repository, that is not the one the item's
newest job follows. That newest job **holds** the item's companions (`holdsCompanions`) when it ended, finished or failed,
no tend job or rework took its pull request (`follow` not `tended` or `reworked`), no proposal handed its work on, and it is
no failed tend.

- **The read** (`src/sources/companions.ts`, the sync loop's half; `src/sources/github/companions.ts`, the source's). In a
  round of every follow, after the census, the companions of each item whose newest job holds them, whose end is reported,
  and whose work item is not done or dropped and whose issue is not closed, are read one by one
  (`JobSource.readCompanions`, `GitHubApi.pullRequest`): state, merge conflicts (the hopper's mirror's answer where it has
  one), base and head branch. What each read saw is kept on the holder (`companions` in its source state, by URL; JSON in the
  job's body, no migration). One merged or closed is marked `ended` and read no more. A read that throws is logged and asked
  again at the next round. No read for an item with no companion.
- **The rebase.** A companion with merge conflicts is due as a `rebase` (`companionDue`) while its holder is the newest
  job of its item and the holder's own followed pull request needs no tend (that one goes first). It goes through the
  tending queue as any rebase: held behind a head that conflicts with it, the **base merge** first, else a **tend job** of
  the item with the tend brief for the companion's URL. The queue's conflict check, the base merge and the base tip are
  asked with the holder as if it followed the companion (`asFollowing`: its URL, base and head branch). The tend is
  recorded as any: `follow: tended`, `tended` with `companion: true`, `job.pull_request_tended` with the companion's URL, and
  the tend note on the companion. The tend job's push goes through the git proxy, so the **shrink guard** (issue #1096)
  judges it. A failed companion rebase is retried once its base moves, at most three in a row (part 3), and its retry keeps
  `companion`. A base merge that pushed marks the companion free of merge conflicts until the next read.
- **What shows it.** The tend job runs the item again, so the item and the job's timeline show the tend and which pull
  request it works on (`job.pull_request_tended`). The companion carries the tend note. The Pull requests card of the
  holder names the companion while the tend job works on it, and goes back to the followed pull request after.
- **After the tend.** The tend job's report follows the item's pull request as any job's does; it is the item's newest job,
  so it holds the companions from then on, and the next read finds the rebased companion with no merge conflicts.

**Not done, by decision.**

- A companion of an item whose issue is closed, or whose work item is done or dropped, is not rebased: a tend is a Run again
  of the item, and Run again reopens a closed issue (issue #2127). Since issue #2752 part 4, a done or closed item's
  companions are still read, and merged when ready; a dropped item's are not read.
- A companion in another repository than the item's: a tend job works in its item's repository. Since issue #2752 it
  is one: "Companion pull requests in another repository" below.
- "Behind" with no merge conflicts, as for a followed pull request (part 4).
- The pull requests a job did not open through the hopper: the census lists them (issue #1176).

Tests: `test/domain/companion-pull-requests.test.ts` (which job holds which companions, what a read keeps, when a rebase
is due, the holder as if it followed one), `test/integration/companion-pull-requests.test.ts` (over the real daemon: a
finished job's second pull request that gets merge conflicts is rebased by a tend job, with no comment from anyone, and
says so on it), `test/sources/pull-request-list.test.ts` (the card names the companion while it is tended).

## Companion pull requests in another repository (issue #2752 part 1, 2026-10-24)

**The problem.** Jobs of a workflow repository's issues opened their change in an app repository the hopper does not work
on, and a bookkeeping pull request in the issue's own repository. When the job followed the bookkeeping one, its pull
request in the app repository was no companion — a companion was of the item's own repository only — so no follow read it.
It got merge conflicts with its base, and nothing rebased it.

**The change.** A companion pull request is one of any GitHub repository (`companionsOf`: every GitHub pull request URL a job
of the item opened through the hopper, but the followed one; a GitLab merge request is none). It is read in its own
repository (`readCompanions` already read each by its repository), and a due rebase goes through the tending queue of the
companion's own repository (`tendNext` groups each due tend by its pull request's repository, not the holder's followed
one). The rest is as for a companion of the item's own repository: the base merge first, else a tend job of the item, which
pushes through the git proxy to that repository as for a followed pull request in another repository (issue #1778).

**Decisions.**
- **No tend note there.** As on a followed pull request in another repository (`tendStartedOn`), the hopper posts its tend
  note only on a pull request of the issue's repository.
- **The merge policy stays.** On a repository the hopper does not work on, the hopper merges only when a person named it on
  in yolo mode (issue #1806, "Yolo mode on a repository the hopper does not work on"); this part does not widen it.

**Left for later parts of issue #2752.** A job whose followed pull request is open and that the hopper does not merge there
(yolo mode off for that repository, or its merge refused) reads as plain finished (`PR ready`): it should say "needs merge in
<repo>" on the job, the issue and the Pull requests view. A companion is rebased, never merged.

Tests: `test/domain/companion-pull-requests.test.ts` ("it holds the ones it opened in another repository too"),
`test/integration/companion-pull-requests.test.ts` ("its second pull request in another repository … is rebased there too").

## Needs merge in a repository the hopper does not merge in (issue #2752 part 2, 2026-10-24)

**The problem.** A job of a workflow issue followed its pull request in an app repository that is not a job repository.
No person named that repository on in yolo mode, so the hopper merged nothing there (issue #1806). The job still read
`PR ready`, its card `waiting for a person to merge`, the same as a job repository with yolo mode off. Nothing said that
this pull request waits on a merge in another repository that the hopper never makes.

**The change.**
- The Pull requests list's card in such a repository waits on `needs merge` in place of `yolo off`
  (`src/domain/pull-request-list.ts`, `waitOf`): the repository is none of the job repositories, and yolo mode does not
  merge there (never named, or named off). The card says `needs merge in <repo>`, and that the hopper does nothing until a
  person merges it there or names the repository on in Settings → Yolo mode.
- The job's title says `needs merge in <repo>` (warn) in place of `PR ready` or `partly done` (`ui/src/model/job.ts`,
  `afterDone`), from the yolo mode view the UI already reads. A finished job with such a pull request no longer reads as
  plain finished. With yolo mode not read yet, it reads as before.
- A job repository with yolo mode off still waits on `yolo off`: a person reviews and merges it there by choice.

**Decisions.**
- **The merge policy stays** (issue #1806, part 1 of this issue). The state only says where the merge waits.
- **From the yolo mode settings, not from GitHub.** A refused merge already has its own wait (`merge refused`, with what
  GitHub said); a missing access shows as the refusal. No new read of GitHub.

**Left for later parts of issue #2752.** The issue label for a pull request that needs a merge in another repository, and
the merge of a ready companion pull request under its own repository's merge gate.

Tests: `test/sources/pull-request-list.test.ts` ("ready in a repository the hopper does not merge in"),
`test/ui/after-done.test.ts` ("a pull request in a repository the hopper does not merge in"),
`test/ui/pull-requests-view.test.ts` (the card's words).

## A ready companion pull request is merged (issue #2752 part 3, 2026-10-24)

**The problem.** Part 1 made a pull request a job opened in another repository a companion, and rebased it. Nothing merged
it: a companion that was ready, in a repository whose merge gate lets the hopper merge, stayed open until a person merged it.

**The change.** Each read of a companion (`readCompanions`, GitHub's half `src/sources/github/companions.ts`) that finds it
open with no merge conflicts asks the same merge as a followed pull request (`mergeWhenReady`, `src/sources/github/follow.ts`):
its change kind, its own repository's merge gate (yolo mode for that repository, change kinds; on a repository the hopper
does not work on, only when a person named it on, issue #1806), ready (not a draft, checks passed, or none within the grace
window), the done criteria of the job that holds it (`mergeHold`), then the merge gate (issue #939). Merged, the read says
so (`byHopper`), the companion is marked `ended`, and `job.companion_merged` records it on the holder. A merge GitHub refuses
is logged, and the companion stays open; a read or merge that throws is asked again at the next round.

**Decisions.**
- **The same gate as a followed pull request.** No new setting: the companion's own repository's yolo mode and change rule
  decide.
- **No merge marker** (issue #1588). After a stop between the merge call and the record, the next read sees the companion
  merged and marks it `ended`, with no `job.companion_merged`. The merge on GitHub is the record that counts.
- **No housekeeping** on a companion (no move to the landing branch, no close as superseded): that stays with followed and
  stray pull requests.

**Left for later parts of issue #2752.** The issue label for a pull request that needs a merge in another repository. A
companion of an item whose work item is done or whose issue is closed is not read (part 1), so it is not merged either.

Tests: `test/integration/companion-pull-requests.test.ts` ("its ready second pull request in another repository is merged
there …", "with yolo mode not on for that repository, it is not merged").

## Needs merge on the issue, and a done item's companions (issue #2752 part 4, 2026-10-24)

**The problem.** Part 2 said `needs merge in <repo>` on the job and its card, but the issue still carried
`hopper:pr-ready`, which reads as "waits for review" by any person who looks at the issue. And a companion of an item whose
work item was done or whose issue was closed was read no more (part 1), so a companion that got ready after the followed
pull request merged and closed the issue was never merged.

**The change.**
- **`hopper:needs-merge`** (`src/sources/github/labels.ts`), a new end label. While an item's pull request is in a
  repository the hopper does not merge in (`needsMergeIn`, `src/domain/yolo-mode.ts`: none of the job repositories, and yolo
  mode not named on for it — the same rule as the card's `needs merge`), its issue carries `hopper:needs-merge` in place of
  `hopper:pr-ready` or `hopper:partly-done`. The job's report puts it on (`needsMergeOf`, `src/sources/github/report.ts`),
  as does a follow that finds the pull request open; the **label mirror** keeps it (`labelsFor`, fact `needsMerge`, by the
  work item's pull request), and swaps it back for `hopper:pr-ready` once a person names the repository on. Like every end
  label it keeps the issue out (Intake's reason `NEEDS_MERGE`, group `pr-waiting`), and taken off by hand it is a Run again.
  The source learns the rule from the user's settings (`needsMerge` beside `yoloMode`, `src/users/source-context.ts`).
- **A done item's companions are read** (`src/sources/companions.ts`): an item that is done, or whose issue is closed, has
  its companions read still, so a ready one is merged under its repository's gate (part 3). None is rebased then: a tend is a
  Run again of the item, and Run again reopens a closed issue (issue #2127). A dropped item's companions are read no more.

**Decisions.**
- **A label, no comment.** The hopper writes only labels to issues ("GitHub text is neutral").
- **One label for a whole and a part.** `hopper:needs-merge` replaces `hopper:partly-done` too: the merge waits on a person
  either way, and the next part runs once that pull request merges.
- **No end to reading a done item's companions** but their own end: each read stops at a companion merged or closed. One
  that a person leaves open is read at each round, one call each.

Tests: `test/sources/github-label-needs-merge.test.ts`, `test/integration/companion-pull-requests.test.ts` ("its companion
that gets ready after the followed pull request merged and closed the issue is merged too").

## A job pushes to its own repository outside the job repositories (issue #1131, 2026-10-14)

**The problem.** A tend job's `git push --force-with-lease` to its own pull request's branch was refused: "<repo> is not
one of the repositories your jobs use, so the hopper pushes nothing there". The git broker let a job push to its own
repository only when that repository was one of its user's **job repositories**. But a job's own repository comes from its
source item, and a job can hold one that is not on that list: a job of the app source (its repositories are the app's
installation's), a direct job, or a job of a repository the user chose no more after intake (a tend job runs its item
again later). Its fetch worked (issue #1015) and GitHub said its user could push, so the refusal named no real reason.

**The change.** The job repositories decide intake, not where a job's own work goes. A push goes to the job's own
repository (or its fork) when its user can push to it (GitHub's `canPush`), with the same ref check (`checkPush`) and the
shrink guard as before. No job repository check is left on a push. A push with no GitHub connection is refused with the
connection's problem (403), as before.

**Not changed.** The GitHub proxy's writes (`hopper-gh`: an issue, a pull request, a comment) stay on the job repositories
(`checkRequest`, issue #1015). A job of a repository outside them still cannot open its pull request there through the
hopper; that is a separate change.

Tests: `test/integration/git-proxy.test.ts` ("pushes to the job's own repository when it is no job repository, forced too").

## Tagged items (issue #1141, 2026-10-14)

Owner request: the hopper should show the pull requests and issues the user is tagged in — a review requested from the
user, an @mention, an assignment — across the job repositories, each with why, age and checks, cleared once handled, and
notify on new review requests.

**As built:**
- **Read with the sync.** A connected account's GitHub source reads its **tagged items** at its discover: each intake sync
  interval, and at once on a sync a person asked for (`tagged.ts`, apart from the listing's timer). One read is GitHub's
  issue search over GraphQL (`taggedItems`, `app/graphql-tagged.ts`): per why one search — `is:open archived:false` and
  `is:pr review-requested:<login>`, `mentions:<login>` or `assignee:<login>` —, scoped by `repo:` qualifiers to the job
  repositories, grouped so each query stays within GitHub's 256 characters, at most ten searches to a request, the first 50
  hits each. Through the intake reserve, as the listing. A request that fails keeps the last list and says why
  (`taggedError`). The App adapter reads none: an installation token has no user.
- **Not intake's, not the user's own.** An item with the source's label is intake's (Intake, Jobs), and a pull request the
  user wrote is the user's own work (Pull requests): neither is tagged. A hit outside the job repositories is dropped.
- **Cleared by GitHub.** Each read replaces the list. A review given drops the request (GitHub's own `review-requested`), a
  merged or closed item is no longer open: the row leaves at the next read, with no state of the hopper's own.
- **Dismiss.** `dismiss`, an intake action on `POST /ui/api/sources/:name/intake` (operator), takes items the last read
  listed off the list for the whys they have now (`dismissTagged`, `src/domain/tagged.ts`). A new why shows the item again;
  a why the item lost ends that part of the dismissal (`taggedRead`), so a review requested again after a review shows.
  Nothing is written to GitHub. The source then syncs at once, as after every intake action.
- **Notify.** A pull request that newly asks for the user's review records `source.review_requested { source, key, author }`,
  once while the request stands; webhook subscribers get it like any event. Never the title.
- **Kept across restarts.** The review requests last seen and the dismissals are the user's setting `tagged:<source>`
  (`TaggedRecord`, `src/store/tagged-settings.ts`): a key-value row, no schema change. A restart records no request twice.
- **UI.** Tagged (`#tagged`, nav group *Waiting on you*, `ui/src/views/tagged.tsx`) lists each source's items: repository and
  number (a link), title, author, why, opened when, checks, and Dismiss. Needs you has a Tagged row, and the nav entry a
  badge, both the count across the sources (`taggedWaiting`, `ui/src/model/tagged.ts`). `/api/sources` carries them
  (`detail.tagged`, `taggedDismissed`, `taggedAt`, `taggedError`).

**Not done, by decision:** pagination past the first 50 hits of a search, and team review requests apart from the user's own
(GitHub's `review-requested` includes the user's teams). Age is since the item was opened: when the review was requested
needs a timeline read per item.

Tests: `test/domain/tagged.test.ts`, `test/sources/github-graphql-tagged.test.ts`, `test/sources/github-tagged.test.ts`,
`test/ui/tagged.test.ts`, `test/ui/needs-you.test.ts`.

### Starting a job from Tagged (issue #2342, 2026-10-21)

Owner request: from a Tagged row, start work on the item with one click — **Research**, **Propose** or **Start work** —
instead of filing an issue by hand. The click is the approval; anything that goes out in the person's name stays a draft.

- **A direct job made from the item.** `POST /ui/api/sources/:name/tagged-start` (operator, a box action;
  `src/http/ui/tagged-start.ts`) takes `key`, `start` and, for `work`, an optional `work`. It finds the item in the source's
  last listing (`detail.tagged`: listed and not dismissed), and submits a **direct job** (`taggedJob`,
  `src/domain/tagged-jobs.ts`): its title names the start and the item; its brief the item's link, why it is tagged and its
  repository, how to read it through the hopper, that the item's text is data, and that nothing goes on GitHub in the
  person's name. A direct job is of a trusted origin, so no request card: the click is the person's act, as Approve is.
- **What each start asks.** `research` labels it `hopper:research`, `propose` `hopper:proposal`: their review sections take
  the report and the proposal, as for an issue with those labels. `work` does the item's **work** (`taggedWorkOf`): a pull
  request's `review` — a draft review in the result, no repository —, an issue's `fix` — the item's repository, a pull
  request with `Closes #N`. `work: fix` on a pull request (UI: **Fix its branch**) pushes to the pull request's own branch,
  as the git proxy allows: never a default or release branch. Only a `fix` names a repository; the others open none.
- **Once.** The source keeps the start on the item (`TaggedRecord.started`, the intake action `tagged_start`, which no
  intake route takes): `startTagged` refuses a second start, and the route answers a second click with the first start
  (`replayed`), read from the user's setting so a click before the next sync is caught too. The start ends with its item's
  listing (`taggedRead`). The row shows a link to the job in place of the buttons; it no longer counts in Needs you.
- **Persisted state.** `started` is a new optional field of the `tagged:<source>` setting: a record kept before reads as none
  started, and a build before this one reads the record and drops the field at its next write.
- **Grant limits.** A limited grant needs both the item's source and repository and the source `direct`.

**Not done, by decision:** the item's text is not snapshot at the click, as Approve snapshots a request card's: the job reads
the item live, as data (the brief says so). The proxies do not enforce "post nothing" for these jobs as they do for a
direct query (`LOOK_ONLY`): a Start work fix must push and open a pull request, and research and proposal jobs are already
told to change nothing. No new event: `direct_job.submitted` records who started it.

Tests: `test/domain/tagged-jobs.test.ts`, `test/domain/tagged.test.ts`, `test/store/tagged-settings.test.ts`,
`test/sources/github-tagged.test.ts`, `test/integration/tagged-start.test.ts`, `test/ui/tagged.test.ts`.

## The machine's terminal (issue #1128, 2026-10-14, part 6)

Owner request, part 4 of the issue, the rest of it: open a machine's herdr session through the hopper, not only a running job's
pane. The **machine's terminal** (glossary) lists every pane of the hopper's herdr session on a machine — the ones no job holds
too: a sign-in a person started by hand, a shell left open, a job's pane after its job ended — and gives each the job's
terminal's view and input.

- **What it reaches.** The hopper's own herdr session on the machine, the one its jobs run in (`MachineHerdr.session`): this
  machine's, an ssh target's, or a client target's (the client serves only its own session). Never herdr's `default` session: the
  hopper never names it (`sessionProblem`), so a person's own herdr tabs outside the hopper's session stay theirs. To reach a pane
  from the hopper, open it in the hopper's session.
- **The port.** `HerdrClient.listPanes()` (`herdr pane list`: pane, tab, workspace, the terminal's title, the agent and its
  state, never the working directory) and the executor port's `paneSession(machine)` (`src/domain/terminal.ts`): the panes, a
  pane's read and its input by pane id, on the herdr the executor reaches the machine by (`herdrAt`, as `machineShell`). The
  engine (`src/engine/machine-terminal.ts`) asks the first of the machine's executors that gives one, as the sweep does.
- **Routes.** `POST /ui/api/machines/:id/terminal/panes` → `{ machineId, panes }`, each pane with `jobId` when a job at work or
  waiting holds it (its lane on that machine, its executor state's pane). `…/screen {paneId, lines?}` →
  `{ machineId, paneId, sessionId, screen, at }`. `…/input {paneId, text} | {paneId, keys}`, a box action. The limits are the
  job's terminal's. 404: no such machine. 409: no executor reaches a herdr session there, or no such pane in it. 502: the
  machine does not answer.
- **Who.** An **admin**, not an operator: a pane no job holds may be a shell on the machine, and typing there is running
  commands as the hopper's user there. Then Access: OpenFGA's `machine_terminal#can_attach` (new type `machine_terminal`,
  `owner: [user]`, `can_attach: owner`), the machine's user told as its owner at each check; fail closed as every Access check
  (`machineTerminalGaps`). Over the API, a token whose scopes name the routes (the Machines section of the scope registry) and,
  for the input, a box grant.
- **Audit.** The job's terminal's sessions (`terminalSessions`), keyed by machine and pane too: `terminal.opened` and
  `terminal.typed` carry `machineId` and `paneId`, and land on the job's timeline when a job holds the pane. Never the text.
- **UI.** Machines → a machine card → Terminal (admin, machine online, with a herdr session): the panes as buttons — the title,
  else the agent, else the pane id, and the job that holds it —; a pick shows the pane terminal the job view uses
  (`ui/src/views/pane-terminal.tsx`, shared).
- **Residual risk.** This is a remote shell on every machine with a hopper herdr session, from anywhere the UI reaches, for an
  admin who passes Access. The control is the role, Access, the box grant over the API, and the audit; the hopper keeps no text.

Tests: `test/integration/machine-terminal.test.ts` (list, view and type through the daemon over the fake herdr, the job's pane
named, the events without the text, an unknown machine or pane, a bad input, an operator, Access down),
`test/ui/machine-terminal-view.test.ts`, `test/herdr/cli-client.test.ts` (`listPanes`), `test/authz/model.test.ts`.

## Change kinds (issue #1076, 2026-10-13)

The problem: every pull request got the same gate. A docs fix waited for a person as long as a change to sign-in did,
and with yolo mode on, a change to sign-in merged as fast as a docs fix. Review needs depend on what kind of change it is.

**As built:**
- **A change kind per pull request.** Each read of an open followed pull request classifies it (`src/domain/change-kinds.ts`,
  pure) by the files it changes (the mirror's `git diff --name-only`, issue #935 part 2) and, for the files whose content
  can change the kind, the lines it changes (the mirror's `git diff -U0`, `changedLines`; the blobs come on demand). Each
  file is, in this order: **sensitive** by path (sign-in, secrets, vault, access, tokens, the sandbox and trust,
  migrations, CI, infra, deploy, shell scripts, dependency manifests and lock files, agent instructions: `AGENTS*.md`,
  `CLAUDE.md`, `SKILL.md`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`); **docs** by path (Markdown and other text, `docs/`); **sensitive** by
  content (a changed line matches a content expression: a secret, a password, a key, a credential, `child_process`,
  `eval`, `new Function`, `process.env`; docs are not read); **tests** by path; **docs** again when every changed line is
  blank or a comment of the file's language (`//`, `/*`, ` * `, `*/`; `#` for Python, Ruby, YAML, TOML); **low risk** by
  path (styles, images); else **code**. The most severe file is the pull request's kind. A file whose content is needed
  and was not read is code: never lighter than what was proved. More files than the mirror names (300), or no files
  known: not classified.
- **Each kind names a merge gate.** `ready`: the hopper merges it once it is ready (not a draft, no merge conflicts, its
  checks passed or none started within the grace window) with no person, yolo mode on or off. `yolo`: only with yolo mode
  on, the gate before kinds. `person`: only a person's Merge now. Built-in: docs and low risk `ready`; tests, code and
  sensitive `yolo`. Not classified: yolo mode decides, as before. The checks a docs-only pull request waits for are the
  ones its repository runs on it: a repository makes them lighter with its own path filters. The gate also says what is
  in motion (`inMotion`) and on its way to the merge (`queueHeads`).
- **Rules per repository.** The change-kind rules are saved with yolo mode (`changeKinds` in its settings and its
  `yolo_mode.changed` event; `POST /ui/api/yolo-mode`, an admin's): `default` over the built-in rule, then per repository
  (`owner/repo`, lowercased). Each list a rule names — the globs of `docs`, `tests`, `lowRisk` and `sensitive` files, the
  `sensitiveContent` expressions (case-insensitive, each must compile) — replaces that list; each merge gate it names
  replaces that gate. `null`: the built-in rule again. Settings → Yolo mode shows each kind's gate and the built-in rule,
  and edits the rules as JSON. `GET /api/yolo-mode` answers the built-in rule as `choices.changeRule`.
- **Recorded.** A kind that is new or changed is the event `job.pull_request_classified` (the pull request, the kind, and
  why: at most five files and the rule each matched), before a merge it allows. The work-item ledger keeps it on the item
  (`changeKind`); a new job of the item clears it. The kind is kept on what the follow saw (`seen.change`, with the key of
  the rule that made it): the same files under the same rule and head are not read again, and a batch answer under
  another rule reads the pull request again, so a rule change applies at the next sync.
- **Shown.** Each Pull requests card has its kind as a badge, why in its title. A card whose kind only a person merges
  waits on `person merges`. The `done` line of a job with yolo mode off says the change rules may still let the hopper
  merge a docs-only or low-risk change.

**Residual risk.** The comment check reads changed lines one by one, without the lines around them: a changed line inside a
string that starts with `//`, or a ` * ` line that continues an expression, reads as a comment. Such a change still
waits for its checks. A docs-only change to a repository whose build reads its Markdown (a prompt, a page) merges with
no person: name those files in the repository's `sensitive` list.

## Jobs ask the hopper, not GitHub: pr status (issue #1072, 2026-10-13)

The problem: a job read GitHub itself to learn where its pull request stood (`pr view`, its checks), and asked again
while it waited. Each read spent the rate limit, and each job had its own view, which could be older than the hopper's
and disagree with what the Pull requests list showed. This is the first part: one read, `pr status`, answered from the
hopper's records.

**`pr status`** (`sh "$HOPPER_GH" pr status N --repo OWNER/NAME`, op `pr.status`, `POST /job/github`): the pull
request's `state` (`open`, `merged`, `closed`), `draft`, `mergeable` (`mergeable`, `conflicts`, `unknown`), `checks`
(`passing`, `pending`, `failing`, `none`, `unknown`) and `failedChecks`, `base`, `head`, why the hopper has not merged
it yet (`waits`, the Pull requests list's words), and its work item (`item`: its `key`, its ledger `state`, `waitingOn`).
A read, like `pr view` (issue #1015): the hopper's own job asks it on any repository its connection sees; another user's
job does not. A repo query (issue #1074, "Repo queries"): `source` says where the answer came from, in this order:

1. `hopper` — the asking user's own records (`ProxyUser.pullRequest`, `src/users/github-proxy.ts`): the pull request's
   card on the Pull requests list (`pullRequestList`, what following it last saw, `seen`), the same view a person reads;
   or, with no card, a pull request the work-item ledger says merged or closed (`WorkItemLedger.byPullRequest`, whatever the URL's case). A card
   not checked yet, or an open pull request only the ledger names, says nothing of its checks, so it is not answered
   from here (`knownPullRequest`, `src/github-proxy/pr-status.ts`, pure). Neither the hopper's GitHub connection nor
   the rate limits are asked. One exception (issue #2321): an open pull request whose records say its checks fail. The
   follow's last read can be of a head a push replaced since (a tend job's force push after a rebase), or of a run a
   newer run of its check superseded, and a job or a person acts on failed checks. So its checks are read again as in
   3 below — the head as it is now, the newest run of each check —, from the repo-query cache while fresh
   (`withReadChecks`): `checks` and `failedChecks` are the read's, what the follow read of a failed check (`reported`)
   stays with the same run, by its URL, and a `checks failing` wait the read does not bear out is dropped. `source`
   stays `hopper`. A read the rate limits refuse, or that fails on GitHub, leaves the records' answer. A second
   exception (issue #2497): an open pull request a tend job works on, or worked on and failed (its card waits `tending`
   or `tend failed`, `tendedAnswer`). Its job follows it no more (`follow: tended`, issue #736), so the records are from
   before the tend: merge conflicts the tend job's push removed, checks of a head it replaced. It is read again the same
   way, whole (`withReadPullRequest`): `state`, `draft`, `mergeable`, `checks` and `failedChecks` are the read's; the
   card's wait and the work item stay. `pr wait` opens no watch on it, since no follow would end the watch: with
   `--for mergeable` it measures from the records, so a read that shows other merge conflicts answers `wait: settled`
   at once; else `wait: none` with a `note` that says why.
2. `cache` — the repo-query cache (`repo-query.ts`): a GitHub read of the same `pr.status` query kept less than
   `REPO_QUERY_FRESH_MS` (30 s) ago, or of a merged pull request, with the item as the ledger says now. Counted against
   the rate limits as every repo query.
3. `github` — read now (`api.ts` `pullStatus`): the pull request (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}`), then its head
   commit's check runs (`GET …/commits/{sha}/check-runs`): failing once one failed (`failure`, `timed_out`,
   `startup_failure`), pending while one runs, none with no run, `unknown` when GitHub refuses them
   (403, 404: the connection may not read checks, issue #855). Commit statuses are not read: the hopper's checks are
   GitHub Actions check runs. Through the rate limits (`pr.status`: 120 an hour per job, 600 per machine) and the shared
   rate limiter, as every proxy call; the answer is kept in the repo-query cache.

**The measure.** Each answer is a `github_proxy.done` event on the job's timeline with `source`: how many of a job's
reads reached GitHub is the count of `source: github`. The job rules' GitHub line (`GITHUB_PROXY_LINE`) tells a job to
ask `pr status`, not GitHub, at most once a minute while it waits; `hopper-gh`'s help says the same.

**A wait on checks: `pr wait`** (part 2, 2026-10-14). Before it, a job that waited on its checks asked `pr status` once a
minute. Now it asks once: `sh "$HOPPER_GH" pr wait N --repo OWNER/NAME [--timeout SECONDS]`, op `pr.wait` of
`POST /job/github` (`waitRequest`, `src/github-proxy/policy.ts`), asked as `pr.status` — the same policy, the same
answer, the same `github_proxy.done` event, which records `wait`:

- the hopper knows the pull request (step 1 above) and its checks run (`prSettled`, `pr-status.ts`, pure: open with
  checks `pending`): it opens a **watch** on the job's stream (issue #613, "The job stream") — `createPrWaits`,
  `src/github-proxy/pr-waits.ts`, its body `{ owner: github, repo, number }`, one per job and pull request (asked again,
  the open one answers) — emits `github.pr_waiting`, and answers 202 with `wait: open`, `waitId`, `until` and
  `waitSeconds`. `--timeout` is the watch's seconds (an hour unless said, at most a day);
- it knows the pull request and its checks ended, or it is merged or closed: 200 now, `wait: settled`;
- it does not know it (a pull request in another repository, for example): answered as `pr status` (the cache, else
  GitHub). Its checks ended, or it is merged or closed: `wait: settled`. Else `wait: none` — nothing would tell the hopper
  when the checks end — with `waitOn`, the `on:` line `pr OWNER/NAME#N checks`, and a `note` that says to end the turn
  with HOPPER_WAITING and that line: the wait check reads the pull request on GitHub in any repository ("Wait checks",
  `pr_checks_ended`) and wakes the job when its checks end (issue #1731; `unwatchedWait`, `pr-status.ts`). `hopper-gh`
  exits 3. Only for `--for checks`: `--for mergeable` answers `wait: none` alone. A running job's own pull request is one
  the hopper does not follow yet: the Pull requests list holds only the pull requests of ended jobs;
- **no checks is not settled** (issue #2322). Right after a push GitHub has not made the head commit's check runs yet, so
  a read says `none`; a moment later they are there, `queued`, which the read counts as running (`pending`). So `checks:
  none` on an open pull request never settles a wait on its checks (`prSettled`), whether the hopper follows it or not.
  No event tells the hopper when checks start, so it opens no watch: it answers `wait: none` with `waitOn` and the note,
  as above. The wait check holds while checks run, or while none started within two minutes of the head commit
  (`checksOutcome`, `NO_CHECKS_MS`), and then wakes the job: a repository with no checks costs the job those minutes.

**Pushed, not polled.** The watch is answered again from the user's records — never GitHub, never on a timer — when an
event says what the hopper saw of a pull request changed (`job.pull_request_seen`: following it saw its wait change, as
checks that ended do; `job.pull_request_followed`, `_merged`, `_closed`, `_abandoned`) and when the job subscribes to its
stream. Settled, it ends with `github.pr_settled` and the status, as JSON text; when the job is on its own wait
(HOPPER_WAITING, issue #998), that wait ends with the same text, as a skill's answer ends it. The stream's sweep ends it
at its deadline (`hopper.expired`) or when the job ends (`hopper.ended`). Watches persist (the job stream's tables), so a
restart loses none: the job's next subscribe answers it again. The skill waits leave a watch whose body names an
`owner` to that owner (`src/skills/waits.ts`).

**`hopper-gh pr wait`** (`src/github-proxy/script.ts`): one `POST /job/github`; on 202 it reads the stream of the watch
with `stream_wait` — the loop `hopper-skill --wait` had, moved to `src/job-stream/script.ts` so both scripts use one —,
then prints the status. Exit 0 the status (settled), 1 a refusal, 3 `wait: none`, 4 the deadline passed.

**Reviews: `pr reviews`** (part 3, 2026-10-15). `sh "$HOPPER_GH" pr reviews N --repo OWNER/NAME`, op `pr.reviews`: a
repo query (the table in "Repo queries"), so the cache answers it again while it is fresh, and on a merged pull request.
On a miss, `GET …/pulls/N/reviews`, every page (`api.ts` `pullReviews`): `reviews`, oldest first (id, author, `state` in
lower case — `approved`, `changes_requested`, `commented`, `dismissed` —, body, submittedAt, url; a pending review, not
yet sent, is left out), and `decision` (`reviewDecision`, pure): the latest review of each reviewer that approves, asks
for changes or was dismissed decides — `changes_requested` when one asks for changes, else `approved` when one approves,
else `none`. A comment alone decides nothing. Rate-limited as `pr.view`.

**The count, in the UI** (part 3). A job's parts list ("A job's parts list", `src/domain/job-bom.ts` `githubCalls`) has a
part `github` under work, once the job asked the hopper anything on GitHub: `N GitHub calls` (or `No GitHub calls`), with
the reads the hopper did on GitHub for the job (`github_proxy.done` with `source: github`), its writes and pushes (one with
no `source`: `pr.create`, `issue.comment`, `git.push` and the like), and the reads it answered with no call (`source`
`hopper` or `cache`). Refused and failed requests are not counted: the first made no call, the second is on the timeline.
The count of a job's reads of GitHub is so the number the issue asks to see drop.

**What stays with git.** A file at a ref and the commit history: a job reads them with git, whose fetch already goes
through the hopper (issue #652, "Git through the hopper") and spends no REST call. Issue state: `issue view`, a repo
query with the ledger's word beside it. No `hopper repo …` command is added for them: it would read GitHub where git
already read it once.

Part 3: `test/integration/github-proxy.test.ts` (`pr reviews` read on GitHub once, then from the cache, with its
decision), `test/github-proxy/repo-query.test.ts` (who may ask it), `test/domain/job-bom.test.ts` (the `github` part:
calls, writes and reads answered with no call; none when the job asked nothing).

Tests: `test/github-proxy/pr-status.test.ts` (the status from a card and from the ledger, nothing known, the policy;
the broker: from the hopper with GitHub not asked, from GitHub once, then from the repo-query cache while fresh),
`test/integration/github-proxy.test.ts` (the real daemon and `hopper-gh`: a followed pull request answered as the Pull
requests list shows it, with no GitHub call; one the hopper does not know read on GitHub, then from the cache).

`pr wait`: `test/github-proxy/pr-wait.test.ts` (when a wait is over; the broker's 200 `settled`, 202 with a watch, and
`none` read as `pr status`; one watch per job and pull request, ended with the status on a pull request event and not
before, the job's own wait ended with it; a skill watch left alone, and the skill waits leaving a pull request's alone),
`test/integration/pr-status.test.ts` (the real daemon and `hopper-gh pr wait`: the job asks once, waits on its stream,
and gets the status once the hopper sees the checks pass; GitHub not asked).

## Job worktrees in `.worktrees` (issue #1188, 2026-10-14)

**The gap.** Issue #1103 asked for every job worktree at `<wd>/.worktrees/<repo>/<job>`, never inside a repository, and
`.hopper-scratch` gone. It shipped `<work tree>/workspace/worktrees/<name>-<job id>` instead — inside the workflow repo's
checkout when the work tree is one — and kept `.hopper-scratch/<job id>` as the scratch dir that the reap, the sweep, the
checkpoint and Work not pushed key on.

**The change** (`src/domain/job-layout.ts`, the one layout; `src/client/reap.ts` keeps the same names, `LAYOUT`, since the
client imports nothing of hopper, and `test/domain/job-layout.test.ts` holds the two together):
- **One place.** Everything a job puts in its work tree is under `<work tree>/.worktrees`, which ignores itself
  (`.gitignore` of `*`, written by the scratch command and by the job worktree command):
  - each job worktree, `.worktrees/<name>/<job id>` (`jobWorktreeOf`): `<name>` the job's repository's, or the work tree's
    own when the worktree is of the work tree;
  - each job's scratch dir, `.worktrees/@scratch/<job id>` (`jobScratchOf`): its temporary files, its credentials dir,
    its temp link's target;
  - the shared dependencies, `.worktrees/@deps/<lockfile hash>/node_modules`.
  A name that starts with `@` is the hopper's own: no GitHub repository name holds `@`, so no repository's worktrees and
  the hopper's areas share a directory.
- **Of what** is unchanged: the work tree itself when it is the top of the job's repository, else the repository's
  checkout `<work tree>/workspace/<name>`, the one the workflow repo tends. The worktree is never in that checkout.
- **Everything reads the one layout.** The reap and the survey (`src/client/reap.ts`), the sweep (`src/engine/sweep.ts`,
  by `worktreeParts` and `scratchParts`), the checkpoint (`src/client/checkpoint.ts`), the credentials
  (`src/client/credential.ts`), kept work (`src/domain/kept-work.ts`), the machine shell, the footer's work-tree line and
  the disk budget's paths: the survey measures `.worktrees`, one path per work tree.
- **The layout before is only cleaned up.** Nothing is made there. The survey still lists `.hopper-scratch/<job id>` and
  `workspace/worktrees/<name>-<job id>` (and measures them while they are there), and a reap takes them by the same rule as
  the new ones: removed when clean and pushed, kept and recorded as `job.work_kept` otherwise, removed whatever they hold
  on a discard. A reap of any job of the work tree, once the layout before holds no job's scratch dir or worktree, removes
  the rest of it — `.hopper-scratch` with its shared dependencies and repository mirrors, and `workspace/worktrees` — and
  runs `git worktree prune` in the work tree's repository and in each checkout of its workspace. A kept old worktree holds
  that back until a person pushes or discards it.

**Not changed.** The temp link `/tmp/hopper-<job id>`, the scratch command's marker `hopper-scratch-ready`, and the
checkout `workspace/<name>`. A client target that runs an older release refuses the new scratch paths until the hopper
loads this release onto it ("Client releases"); the sweep reaps what that left once it has.

Tests: `test/domain/job-layout.test.ts` (every job worktree under `<wd>/.worktrees/`, real git), `test/herdr/job-worktree.test.ts`,
`job-worktree-reap.test.ts` (the layout before cleaned up), `test/client/reap.test.ts`, `test/client/survey-roots.test.ts`,
`test/engine/sweep.test.ts`, `test/domain/kept-work.test.ts`, `test/herdr/shared-deps.test.ts`.

## Leftovers a person decides (issue #1116, 2026-10-16)

**The gap.** After issue #1188 the sweep removes an old `.hopper-scratch/<job id>` of an ended job when it is clean and
pushed, and keeps one with work not pushed, which Failures lists under Work not pushed. Two kinds of old dir stay out of that
path: a dir whose job the hopper does not know (another hopper's, a test's, anything else left there; the sweep never touches
a job it does not know), and a repository mirror `.hopper-scratch/repos/<owner>/<name>.git` that a kept worktree still uses.
Nobody saw them, and nothing removed them.

**The change** (`src/client/leftovers.ts`, the scripts; `src/domain/leftovers.ts`, pure; `src/engine/sweep-leftovers.ts`;
`src/http/ui/leftovers.ts`; Machines, `ui/src/views/machine-leftovers.tsx`):
- **A leftover** (glossary) is a dir right in a work tree's `.hopper-scratch` (not `deps`, not `repos`) whose name is no job
  the hopper knows, or a repository mirror there. A known job's dir is not one: the sweep reaps an ended one by the reap's
  rule, and a live one is its job's. A mirror is listed only while a dir in `.hopper-scratch` holds the layout before; once
  none does, the next reap in that work tree removes the rest of it, mirrors too, as before (issue #1188).
- **The listing.** After its reaps, each pass asks the machine (`MachineShell.leftovers`; a client target's `POST /leftovers
  {roots}`) about the work trees the survey found. The script only reads: each leftover with its age, whether it holds work
  not pushed (by the reap's own rule, `UNPUSHED_SH` in `src/client/reap.ts`: a change, a commit no remote has, or a stash; for a
  mirror, a branch of its own no remote has), the worktrees that still use a mirror, and its size (one `du -skx` per work
  tree, cut off at 20 s; none where `timeout` is missing). The sweep keeps the leftovers it does not judge per machine, in
  memory (`Sweep.leftovers`), as it keeps the disk measure. A listing that fails keeps the last one and is logged once; a
  client older than this lists none.
- **A person decides.** `GET /api/machines` carries each machine's listing as `leftovers`, and its Machines card lists each
  one: the path, what it is, its size and age, "work not pushed", and "kept" when a keep stands. `POST
  /ui/api/machines/leftovers {machineId, path, decision}` (operator, a box action):
  - `keep` records `machine.leftover_kept` and removes nothing. The listing shows it kept on the next passes.
  - `remove` asks first in the UI (what is lost, that it cannot be undone), then removes the dir on its machine whatever it
    holds (`MachineShell.removeLeftover`; a client target's `POST /leftover-remove {path}`), its mirror's empty owner dir too,
    and runs `git worktree prune` in the work tree's repository, its workspace's checkouts and the mirrors left. Then
    `machine.leftover_removed` with whether it held work not pushed, its size, and `gone` when it was no longer there.
  - Only a path the sweep listed on that machine is taken (409 else), and the script takes only a dir right in
    `.hopper-scratch` or a mirror in its `repos` (`isLeftoverPath`: absolute, no `.` or `..` part, one `.hopper-scratch`
    part), never a link. A machine offline or out of reach, or a removal that left the dir there, is a 409, and the
    leftover stays listed.
- **The sweep removes none by itself.** Nothing else changes in the reap or the sweep.

**Not changed.** The reap's rule, Work not pushed and its Discard, and the rest of the layout before going once nothing holds
it. A keep is a decision on Machines only: a later reap that finds the layout before free removes a kept mirror with the rest.

Tests: `test/client/leftovers.test.ts` (the listing and the removal for real: real git, a real mirror and its worktree),
`test/engine/sweep-leftovers.test.ts` (what is listed, keep, remove, refusals), `test/ui/leftovers.test.ts` (the card's text),
and the reap's tests for the shared rule (`test/client/reap.test.ts`, `test/herdr/job-worktree-reap.test.ts`).

## Failover to signed-in machines (issue #1128, 2026-10-14, part 7)

Owner request, part 5 of the issue: when an account is expired or out of spend, pause its lanes and move work to machines on
other accounts, not hold it there.

- **Out of spend: already so.** A usage source reads its machine's own account (issue #139); a week or session window at the
  hard limit caps that executor's lanes on that machine at 0 ("The decider", steps 1-2), so new jobs go to machines on
  other accounts. Nothing changes there.
- **Signed out: new.** `claude auth status` gives no expiry ("Tool accounts"), so "expired" is known only once the tool reads
  signed out. A **signed-out tool** (glossary) is a usage source whose account names its machine and has `signedOut`
  (`signedOutOf`, `src/decider/signed-out.ts`, pure, from each source's state at each gather). The decider takes them as
  `DecisionInputs.signedOut` (absent on Decisions stored before it: none) and:
  - places no new job of the source's executors on that machine (`eligible`; every job when the source names no executor,
    as a reading that names none limits every job). The job goes to another machine of its executor, or
  - is held with why, when every machine it may go to is signed out, or it is pinned to one (`nativeHold`). The hold says to
    sign it in from Accounts; once the tool reads signed in again (a **tool sign-in** reads it at once), the next Decision
    places it.
  - The reasons name each one (`m: claude signed out (usage source s): no new job of executor e`); a machine whose every
    executor is kept off says so as its idle reason, and its idle lanes close as at any machine with no job to run.
- **What is not moved.** A job resuming returns to its pane there (`pendingAnswer`): a sign-in from the hopper answers its
  not-signed-in question ("Tool sign-in"), or, with another machine signed in, the signed-out move takes it there (issue
  #1211, "The signed-out move"). A job that holds a lane there now is not stopped: it may be at work, signed in
  before the read. A read that failed is not a sign-out (`unknown`): a machine not dialled in is offline anyway.
- **Freshness.** The read is the source's (`intervalSeconds`, 10 minutes by default). A job placed in that gap meets Claude's
  login and asks its not-signed-in question; the sign-in answers it.

Tests: `test/decider/signed-out.test.ts`, `test/integration/usage-accounts.test.ts` (a job held on a signed-out machine
starts once it is signed in from the hopper).

## Signed-out tools in Needs you, the sign-in link, and the terminals from the CLI (issue #1128, 2026-10-14, part 8)

Owner request, part 2 of the issue (a Needs-you item when a login expires) and what part 7 left: a link from the question to
Accounts, and a CLI for the terminals.

- **Needs you: Accounts.** A row of its own (`NEEDS_YOU_KINDS` `accounts`, after Logins, linked to `#accounts`): one line per
  machine whose agent tool reads signed out (`signedOutLines`, `ui/src/model/tool-accounts.ts`), from the tool accounts the
  Accounts badge already reads (`GET /api/tool-accounts`, polled every 30 s). It shows as soon as the usage source reads the
  sign-out (its `intervalSeconds`), and goes when a read says signed in. An `unknown` read is not counted: a failed read is not
  a sign-out, as for failover.
- **No warning before the expiry.** `claude auth status` gives no expiry, and Claude renews its own access token with its refresh
  token, so an expiry of the access token is no sign-out to come. The hopper has no time to warn at; the sign-out is the signal.
  When a tool gives one, its usage source carries it on `Account` and the row names it (issue #1211, "The signed-out move").
- **The question links to Accounts.** A not-signed-in question's card says "Sign Claude in on <machine> from Accounts", a link
  to `#accounts`, and what the sign-in does: at Claude's prompt it answers the question; at Claude's login screen
  (`LOGIN_SCREEN_MARK`) a person answers after it. The UI imports nothing of `src/` at runtime, so `ui/src/model/questions.ts`
  says the start of `NOT_SIGNED_IN` and the login mark again; `test/ui/question-machine.test.ts` builds its questions from the
  `src/domain/questions.ts` constants, so the two cannot drift apart unnoticed.
- **`hopper terminal`** (`src/cli-operator-terminal.ts`): the routes of the job's terminal (`job <job>`, operator) and the machine's
  terminal (`machine <machine> [<pane>]`, admin), as every operator action — a UI session minted for one call, or a grant's API
  token. With no verb it reads the screen (`--lines`) or, for a machine with no pane, lists the panes; `type` writes the text on
  **stdin**, never an argument, so what a person types stays out of the shell's history and the process list; one end of line is
  dropped (press Enter with `keys enter`); `keys <key>...` presses keys. The daemon checks the keys, the limits, the role and
  Access. Its terminal sessions say `via: cli`.

Tests: `test/ui/needs-you.test.ts`, `test/ui/needs-you-view.test.ts`, `test/ui/accounts-view.test.ts`,
`test/ui/question-machine.test.ts`, `test/integration/machine-terminal.test.ts` (`hopper terminal`).

## The signed-out move (issue #1211, 2026-10-16)

Follow-up of issue #1128. Failover ("Failover to signed-in machines") kept new jobs off a signed-out machine, but a job that
already waited there on its **not-signed-in question** stayed, until a person signed the tool in on that machine. Now it goes
on at a signed-in machine, with no person.

- **When.** On each engine tick (`src/engine/signed-out-move.ts`, one pass at a time, beside auto-park), a job on a question
  (`waiting_answer`) whose open question starts with `NOT_SIGNED_IN` moves when (`signedOutMove`, `src/decider/signed-out.ts`,
  pure):
  - the machine that raised the question has a **signed-out tool** that keeps the job's executor off it;
  - the job names no machine of its own (`spec.machineId`: a person's or a routing rule's pin stays);
  - another machine is online, runs the job's executor, has no signed-out tool for it, and a usage source reads its tool
    signed in as an identity (`connectedOf`): a machine with no usage source, or a read that failed, is not a target.
  It is not required that a lane is free there now: the job waits in the queue for one, as any job does.
- **How.** The hopper takes a checkpoint of the job ("Checkpoints and resume elsewhere"), then, in one transaction, parks it
  (`recordPark`) and answers its question as `signed-out-move` (`SIGNED_OUT_MOVE_BY`, a trail attempt of role `fixed`, its
  reason naming the tool, the machine it left and the machines signed in). Parked, the job keeps the answer
  (`signedOutMoveAnswer`). Then the executor ends its pane and agent (`Executor.park`), and the hopper takes one more
  checkpoint, so the session is whole (the one before stands if it fails). Then:
  - **From its checkpoint**, when it holds the agent session: picked up to resume elsewhere (`recordUnpark`, elsewhere). The
    claim is that of "Checkpoints and resume elsewhere": a new job worktree, the checkpoint restored, the same session, told
    `elsewhereBrief` and the answer. Text the old pane held unsent behind Claude's screen (`turn.unsent`) goes after the
    answer, so nothing the hopper meant to send is lost.
  - **As a new start**, when Claude never got the job's task: no agent session recorded, or a checkpoint with no session, no
    commit and an empty patch (Claude writes its session file at its first message). Queued, not pinned, with no answer
    pending: the claim runs the job as at its first start. `job.unparked { to: queued, elsewhere: true }` says so.
  - A checkpoint that cannot be taken (its machine not reached, its executor takes none), or one that holds work but no
    session, does not move the job: it stays on its question for a sign-in or a person, and the move tries it again after
    10 minutes (`MOVE_RETRY_MS`).
- **The decider.** A job resuming elsewhere has no pane to return to, so a signed-out tool keeps it off a machine as it keeps a
  new job off (`signedOutFor`). Before, any job with an answer pending was let through, and the moved job could go back to
  the machine it left.
- **What is not moved.** A question of Claude's login screen (it starts with `NOT_SIGNED_IN` too) moves the same way: the
  machine reads signed out, and the screen ends with the pane. A pinned job, and a job whose machine reads signed in again
  before the pass (the sign-in answers its question instead).

### Warning before a tool's sign-in ends (part 2)

`claude auth status` gives no expiry ("Signed-out tools in Needs you"), so no Claude sign-in carries one. When a tool gives
one, its usage source sets `Account.expiresAt` (ISO); the tool accounts carry it on each signed-in machine
(`ToolAccountMachine.expiresAt`, `GET /api/tool-accounts`). Needs you's Accounts row then names a machine whose sign-in ends
within a day (`EXPIRY_WARNING_MS`), or has ended, with "sign it in again from Accounts" (`signedOutLines`,
`ui/src/model/tool-accounts.ts`, read against the server's minute).

Tests: `test/decider/signed-out.test.ts` (`signedOutMove`, `connectedOf`, a job resuming elsewhere kept off),
`test/integration/signed-out-move.test.ts` (a job held on a signed-out machine starts again on the signed-in one, its
question answered by the move; it stays with no machine signed in; it stays with a checkpoint that holds work and no session),
`test/herdr/startup-screens.test.ts` (the unsent text after the answer elsewhere), `test/http/tool-accounts.test.ts`,
`test/ui/accounts-view.test.ts`.

## A merged part moves its item on (issue #1231, 2026-10-15)

The problem: a job's part pull request (`Part of #N`) merged while the job still ran. The job's end was then judged
done, not partly done: a merged pull request that only refers to the issue counts as done ("Done is a pull request").
So the report put `hopper:pr-ready` on the issue and kept `follow: open` with no pull request named, as none open was
left. The follow looks only for an open pull request: it found none each sync and returned nothing. The work item stayed
in PR open ("waiting on its pull request: checks and the merge") with no job, and no next part ran. No view counted it.

- **The follow names the merged part** (`src/sources/github/follow.ts` `mergedPartOf`). A followed job with no pull
  request named, and none open, is given its own part merged since the job began: a pull request of its repository whose
  body says `Part of #N`, merged at or after the job's `createdAt`. Its merge is then followed as any part's:
  `job.pull_request_merged` with `part: true`, the item moves to partly done, `hopper:pr-ready` comes off, and the next
  sync offers the issue again, so a new job takes the next part. An item already stuck this way moves on the next follow
  round after the update: the follow is the reconcile pass, and nothing is migrated.
- **The next part reads the earlier part.** The done line says: a merged pull request with `Part of #N` is an earlier
  part; read its body first, and do the work it lists as left.
- **What the follow cannot move is stuck work.** An item in PR open for an hour that names no open pull request, or
  whose job follows none (`following`), is blocked by the item reconciler (issue #1891, "The item lifecycle"), and a
  blocked item is in Stuck work as `pr_open_stale`, by its job's id: "Items blocked with no pull request to wait on". It
  has no bulk action: a person looks at the issue, presses Run again when work is left, or closes the issue. The Failures
  view reads the ledger's blocked items for it (`viewOf`, `blockedStuck`).
- Not changed: the done check still counts a merged pull request that refers to the issue as done. A part whose job ends
  done is caught by the follow above, so the item never waits on nothing.

**Verification:** `test/sources/github-follow.test.ts` (a merged own part named and followed as a part; one merged before
the job began is not), `test/integration/pull-request-follow.test.ts` (the item leaves PR open for partly done, and the
next part is queued), `test/domain/work-items.test.ts` (`prOpenStuck`), `test/domain/stuck.test.ts` (the cause),
`test/sources/github-context.test.ts` (the done line).

## A job source not configured says so (issue #1243, 2026-10-15)

The problem: a `github-app` job source that was on with empty options (no `appId`, no `slug`, no private key) was paused
and silent. Each sync still ran a pass: it asked GitHub nothing and logged `REST 0, GraphQL 0`, which reads as a healthy
quiet source. The Sources view hid it ("an unset GitHub App is not shown", issue #254), so its intake was dead and nothing
said why.

- **A setup problem** (`JobSource.setupProblem`, `SetupProblem` in `src/domain/sources.ts`). The app source's names what of
  its identity is not set (`loadGitHubApp` now returns `missing`), or that the key is no key, and its help page
  (`github-app-setup`). It is read at each sync, as `paused` is.
- **No empty pass** (`src/sources/sync.ts`). While a source has a setup problem and no job of its own needs a check or a
  report, the sync loop runs no pass: no traffic line, no `lastOkAt`. Its status is `needs-setup` with `setupProblem`;
  `itemsSeen` 0, and the UI shows *not configured* in place of each count. With jobs of its own to report, the pass runs
  for them, as for a paused source, and the status stays `needs-setup` with the setup problem, never ok (issue #1351).
- **Said once.** The log says `hopper: source <name> not configured: <reason>` when the problem starts or changes, and
  `hopper: source <name> configured` once when it clears. No event: the status and Needs you carry it.
- **Asked for in place.** Sources shows the source as *needs setup*, with a setup card: what is missing, the steps (an
  app already installed, or `scripts/create-github-app.sh`; its id and slug in Plugins; its key in the runtime), and a
  link to the help page `help/github-app-setup.md`. Needs you has a **Setup** row (`#sources`), one line per source.
- **Clears by itself.** Config completed later (the key given to the runtime, the id and slug saved) clears it at the
  next sync, with no restart.
- Why not a failure-assessor **problem**: a problem groups failed jobs and holds new ones of its scope. A source with
  no config has no failed job, and must hold nothing else.
- Not done here (later parts of issue #1243): pick an app already installed from the list of apps the connected account
  can see, and keep the app's private key in the vault through a write-only field, not in the runtime.

**Verification:** `test/sources/sync-setup.test.ts` (no pass, `needs-setup`, said once; cleared at the next sync; a pass
still runs for its own jobs), `test/integration/github-app.test.ts` (an enabled app source with empty options, and with no
key; the key given clears it without a restart), `test/ui/sources.test.ts`, `test/ui/sources-view.test.ts` (the setup
card), `test/ui/needs-you.test.ts` (the Setup row), `test/sources/app-config.test.ts` (`missing`).

## What holds the event loop (issue #1154, 2026-10-15)

Seen on a hopper in a container on WSL with about six jobs at work: the event loop stalled again and again, at first up
to 80 s, after an update up to about 5 s. While it stalled, `/api/health` and `hopper update drift` did not answer, every
sandbox box's link ended, and their dial-ins were then refused as `stale`. The watchdog (issue #1002, "A box start holds
nothing else") said only which routes were in flight; most stalls had none, so it could not say what held the loop.

- **The watchdog names the store's part** (`src/store/slow-calls.ts`, `src/http/event-loop.ts`). Every store call blocks
  the event loop while it lasts ("Database": the Store port stays synchronous). Every call is totalled by its
  statement's verb and first table only (`statementOf`: `SELECT jobs`, `INSERT checkpoints`): never a literal, a
  parameter or a schema name. The watchdog reads the totals at each tick, and a stall's store calls are the difference
  at its end (issue #1383: before, only calls of 100 ms or more were kept, so many fast calls said nothing). A stall's
  log line adds the time the store held the loop in it and the three statements that held it longest — `…; store calls
  in it: 3.9 s (SELECT jobs 2.1 s ×3, INSERT checkpoints 1.8 s)` —, or `no store call in it`: then the hopper's own code
  held it. `/api/health`'s
  `eventLoopStall` carries the same as `store`, and the top bar's **stalled** badge says it.
- **A stall is raised, not only logged.** `hopper.event_loop_stalled` (`ms`, `during`, `store`, `skipped`), an instance
  event, in every user's log, so webhooks and notifiers take it. At most one a minute (`RAISE_EVERY_MS`); `skipped`
  counts the stalls logged since the last one raised. A stall is no **Problem**: it holds no job and has no cause to
  resolve.
- **A checkpoint is scrubbed off the event loop** (`src/engine/checkpoint-scrub.ts`). Each job at work is checkpointed
  every 10 minutes ("Checkpoints and resume elsewhere"); its agent session's log may be tens of MiB, unpacked, masked
  line by line (each a JSON parse and write) and packed again. That ran on the event loop, for each job, and is the one
