  (`run.jobId` is `schedule:<name>` in the sandbox runs ledger and the trace). The output is kept, at most 1 MiB, with
  the start, end, outcome (`succeeded`, `failed`, `interrupted`), exit code and problem; the newest 30 runs of each
  schedule are kept.
- **The schedule's vault grant** (`grant`, `hopper schedule grant`). A person's act, after Access as a job's vault grant
  (OpenFGA `vault_grant#can_grant`, the key `schedule:<name>`); a delegate approver is refused, since nothing waits.
  `revoke` takes it back. A save that changes the template, the repository, the folder or the script takes it back: a
  person grants what runs now. A time or a timeout keeps it.
- **A failed run.** A script that exits non-zero, a timeout, or a run the hopper could not start (exit 125 and the
  problem: the template not ready, no grant, the files not read, the schedule removed) is `step_schedule.run_failed`.
  The Grok Bot routine sends it as it sends `job.failed` (`error` the problem, or the exit code). Needs you's
  **Schedules** row lists each schedule whose newest run did not succeed, with why and `hopper schedule runs <name>`,
  until a run of it succeeds (`GET /api/step-schedules` `failed`).
- **Reads.** `GET /api/step-schedules` (each schedule, its next due time, its newest run), `GET /api/step-schedules/:name`
  (its runs with their output), `hopper schedule list` and `hopper schedule runs <name>`. `remove` (409 while a run has
  not ended) removes the schedule and its runs.

**Decisions:**
- **The grant is the schedule's, not a job's.** The vault's law gives only to a job a person granted it; a schedule has
  no job, so the person's grant is kept on the schedule, decided by Access as a job's is. It covers what the schedule
  runs: a save that changes that drops it.
- **A claim in the database, then a saga.** The two unique indexes make "once per due time" and "never two at once" the
  database's, across restarts and hosts; the saga gives the run's lease and the resume on another host, and the ledger
  check makes a resume never run the script twice.
- **No minted credential, and daily times only.** The backup needs vault secrets only. Minting for a run with no job is
  its own change to the vault's mint (which checks a job at work); a cron expression is not needed yet.
- **No page of its own.** The command line and the API are the acceptance; Needs you's row links to Vault.

**Residual risk, stated.** A run executes what the repository's default branch holds when it starts: whoever can push
there changes what runs with the schedule's vault secrets. The person who grants a schedule trusts that branch, as the
repository's own review guards it. The script holds the secret values in its box, and can send one to an egress host the
template names, as a box step can (issue #1875).

**Not built.** A minted credential for a scheduled run; a cron expression; a UI page for schedules; the scheduled
read-only infra check of issue #871 (it can use a schedule once a run can mint).

Tests: `test/domain/step-schedules.test.ts` (due times, a missed one once, what a save may hold, what changes what runs),
`test/step-schedules/service.test.ts` (the real database: claimed once however often a hopper looks, two hoppers claim
once, after a restart a due time that ran is not run again and a missed one runs once, a run whose box started is not
run again, never two at once, the folder at its paths, the secrets only after the grant and masked, failures, the grant
taken back), `test/integration/step-schedules.test.ts` (the real daemon, saga coordinator and CLI: save, list, grant, run
now, a run that cannot read its files fails and is listed for Needs you, revoke, remove), `test/vault/step-delivery-schedule.test.ts`,
`test/sandbox/files-tar-prefix.test.ts`, `test/cli-operator-schedule.test.ts`, `test/plugins/grokbot-step-schedules.test.ts`,
`test/ui/step-schedules-needs-you.test.ts`.

## Kept delivery tracks and deployment records (issue #2775, part 1, 2026-10-25)

Owner requirement: every job says where its work is and where it ended up. A finished fix must never sit unshipped with
nobody able to see it: #2766 merged to `main`, and was not on `dev` or running anywhere. The issue names a "saga object"
per job and a "deployment object". "Saga" is the coordinator's word ("Sagas: work that survives a stop"), and the issue's
saga is one job's way through the **delivery steps**, which the glossary calls its **delivery track**. So the object is
the **kept delivery track**: the delivery track ("Delivery forecasts"), kept in the database, with its end.

- **The kept delivery track** (`KeptTrack`, `src/domain/kept-tracks.ts`, table `delivery_tracks`, tenant migration 101).
  Born at the job's `job.queued`. It keeps the marks its events gave (each the first one: queued, started, finished, its
  pull request, merged, the batch runs that carried it, landed, its pull request closed), every delivery step it started
  and ended (the transitions), the step it is in, since when, its **blocker** and what it waits on in plain words. A change
  merged on the landing branch but not promoted is open in `landing_checks`, "a green run of the checks on the landing
  branch", never done. Past its landing checks, the scheduled steps come from its repository's promotion set schedule and
  gate clearances, as the forecast's do; a repository with no schedule holds it in `promotion_set`, and it says it waits
  on one.
- **It closes only with its deployment record** (`DeploymentRecord`, table `deployment_records`): `deploy` once its
  production step ended — the artifact (its pull request), the target (`production`), the expected state (`delivered`), the
  observed state at each hop (each step) —; `none` once its job ended with no change to deliver — failed, cancelled or
  rejected before a merge, finished with no pull request (a research or a proposal job: `report`), or its pull request
  closed with no merge — with its source and its outcome; or a person's **no-deploy mark**. Every job gets exactly one
  record row (part 2: a flip writes over a `none` row; a `deploy` row is never written over).
- **The kept-track pass** (`src/engine/kept-tracks.ts`): every minute, under its lease `kept-tracks` ("Several hoppers on
  one database"), the events after its cursor are folded into the open tracks' marks, and every open track is judged
  again: its job's status and the scheduled steps move with no event. The tracks it changed, their records and the new
  cursor are one transaction, so a pass a stop cut short is done again from the same cursor, on any host. The fold is
  idempotent: each mark is the first one, so an event folded twice changes nothing. The first pass of a hopper keeps the
  tracks of the last 30 days, not the whole log. A job the store no longer holds closes by its events.
- **Read on its own.** `GET /api/delivery-tracks` (by job, repository, state) and `GET /api/deployments` (by job,
  repository, target, kind). `POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/no-deploy` (operator) is the no-deploy mark,
  `delivery_track.no_deploy_marked`; it changes no job, pull request or promotion.
- **The job page** shows its Delivery panel (`ui/src/views/job-delivery.tsx`): in progress, the step, since when and what
  it waits on; completed, its deployment record; then each step.

**Decisions:**
- **Not a coordinator saga.** A saga's steps are acts the hopper does, tried five times and then compensated. A track's
  steps are things that happen elsewhere — a merge, a batch run, a cutoff, a person's gate clearance — over days. A pass
  that folds events from a cursor gives the same durability (state in the database, idempotent folds, any host under a
  lease) with nothing to retry.
- **The delivery steps, not new stages.** The issue's "built, promoted, image ready, running, deployed" are the delivery
  steps the forecast already measures and the glossary already names; a second set of names for the same way would be a
  synonym.
- **A pass, not a hook at each job start.** A job is made on many paths; the pass reads the one log they all write. The
  record is at most a minute late; its times are the events', not the pass's.

**What is left** (later parts): the hopper's own stages past `dev` — `beta`, `canary` and `stable`, the image built for
each, and which instance runs it — as observed hops of a `deploy` record; the commit of the merge in the artifact; a
no-deploy button on the job page and in the operator CLI; the in-progress position on the Jobs list.

**Verification:** `test/domain/kept-tracks.test.ts` (the fold, the step and what it waits on, each kind of close, a fold
twice), `test/engine/kept-tracks.test.ts` (the real database: a track from the start, a merged fix open in
`landing_checks`, a restart that goes on from the cursor, a deploy record and two `none` records, the records queried on
their own, a closed track final, the first pass's window), `test/integration/delivery-tracks.test.ts` (the HTTP routes,
the no-deploy mark, 404 and 409), `test/ui/job-delivery-view.test.ts`.

### Part 2: the deployment expectation (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

Owner requirement: until a deployment has fully completed, what a job is expected to deploy can change — deploy midway,
then don't — and the object keeps each flip and shows the latest. The moment the deployment completes, the object is
final, even while the job runs other stages. A no-deploy record is never final: the code is latent and can be deployed
later, even years later.

- **A deployment expectation** (`DeploymentExpectation`, `src/domain/kept-tracks.ts`): a person's flip, `deploy` or
  `none`, with who, when and their note. Every flip is kept, in order, on the track (`expectations`) and on its record;
  the last one holds. With no flip the hopper judges, as in part 1.
- **`none`** (`POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/no-deploy`, `delivery_track.no_deploy_marked`): the no-deploy mark. It closes
  the track with a `none` record, outcome `marked`. 409 when the track is closed already.
- **`deploy`** (`POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/deploy`, `delivery_track.deploy_expected`): on an open track it records the
  flip; on a closed `none` track it opens the track again, its `none` record kept with the flip, its marks folded again
  from its job's events (the pass folds the events of open tracks only). While a person's last flip is `deploy`, the pass
  does not close the track as `none` when its job ends with no change: it stays open and says what it waits on. 409 when
  the last flip is `deploy` already.
- **Locked: a `deploy` record** (`lockedOf`). The pass makes it once the production step ended, whatever a person said
  before: if it deployed, it deployed. Both routes answer 409 on it and change nothing, and the store writes over neither
  its track nor its record (`WHERE … kind <> 'deploy'`). A change after that goes to a new job. A `none` record is never
  locked: the store writes over it as a person flips it.
- **No migration.** The lock is the record's kind (`deploy`), so the rows of part 1 read the same; `expectations` is a new
  optional field in the JSON bodies, absent on the old rows (no flip).
- **The job page** (`ui/src/views/job-delivery.tsx`): "Mark no-deploy" while the track is open, "Expect a deployment"
  unless the last flip is `deploy`, neither on a delivered record, which says it is final; then each flip.
- **The operator CLI** (`src/cli-operator-deployment.ts`): `hopper deployment --job <id> [--expect deploy|none [--note
  <text>]]` reads the track or flips it; `hopper deployment --list [--repo] [--target] [--kind]` reads the records.

**Decisions:**
- **Two flips, not three.** The issue names "deploy, don't deploy, cancel". A cancel of an expected deployment is a flip
  to `none`, and a cancel of a no-deploy mark is a flip to `deploy`; a third word for one of the two would be a synonym.
- **Two routes, one per flip**, each with its own event: the no-deploy route and its event stay as part 1 made them.
- **A flip to `deploy` keeps the `none` record**, so the job's deployment section never empties once it has a record.

**What is left** (later parts): the hopper's own stages past `dev` (`beta`, `canary`, `stable`, the image and the
instance that runs it) as observed hops; the merge commit in the artifact; the in-progress position on the Jobs list;
spec-change events on the track; the intercession design (pause, reroute, take ownership — who, which actions at which
step, how it meets the stage-ownership hand-off), written down and agreed before it is built.

**Verification:** `test/domain/kept-tracks.test.ts` (the flips, the reopen and its lock, the lock whatever was said),
`test/integration/delivery-tracks.test.ts` (both routes, 409 on a locked record, the store's guard),
`test/ui/job-delivery-view.test.ts` (the buttons, the final record, the flips listed), `test/cli/deployment.test.ts`.

### Part 3: text edits on the track (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

The issue asks the track to record a change of the job's spec while it runs: when, at which step, and a reference to
the change. It asks the track to record it only: telling the running agent is the agent-execution layer's concern.

- **What a spec change is here: an edit of the job's item text** (its title or body; the **item snapshot**'s text,
  issue #662). A sync already sees it: for a job that waits, `item.changed_since_snapshot` holds it; for a started job,
  `refreshEdit` (`src/engine/item-snapshots.ts`) lowers its trust (issue #655 part 7) and keeps the text it saw
  (`editSeen`). That second case now also appends **`item.edit_seen`**: the item's key, the SHA-256 of the text the job
  last saw (`fromHash`) and of the live text (`toHash`), and who edited it. Once per new text, as `editSeen` already
  ensures. Never the text. New comments are no edit (issue #747).
- **The track folds both events** into `textEdits` (`TextEdit`, `src/domain/kept-tracks.ts`): the event's seq, when, the
  delivery step the track was in at that event, which event, the key, the two hashes and the editors. The same event
  folded twice is kept once (by its seq). A text edit changes no step and closes nothing. The hashes are the reference:
  the item snapshot and the job's `editSeen` hold the texts.
- **The job page** lists each text edit: when, at which step, and by whom.
- **No migration**: `textEdits` is a new optional field in the track's JSON body and its marks.

**Decisions:**
- **No word "spec change".** The job's `spec` is its executor, model and work tree (`job.respecified`), not its
  text. The issue's "spec change" is an edit of the item text, so the track calls it a **text edit**.
- **A new event for a started job, not `job.trust_lowered`.** That one is written only when the stamp drops, so a second
  edit of a job already `untrusted` would be lost.

**What is left** (later parts): the hopper's own stages past `dev` as observed hops; the merge commit in the artifact;
the in-progress position on the Jobs list; the intercession design, written down and agreed before it is built.

**Verification:** `test/domain/kept-tracks.test.ts` (both events folded, each at its step, kept once),
`test/integration/trust-edit.test.ts` (one `item.edit_seen` per new text, with its hashes and editor),
`test/ui/job-delivery-view.test.ts` (the text edits listed).

### Part 4: the hopper's own channels as observed hops (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

The issue's example is a fix merged to `main` that was not on `dev` or anywhere it runs. Parts 1 to 3 follow a change to
`dev` (the batch run's promotion). After that, a repository with a **promotion set schedule** has scheduled steps; the
hopper's own repository moves `dev` → `beta` → `canary` → `stable` instead (issue #1073), with no schedule. This part reads
those moves as observed hops.

- **The merge commit.** `landing_batch.promoted` has `merge`: the batch run's merge commit on the tested branch. The fold
  keeps it on the track's marks (`commit`), and a `deploy` record's artifact names it (`artifact.commit`) beside its pull
  request.
- **On canary.** `landing_batch.canary_started` now has `mergeCommits`: the merge commits (two parents or more) of the
  compare of `stable` with `canary` that started the candidate. A track whose `commit` is one of them is on that candidate:
  the first such event ends its **promotion set** step and starts its **test gate** (the canary window). Each such
  candidate's tip is kept (`canaryTips`), because a held candidate can be followed by a later one that carries it too.
- **On stable.** `landing_batch.canary_promoted` of one of those tips is the move of `stable` to it: the **production**
  step starts and ends then, and the track closes with its `deploy` record, locked. Observed hops win over a schedule.
- **Not observed yet.** `beta` (moved by `scripts/promote.sh`, with no event), and the install that runs it: an
  update's `update.applied` is written to the instance's events, not to a user's, so the kept-track pass does not read it.
  A track in the promotion set with no canary hop still says what the schedule says.
- **No migration**: the new marks and `artifact.commit` are optional fields of the JSON bodies; `mergeCommits` is an
  optional field of the event, so an older event moves no track.

**Decisions:**
- **A merge commit, not every commit, of the candidate.** The batch run's merge is a merge commit, and the compare answers
  at most 250 commits: the merge commits keep the event small.
- **Delivered at stable.** `stable` is the channel every install that is not in the canary subset follows. The
  install that runs it is not seen from a user's events, so the record says what the hopper observed.

**What is left** (later parts): the in-progress position on the Jobs list; the intercession design, written down and
agreed before it is built.

**Verification:** `test/domain/kept-tracks.test.ts` (on canary in the test gate, on stable delivered with its commit; a
held candidate, then a later one), `test/landing-batches/canary.test.ts` (`mergeCommits` on the start),
`test/ui/job-delivery-view.test.ts` (the commit on the record).

### Part 5: the delivery step on the Jobs list (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

The issue asks that a job in progress shows its position. The job page does since part 1. The Jobs list did not: a
finished job whose fix merged but was not promoted read `done` there, which is the issue's example.

- **A Delivery column** on the Jobs view's list (`ui/src/views/job-row.tsx`): for a job whose kept delivery track is open,
  its delivery step; the cell's title says since when and what it waits on. Empty for a job with no open track. Only a wide
  screen shows it, as the last event.
- **Read with the graph** (`ui/src/views/jobs.tsx`): `GET /api/delivery-tracks?state=open`, again each time the view reads
  the job graph. No new route, no new event and no migration.

**Decisions:**
- **Open tracks only.** A closed track's record is on the job page; the list's question is "what is still on its way".
  It also keeps the read small: a closed track is final, and they grow without end.
- **A column, not the stage badge.** The job stage is the job's own life; the delivery step is its change's. Two
  meanings in one badge would be a synonym.

**What is left** (later parts): the intercession design (pause, reroute, take ownership: who, which actions at which
step, how it meets the stage-ownership hand-off), written down and agreed with a person before it is built; `beta` and
the install that runs a change, as observed hops.

**Verification:** `test/ui/jobs-table.test.ts` (an open track's step and its title on the row, none without one).

### Part 6: interventions and the delivery hold (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

The issue asks that a person can step into a job's change from the step it is in: pause it and resume it, reroute it,
and take ownership of it and hand it back. It asks that the design is written down and agreed before it is built. A
person accepted this design (Path 1 of the proposal of part 6): map each act onto an act the hopper has, and add one
new act, the **delivery hold**.

**The design** (agreed):

| Act | At `queued`, `coding` | At `pr_checks` | From `landing` on | At `test_gate`, `production` |
|-----|------|------|------|------|
| Pause | Park (the job at work) | Park (the job at work), else a hold | a hold | a hold: the gate holds the change already, so it records that a person owns it |
| Resume | Pick up | Pick up, or release | release | release |
| Reroute back | — | Run again (the job ended) | Run again, before `production` | — at `production` |
| Skip ahead | expedite, as the promotion set schedule allows | the same | the same, up to the cutoff of its set | — |
| A different target | refused (409): `production` is the only target; a second target earns this act | | | |
| Take ownership | — | a hold, `owner` `person` | the same | the same |
| Hand back | — | release | release | release |

- **The delivery hold** (`delivery_track.held`, `delivery_track.released`): who, the step, the reason and the owner.
  `owner` `hopper`: a pause; the step's own owner (yolo mode, the batch runner, the schedule) keeps the change but does
  not act on it while it is held. `owner` `person`: the person owns it; the step's owner does not act on it until they
  hand it back. The release is the resume and the hand back: the step's owner acts again at its next pass.
- **Where the work in progress stops.** Park ends the pane and keeps the work tree and the agent session, as now. A hold
  while a batch run carries the change does not stop that run: the change leaves at the next run, and a run that carries
  it already finishes as it is (a bisect cannot take a change out partway). A hold at a gate stops nothing.
- **Who.** Least role `operator` for a hold, Park and Pick up, as for the other job acts. A release that lets a merge or a
  promotion go on is a **box action**, as a merge is. Reroute is `operator` and a box action: Run again starts a job. A job
  never steers its own track, and no `/job/*` route is added. An API token needs the new scope `delivery_tracks:steer`;
  the delegate approver's preset does not get it.
- **A refused act appends no event**, so the track stays as it was.

**This part** builds the record and the rule of which act a step allows:

- **Interventions** (`Intervention`, `src/domain/track-interventions.ts`): the fold keeps each person's act on the job's
  change on its track, `interventions`, with who, the act, the step the track was in before it, and when: Park and Pick up
  (`job.parked`, `job.unparked` with a person, not an auto-park, a move or a job's own park), Run again (`job.rerun` `by`
  `user`), Merge now (`job.pull_request_merged` with a person), the expedite flag (`delivery_expedite.changed` that names
  the job, its issue or its pull request), and a hold and its release. Each is kept once (by its seq).
- **The hold** (`hold`, `holdOf`): the last hold, if no release came after it.
- **`allowedActs(track, job, delivery)`**: the acts the step allows, from the table: none on a closed track; only release
  on a held change; only Pick up on a parked job; Park for a job at work; else, from `pr_checks` on, hold and take
  ownership; Run again once the job ended, before `production`; expedite while the flag can change its promotion set,
  when the schedule allows it (`out_of_cadence`) and the flag is not on already.
- **No migration**: `interventions` and `hold` are new optional fields of the track's JSON body and its marks.

**Decisions:**
- **"Intervention", not "intercession".** One word for a person's act on a change, in code and UI.
- **The acts that exist, not new ones**, but for the hold: people know them, and each already has its permission, its
  event and its tests.
- **The hold is a track's, not a job's.** A **hold** is a Decision's, on a waiting job; a delivery hold holds a change
  past its job's end, so it is a new word.

**What is left** (later parts): the routes `POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/hold|release`, the scope `delivery_tracks:steer`, the CLI
`hopper deployment hold|release` and the Delivery panel's acts from `allowedActs`, and a held mark on the Jobs list;
Run again from `landing_checks` on closes the track `none`, outcome `rerouted`, with a link to the new job's track;
`beta` and the install that runs a change, as observed hops.

**Verification:** `test/domain/track-interventions.test.ts` (each act kept at its step, the hopper's and a job's own acts
not, the hold until its release, an expedite flag on the issue or the pull request, a fold twice, the acts each step
allows).

### Part 7: the delivery hold's effect (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

The step's owner does not act on a held change. Each owner reads the holds from the hold and release events at each ask
(`heldJobs`, `src/domain/track-interventions.ts`; the store reads in `src/users/delivery-holds.ts`), not from the kept
track, so a hold counts from its event on and not from the next pass of the tracks.

- **Yolo mode** (GitHub and GitLab): a held job's ready pull request or merge request is not merged. The wait says why on
  what the follow saw (`mergeError`, `holdWhy`: who owns it, the step, since when and the reason, never the person). The
  release lets the next sync merge it. A person's Merge now is a person's act and still merges.
- **The batch runner**: the landing branch is one line, so a batch run cannot leave out one change in the middle. It takes
  the landing branch up to the first held merge, the first parent of that merge (`heldCut`), and the changes after it wait
  with it. With the first merge held, no batch run starts. The pass says which pull request is held. The pending merges
  for the work-item ledger stay the whole landing branch's. A batch run that carries the change already finishes as it is.
- **The stable move**: when the canary window passed, `stable` does not move to a candidate that carries a held change.
  The canary says which pull requests are held, and the next pass after the release moves it.
- The held pull requests of a repository are each held job's pull request, as the job names it, else as its track does.
- The connected account's GitHub source now passes the done criteria of a job's conditional skills (issue #1924) and the
  deletes its issue allows to its GitHub source, with the delivery hold. Before, it did not pass them, so yolo mode merged
  with no done criteria checked.

**Decisions:**
- **A cut, not a revert.** To leave a held change out of the batch from the middle, the hopper would have to revert it on
  the landing branch. The cut changes nothing on GitHub, and the release lets everything go on.
- **Events, not tracks.** The kept-track pass runs every 60 seconds; a merge in that time would not see a new hold.

**What is left** (later parts): the routes `POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/hold|release`, the scope
`delivery_tracks:steer`, the CLI `hopper deployment hold|release`, the Delivery panel's acts from `allowedActs` and a held
mark on the Jobs list; Run again from `landing_checks` on closes the track `none`, outcome `rerouted`; `beta` and the
install that runs a change, as observed hops.

**Verification:** `test/domain/delivery-holds.test.ts`, `test/users/delivery-holds.test.ts`,
`test/landing-batches/held.test.ts`, `test/sources/github-yolo-delivery-hold.test.ts`,
`test/sources/account-merge-holds.test.ts`.

### Part 8: the hold and release routes (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

A person puts a delivery hold on a job's change, and releases it, from the API, the CLI and the job page.

- **The routes** (`src/http/ui/delivery-hold.ts`): `POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/hold` with `job`, `owner` (`hopper`, the
  default: a hold; `person`: take ownership) and an optional `reason` appends `delivery_track.held` at the step the track is
  in; `POST /ui/api/delivery-tracks/release` with `job` and an optional `reason` appends `delivery_track.released`. Least
  role `operator`. Each takes only an act `allowedActs` allows for the track's step, with the hold as its events say now
  (`jobHold`), not as the pass kept it: 404 for a job with no kept track, 409 for an act the step does not allow, with the
  reason. A refused act appends no event. The route keeps the act on the kept track too (`withIntervention`), so its answer
  shows it at once; the pass folds the same event again and keeps it once (by its seq).
- **A release is a box action** (`BOX_ACTIONS`, kind `approve or merge work`): it lets a merge or a promotion go on. A hold
  is none, as a cancel is none.
- **The scopes** come from the routes, as every route's does: `delivery-tracks:hold` and `delivery-tracks:release`, in the
  Jobs section. The delegate approver's preset does not get them.
- **The acts on the answer**: `GET /api/delivery-tracks`, and the answer of each route that changes a track, carry `acts`,
  the acts each track's step allows now (`withActs`, from its job and its repository's delivery settings). They are never
  kept.
- **The CLI**: `hopper deployment --job <id> --hold [--owner hopper|person] [--reason <text>]` and `hopper deployment --job
  <id> --release [--reason <text>]`.
- **The Delivery panel** (`ui/src/views/job-delivery.tsx`): Hold, Take ownership and Release (Hand back, for a change a
  person owns) from `acts`; the hold, with who, the step, since when and the reason; each intervention, with the act, who,
  when and the step. Park, Pick up, Run again and expedite stay the job page's own buttons.
- **The Jobs list**: the Delivery cell says `held` while a delivery hold holds the change, and its title says who owns it.

**Decisions:**
- **Two routes, two scopes, not one `delivery_tracks:steer`.** A scope is the route's area and its last path part, and
  a box action is a whole route. A release is a box action and a hold is not, so they are two routes. "Steer" is a research
  report's word in the glossary.
- **The hold from its events.** The pass keeps the hold on the track only at its next run; the route reads the hold and
  release events, as the step's owner does (part 7).

**What is left** (later parts): Run again from `landing_checks` on closes the track `none`, outcome `rerouted`, with a link
to the new job's track; `beta` and the install that runs a change, as observed hops.

**Verification:** `test/integration/delivery-hold-acts.test.ts` (a hold and a release, each kept once; taking ownership and
handing it back; each refused act changes nothing), `test/integration/delivery-tracks.test.ts`, `test/cli/deployment.test.ts`,
`test/ui/job-delivery-view.test.ts`, `test/ui/jobs-table.test.ts`.


### Part 9: Run again reroutes a change (issue #2775, 2026-10-25)

Run again is the reroute back of the design of part 6. The new job carries the work on, so the ended job's change is no
longer on its way. Before this part the ended job's track stayed open, at `pr_checks` or later, and waited on a merge or a
promotion that its new job did instead.

- **`job.rerun` names the new job**: `nextJobId`. An older event names none.
- **The fold** keeps the first run again on the track's marks (`rerouted`): when, the new job, and the person who asked,
  if a person did.
- **The close.** A track whose job ran again closes `none`, outcome `rerouted`, at the time of the run again, with
  `nextJob`, the new job, and `by`, the person. A change delivered before it stays delivered: its `deploy` record is
  locked. A person's flip to deploy after the run again opens the track again, as for any `none` record.
- **The job page** says the item ran again in a new job, and links the new job, whose own track carries the work on.
- **No migration**: `rerouted` and `nextJob` are optional fields of the JSON bodies; `nextJobId` is an optional field of
  the event.

**Decisions:**
- **Every run again, not only a person's.** Tending, the failure assessor and the item reconciler also start a new job of
  the item, and the old track would wait on that job's change all the same. Only a person's run again is an
  intervention (part 6).
- **At any step before delivery, not only from `landing_checks` on.** A finished job whose pull request is open, run
  again, also hands its change to the new job.

**What is left** (later parts): `beta` and the install that runs a change, as observed hops.

**Verification:** `test/domain/kept-tracks.test.ts` (run again closes the track `rerouted`, with the new job; a delivered
change stays delivered; a flip to deploy after it), `test/ui/job-delivery-view.test.ts` (the link to the new job),
`test/integration/jobs.test.ts`, `test/integration/failures.test.ts`, `test/integration/operator-cli-failures.test.ts`
(`nextJobId` on `job.rerun`).

## New repositories (issue #2795, part 1, 2026-10-25)

Owner request: everything in the hopper is a setting with a sensible default, and an escalation to a person by default is
the default value of a setting, never a behaviour with no setting. The issue names several such flows (intake, a question
that goes to a person and back into the job, a default setup that wires them all). This part does one of them: the hopper
sees a repository it did not reach before, and the person chooses whether it is added to the job repositories at once or
the person is asked.

**As built:**
- **A new repository** is one that a connected account reaches now (where the hopper's app is installed, or what a
  personal access token reaches) and that no read before saw. It is never one of the account's job repositories, and never
  one that another account has for its jobs (issue #1448). The first read of an account only learns what it reaches:
  nothing it reached then is new, so connecting an account never adds every repository (issue #321's rule stays).
- **The new-repository policy** is the user's setting per connected account (`newRepositories:<account key>` in the user
  schema's `settings`, `src/store/new-repository-settings.ts`): `mode` for every owner and `owners`, an owner's own mode,
  which wins, matched in any case. Each mode is `ask` or `accept`. The default is `{ mode: 'ask', owners: {} }`: a value
  of the setting, which the person can change.
- **After each read that worked** (`installations.ts` `found`, on Refresh, on the schedule and on connect), the policy
  runs on what the read saw (`findNewRepositories`, `src/domain/new-repositories.ts`, pure): `accept` adds the repository
  to the job repositories and the source syncs at once (`onChange`); `ask` keeps a **new-repository ask** with when the
  hopper first saw it. An ask is dropped once its repository is chosen, no longer reached, or taken by another account. A
  dismissed repository stays seen, so it is not asked about again. Each outcome is logged with the repositories.
- **A change of the policy** applies at once to what the last read saw: an owner switched to `accept` adds its waiting
  asks to the job repositories without a new read.
- **The route.** `POST /ui/api/connected-accounts` `{ action: 'new-repositories', provider, key?, policy?, dismiss? }`
  (admin): `policy` is the whole policy; `dismiss` drops asks. An owner with a `/` is refused (400). Adding an ask to the
  job repositories is the existing `choose`. The connected account's status carries `newRepositories: { policy, asks }`.
- **Sources** (`ui/src/views/new-repositories.tsx`), under the repositories: *A new repository the app reaches:* with
  **ask me** or **add to job repositories**; when the account reaches more than one owner, a choice per owner (**as
  above**, ask me, add to job repositories); and each ask with **Add to job repositories** and **Dismiss**.

**Decisions:**
- **Per connected account, not per user.** A repository is a job repository of one account only, and each account reaches
  its own owners. The record is keyed as the job repositories are (`keyed.ts`).
- **The first read is a baseline.** Without it, a hopper that updates to this build would ask about every repository it
  already reaches.
- **No event yet.** The connected accounts' `choose` records no event either; the log line says what the policy did. An
  event (so a notifier can tell the person of an ask) is a later part.

**What is left** (later parts of #2795): a catalog of the settings that make up the flows, with their scope (instance,
user, owner, repository); a "create your default assistant" step that sets up the expected connections and webhooks and
the default values in one go; one general model for the circular flows (intake → job → question → person → back into the
job), so that each new flow is an instance of it; the voice agent stage, which the hopper does not have yet; an event and
a notification for a new-repository ask.

**Verification:** `test/domain/new-repositories.test.ts`, `test/integration/new-repositories.test.ts` (asked by default,
dismissed and not asked again; an owner's `accept` adds the repository and its issue becomes a job; a bad owner is 400),
`test/ui/new-repositories-view.test.ts`.
